modules.title: The Galilean group
modules.doc:
This file defines Galilean transformations in `d` spatial dimensions, together with their group
law and their action on `Time × Space d`.

An element consists of a spatial orthogonal transformation `R`, a boost velocity `v`, a spatial
translation `a`, and a time translation `b`. We use the active convention
`(t, x) ↦ (t + b, R x + v t + a)`.

sections.text: ## A. Basic support lemmas
## B. Group operations
## C. Action on time and space
## D. Subgroup inclusions

declarations.name: GalileanGroup
declarations.doc:
A Galilean transformation in `d` spatial dimensions. The fields are, in order, the spatial
orthogonal part, boost velocity, spatial translation, and time translation.
declarations.statement:
structure GalileanGroup (d : ℕ := 3) where
  /-- The spatial orthogonal part. -/
  rotation : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin d) ℝ
  /-- The boost velocity. -/
  velocity : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)
  /-- The spatial translation. -/
  spaceTranslation : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)
  /-- The time translation. -/
  timeTranslation : Time

declarations.name: GalileanGroup.orthogonal_smul_smul
declarations.statement:
lemma orthogonal_smul_smul (R : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin d) ℝ) (c : ℝ)
    (v : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) :
    R • (c • v) = c • (R • v)

declarations.doc: The identity Galilean transformation.
declarations.statement: instance : One (GalileanGroup d)

declarations.name: GalileanGroup.one_rotation
declarations.statement: lemma one_rotation : (1 : GalileanGroup d).rotation = 1

declarations.name: GalileanGroup.one_velocity
declarations.statement: lemma one_velocity : (1 : GalileanGroup d).velocity = 0

declarations.name: GalileanGroup.one_spaceTranslation
declarations.statement: lemma one_spaceTranslation : (1 : GalileanGroup d).spaceTranslation = 0

declarations.name: GalileanGroup.one_timeTranslation
declarations.statement: lemma one_timeTranslation : (1 : GalileanGroup d).timeTranslation = 0

declarations.doc: The product whose action is composition: `(g * h) • tx = g • h • tx`.
declarations.statement: instance : Mul (GalileanGroup d)

declarations.name: GalileanGroup.mul_rotation
declarations.statement:
lemma mul_rotation (g h : GalileanGroup d) :
    (g * h).rotation = g.rotation * h.rotation

declarations.name: GalileanGroup.mul_velocity
declarations.statement:
lemma mul_velocity (g h : GalileanGroup d) :
    (g * h).velocity = g.rotation • h.velocity + g.velocity

declarations.name: GalileanGroup.mul_spaceTranslation
declarations.statement:
lemma mul_spaceTranslation (g h : GalileanGroup d) :
    (g * h).spaceTranslation =
      g.spaceTranslation + g.rotation • h.spaceTranslation + h.timeTranslation.val • g.velocity

declarations.name: GalileanGroup.mul_timeTranslation
declarations.statement:
lemma mul_timeTranslation (g h : GalileanGroup d) :
    (g * h).timeTranslation = g.timeTranslation + h.timeTranslation

declarations.doc: The inverse Galilean transformation.
declarations.statement: instance : Inv (GalileanGroup d)

declarations.name: GalileanGroup.inv_rotation
declarations.statement:
lemma inv_rotation (g : GalileanGroup d) :
    g⁻¹.rotation = g.rotation⁻¹

declarations.name: GalileanGroup.inv_velocity
declarations.doc: The inverse boost velocity formula.
declarations.statement:
lemma inv_velocity (g : GalileanGroup d) :
    g⁻¹.velocity = -(g.rotation⁻¹ • g.velocity)

declarations.name: GalileanGroup.inv_spaceTranslation
declarations.statement:
lemma inv_spaceTranslation (g : GalileanGroup d) :
    g⁻¹.spaceTranslation =
      -(g.rotation⁻¹ • g.spaceTranslation) +
        g.timeTranslation.val • (g.rotation⁻¹ • g.velocity)

declarations.name: GalileanGroup.inv_timeTranslation
declarations.statement:
lemma inv_timeTranslation (g : GalileanGroup d) :
    g⁻¹.timeTranslation = -g.timeTranslation

declarations.doc: The Galilean transformations form a group under composition.
declarations.statement: instance : Group (GalileanGroup d)
instance : Inhabited (GalileanGroup d)

declarations.name: GalileanGroup.actSpace
declarations.doc: The Galilean action on space at the time `t`, `x ↦ R x + v t + a`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def actSpace (g : GalileanGroup d) (t : Time) (x : Space d) : Space d

declarations.name: GalileanGroup.act
declarations.doc: The Galilean action on `Time × Space d`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def act (g : GalileanGroup d) (tx : Time × Space d) : Time × Space d
noncomputable instance : MulAction (GalileanGroup d) (Time × Space d)

declarations.name: GalileanGroup.smul_fst
declarations.statement:
lemma smul_fst (g : GalileanGroup d) (tx : Time × Space d) :
    (g • tx).1 = tx.1 + g.timeTranslation

declarations.name: GalileanGroup.smul_snd
declarations.statement:
lemma smul_snd (g : GalileanGroup d) (tx : Time × Space d) :
    (g • tx).2 = g.actSpace tx.1 tx.2

declarations.name: GalileanGroup.smul_mk
declarations.statement:
lemma smul_mk (g : GalileanGroup d) (t : Time) (x : Space d) :
    g • ((t, x) : Time × Space d) = (t + g.timeTranslation, g.actSpace t x)

declarations.name: GalileanGroup.actSpace_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma actSpace_apply (g : GalileanGroup d) (t : Time) (x : Space d) (i : Fin d) :
    g.actSpace t x i =
      (g.rotation • (x -ᵥ (0 : Space d))) i + t.val * g.velocity i + g.spaceTranslation i

declarations.name: GalileanGroup.ofEuclidean
declarations.doc:
A Euclidean spatial transformation as a Galilean transformation with zero boost and no time
translation.
declarations.statement: def ofEuclidean (g : EuclideanGroup d) : GalileanGroup d

declarations.name: GalileanGroup.ofEuclidean_rotation
declarations.statement:
lemma ofEuclidean_rotation (g : EuclideanGroup d) :
    (ofEuclidean g).rotation = g.linear

declarations.name: GalileanGroup.ofEuclidean_velocity
declarations.statement:
lemma ofEuclidean_velocity (g : EuclideanGroup d) :
    (ofEuclidean g).velocity = 0

declarations.name: GalileanGroup.ofEuclidean_spaceTranslation
declarations.statement:
lemma ofEuclidean_spaceTranslation (g : EuclideanGroup d) :
    (ofEuclidean g).spaceTranslation = g.translation

declarations.name: GalileanGroup.ofEuclidean_timeTranslation
declarations.statement:
lemma ofEuclidean_timeTranslation (g : EuclideanGroup d) :
    (ofEuclidean g).timeTranslation = 0

declarations.name: GalileanGroup.euclidean.incl
declarations.doc: Inclusion of the Euclidean group into the Galilean group.
declarations.statement: def euclidean.incl : EuclideanGroup d →* GalileanGroup d

declarations.name: GalileanGroup.ofOrthogonal
declarations.doc: A pure orthogonal spatial transformation as a Galilean transformation.
declarations.statement: def ofOrthogonal (R : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin d) ℝ) : GalileanGroup d

declarations.name: GalileanGroup.ofOrthogonal_rotation
declarations.statement:
lemma ofOrthogonal_rotation (R : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin d) ℝ) :
    (ofOrthogonal R).rotation = R

declarations.name: GalileanGroup.ofOrthogonal_velocity
declarations.statement:
lemma ofOrthogonal_velocity (R : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin d) ℝ) :
    (ofOrthogonal R).velocity = 0

declarations.name: GalileanGroup.ofOrthogonal_spaceTranslation
declarations.statement:
lemma ofOrthogonal_spaceTranslation (R : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin d) ℝ) :
    (ofOrthogonal R).spaceTranslation = 0

declarations.name: GalileanGroup.ofOrthogonal_timeTranslation
declarations.statement:
lemma ofOrthogonal_timeTranslation (R : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin d) ℝ) :
    (ofOrthogonal R).timeTranslation = 0

declarations.name: GalileanGroup.orthogonal.incl
declarations.doc: Inclusion of the orthogonal group into the Galilean group.
declarations.statement: def orthogonal.incl : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin d) ℝ →* GalileanGroup d

declarations.name: GalileanGroup.rotation.incl
declarations.doc: Inclusion of the existing spatial rotation subgroup into the Galilean group.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def rotation.incl : EuclideanGroup.RotationGroup d →* GalileanGroup d

declarations.name: GalileanGroup.ofSpaceTranslation
declarations.doc: A pure spatial translation as a Galilean transformation.
declarations.statement: def ofSpaceTranslation (a : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) : GalileanGroup d

declarations.name: GalileanGroup.ofSpaceTranslation_rotation
declarations.statement:
lemma ofSpaceTranslation_rotation (a : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) :
    (ofSpaceTranslation a).rotation = 1

declarations.name: GalileanGroup.ofSpaceTranslation_velocity
declarations.statement:
lemma ofSpaceTranslation_velocity (a : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) :
    (ofSpaceTranslation a).velocity = 0

declarations.name: GalileanGroup.ofSpaceTranslation_spaceTranslation
declarations.statement:
lemma ofSpaceTranslation_spaceTranslation (a : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) :
    (ofSpaceTranslation a).spaceTranslation = a

declarations.name: GalileanGroup.ofSpaceTranslation_timeTranslation
declarations.statement:
lemma ofSpaceTranslation_timeTranslation (a : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) :
    (ofSpaceTranslation a).timeTranslation = 0

declarations.name: GalileanGroup.spaceTranslation.incl
declarations.doc: Inclusion of spatial translations into the Galilean group.
declarations.statement:
def spaceTranslation.incl :
    Multiplicative (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) →* GalileanGroup d

declarations.name: GalileanGroup.spaceTranslationGroup.incl
declarations.doc: Inclusion of the existing spatial translation subgroup into the Galilean group.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def spaceTranslationGroup.incl :
    EuclideanGroup.TranslationGroup d →* GalileanGroup d

declarations.name: GalileanGroup.ofTimeTranslation
declarations.doc: A pure time translation as a Galilean transformation.
declarations.statement: def ofTimeTranslation (b : Time) : GalileanGroup d

declarations.name: GalileanGroup.ofTimeTranslation_rotation
declarations.statement:
lemma ofTimeTranslation_rotation (b : Time) :
    (ofTimeTranslation (d := d) b).rotation = 1

declarations.name: GalileanGroup.ofTimeTranslation_velocity
declarations.statement:
lemma ofTimeTranslation_velocity (b : Time) :
    (ofTimeTranslation (d := d) b).velocity = 0

declarations.name: GalileanGroup.ofTimeTranslation_spaceTranslation
declarations.statement:
lemma ofTimeTranslation_spaceTranslation (b : Time) :
    (ofTimeTranslation (d := d) b).spaceTranslation = 0

declarations.name: GalileanGroup.ofTimeTranslation_timeTranslation
declarations.statement:
lemma ofTimeTranslation_timeTranslation (b : Time) :
    (ofTimeTranslation (d := d) b).timeTranslation = b

declarations.name: GalileanGroup.timeTranslation.incl
declarations.doc: Inclusion of time translations into the Galilean group.
declarations.statement: def timeTranslation.incl : Multiplicative Time →* GalileanGroup d

modules.title: Reference frames
modules.doc:
A point in space and a list of coordinates are different kinds of data. Assigning coordinates to a
point requires an origin and a basis for measuring displacements from that origin. A
`ReferenceFrame` records those choices at every time.

This distinction is built into `Space d`, which is an affine space. Two points determine a
displacement, but no point is automatically the zero point. The chosen origin therefore belongs to
the frame, not to space itself. Similarly, a displacement has coordinate components only after a
basis has been chosen. Real-valued coordinates in all frames use the same implicit units of space
and time. Different frames represent different coordinate grids, not different units.

Most applications should use frames that are both inertial and orthonormal. In orthonormal frames,
the norm and inner product of coordinate vectors are given by the familiar Euclidean formulas. The
extra generality here also permits nonorthonormal coordinate grids. Giving every coordinate tuple
the standard Euclidean norm and dot product, independently of its basis, would make coordinate
transformations involving such a grid non-isometric: the same geometric displacement could acquire
different lengths, or a pair of displacements a different angle, merely by changing frames. Instead,
the metric on frame vectors is pulled back from geometric displacement space through the frame
basis. The usual component formulas are recovered for orthonormal frames.

sections.text:
## A. Reference frames

A reference frame can be pictured as a coordinate grid carried through time. It is part of how
motion is described, not an additional physical object moving with the particles.

## B. Inertial reference frames

In Newtonian mechanics, an inertial coordinate grid does not rotate or change scale, and its origin
moves in a straight line at constant velocity. These conditions restrict the frame, not the
particles described in that frame.

## C. Vectors in a reference frame

`frame.Vector` is the common coordinate carrier for vector quantities expressed relative to
`frame`. It intentionally records the coordinate frame but not the physical dimension, so relative
position, velocity, acceleration, force, momentum, and similar quantities can use the same
componentwise calculations. Their different physical roles, units, and transformation laws must be
supplied by the surrounding definitions. When a vector represents a displacement, `dispEquiv`
converts its coordinates into the corresponding geometric displacement at a given time.

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.ReferenceFrame
declarations.doc: A time origin and a time-indexed spatial origin and basis in `d`-dimensional space.
declarations.statement:
structure ReferenceFrame (d : ℕ) where
  /-- The instant assigned time coordinate zero. -/
  timeOrigin : Time
  /-- The point assigned coordinate zero at each time. -/
  origin : Time → Space d
  /-- The basis used to turn displacement vectors into coordinate components at each time. -/
  basis : Time → Module.Basis (Fin d) ℝ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d))

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.ReferenceFrame.fromReferencePoints
declarations.doc:
Build a reference frame from the trajectories of a collection of reference points.

At each time, the reference points must form an affine basis: none is redundant, and together they
span the whole space. One reference point is chosen as the origin, and the displacements from it to
the remaining points form the coordinate basis. The resulting frame need not be inertial or
orthonormal.
declarations.statement:
def ReferenceFrame.fromReferencePoints
    (timeOrigin : Time)
    (referencePoints : Finset (Time → Space d))
    (independence : ∀ t, AffineIndependent ℝ fun point : referencePoints => point.val t)
    (spans_space : ∀ t, affineSpan ℝ {point.val t | point : referencePoints} = ⊤) :
    ReferenceFrame d

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.ReferenceFrame.timeEquiv
declarations.doc: Convert a frame's real-valued time coordinate into an instant in affine time.
declarations.statement: def timeEquiv (frame : ReferenceFrame d) : ℝ ≃ᵃ[ℝ] Time

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.ReferenceFrame.IsMetricConserved
declarations.doc: Whether the frame basis induces the same inner product on coordinates at every time.
declarations.statement: def IsMetricConserved (frame : ReferenceFrame d) : Prop

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.ReferenceFrame.Orthonormal
declarations.doc: Whether the frame's coordinate basis is orthonormal at every time.
declarations.statement: def Orthonormal (frame : ReferenceFrame d) : Prop

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.ReferenceFrame.Orthonormal.isMetricConserved
declarations.doc: An orthonormal frame conserves its coordinate metric.
declarations.statement: lemma Orthonormal.isMetricConserved (h : frame.Orthonormal) : frame.IsMetricConserved
instance [h : Fact frame.Orthonormal] : Fact frame.IsMetricConserved

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.ReferenceFrame.IsInertial
declarations.doc: Whether a reference frame is related to its initial grid by uniform translation alone.
declarations.statement:
structure IsInertial (frame : ReferenceFrame d) : Prop where
  /-- Elapsed time times `velocity` is exactly the origin's displacement. -/
  origin_moves_uniformly :
    ∃ velocity, ∀ t₁ t₂, frame.origin t₂ -ᵥ frame.origin t₁ = (t₂ -ᵥ t₁) • velocity
  /-- The coordinate axes neither rotate nor change scale with time. -/
  basis_conserved : ∀ t₁ t₂, frame.basis t₁ = frame.basis t₂

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.ReferenceFrame.IsInertial.velocity
declarations.doc: The time-independent velocity of an inertial frame's coordinate origin.
declarations.statement: def IsInertial.velocity (h : frame.IsInertial) : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.ReferenceFrame.IsInertial.isMetricConserved
declarations.doc: An inertial frame conserves its coordinate metric.
declarations.statement: lemma IsInertial.isMetricConserved (h : frame.IsInertial) : frame.IsMetricConserved

declarations.doc: Inertiality provides the conserved metric needed for metric operations on frame vectors.
declarations.statement: instance [h : Fact frame.IsInertial] : Fact frame.IsMetricConserved

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.ReferenceFrame.Vector
declarations.doc: The `d` real components used to express a vector quantity relative to `frame`.
declarations.statement:
structure Vector (frame : ReferenceFrame d) where
  /-- One scalar coefficient for each axis of the frame. -/
  components : Fin d → ℝ

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.ReferenceFrame.Vector.componentEquiv
declarations.doc: Equivalence between frame vectors and coordinate components
declarations.statement: def componentEquiv : frame.Vector ≃ (Fin d → ℝ)
instance : AddCommGroup frame.Vector
instance : Module ℝ frame.Vector

declarations.doc: Scalar multiplication by a positive real.
declarations.statement: instance : SMul {x : ℝ // 0 < x} frame.Vector

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.ReferenceFrame.Vector.componentLinearEquiv
declarations.doc: Linear equivalence between frame vectors and coordinate components.
declarations.statement: def componentLinearEquiv : frame.Vector ≃ₗ[ℝ] (Fin d → ℝ)

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.ReferenceFrame.Vector.dispEquiv
declarations.doc:
Equivalence between frame vectors and geometric displacements in space,
defined by the frame's basis at time coordinate `t`.
declarations.statement: def dispEquiv (t : ℝ) : frame.Vector ≃ₗ[ℝ] EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)

declarations.doc: Use the same topology for frame vectors as components' product topology.
declarations.statement: instance : TopologicalSpace frame.Vector

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.ReferenceFrame.Vector.componentContLinearEquiv
declarations.doc: Continuous linear equivalence between frame vectors and coordinate components.
declarations.statement: def componentContLinearEquiv (frame : ReferenceFrame d) : frame.Vector ≃L[ℝ] (Fin d → ℝ)
instance : FiniteDimensional ℝ frame.Vector

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.ReferenceFrame.Vector.contDispEquiv
declarations.doc:
Continuous equivalence between frame vectors and geometric displacements in space,
defined by the frame's basis at time coordinate `t`.
declarations.statement: def contDispEquiv (t : ℝ) : frame.Vector ≃L[ℝ] EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)

declarations.doc: The physical norm on frame vectors, pulled back from geometric displacement space.
declarations.statement: instance [_h : Fact frame.IsMetricConserved] : NormedAddCommGroup frame.Vector

declarations.doc: The physical inner product on frame vectors, pulled back from geometric displacement space.
declarations.statement: instance [Fact frame.IsMetricConserved] : InnerProductSpace ℝ frame.Vector

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.ReferenceFrame.Vector.norm_euclidean_if_orthonormal
declarations.doc: In an orthonormal frame, the norm is the square root of squared components.
declarations.statement:
lemma norm_euclidean_if_orthonormal [h : Fact frame.Orthonormal] :
    ∀ v : frame.Vector, ‖v‖^2 = ∑ i, (v.components i)^2

declarations.name: ClassicalMechanics.ReferenceFrame.Vector.inner_euclidean_if_orthonormal
declarations.doc: In an orthonormal frame, the inner product is the sum of component products.
declarations.statement:
lemma inner_euclidean_if_orthonormal [h : Fact frame.Orthonormal] :
    ∀ v w : frame.Vector, inner ℝ v w = ∑ i, v.components i * w.components i

modules.title: Space
modules.doc:
In this module, we define the the type `Space d` which corresponds
to `d`-dimensional flat Euclidean space and prove some properties about it.

The scope of this module is to define on `Space d` basic instances related translations and
the metric. We do not here define the structure of a `Module` on `Space d`, as this is done in
`Physlib.SpaceAndTime.Space.Module`.

Physlib sits downstream of Mathlib, and above we import the necessary Mathlib modules
which contain (perhaps transitively through imports) the definitions and theorems we need.

## Implementation details

The exact implementation of `Space d` into Physlib is discussed in numerous places
on the Lean Zulip, including:

- https://leanprover.zulipchat.com/#narrow/channel/479953-Physlib/topic/Space.20vs.20EuclideanSpace/with/575332888

There is a choice between defining `Space d` as an `abbrev` of `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)`,
as a `def` of a type with value `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)` or as a structure
with a field `val : Fin d → ℝ` :

+---------------------------------------------------+---------+-------+-----------+
|                                                   | abbrev  |  def  | structure |
+---------------------------------------------------+---------+-------+-----------+
| allows casting from `EuclideanSpace`              |   yes   |  yes  |    no     |
| carries instances from `EuclideanSpace`           |   yes   |  no   |    no     |
| requires reproving of lemmas from `EuclideanSpace`|   no    |  yes  |    yes    |
+---------------------------------------------------+---------+-------+-----------+

The `structure` is the most conservative choice, as everything needs redefining. However,
there is are two benefits of using it:

1. It allows us to be precise about the instances we define on `Space d`, and makes
  future refactoring of those instances easier.
2. It allows us to give the necessary physics context to results about `Space d`, which
  would not otherwise be possible if we reuse results from Mathlib.

In this module we give `Space d` the instances of a `NormedAddTorsor`
and a `MetricSpace`. These physically correspond to the statement that
you can add a vector to a point in space, and that there is a notion of distance between
points in space. This notion of distance corresponds to a choice of length unit.

In `Physlib.SpaceAndTime.Space.Module` we give `Space d` the structure of a `Module`
(aka vector space), a `Norm` and an `InnerProductSpace`. These require certain choices, for example
the choice of a zero in `Space d`.

This module structure is necessary in numerous places. For example,
the normal derivatives used by physicists `∂_x, ∂_y, ∂_z` require a
module structure.

Because of this, one should be careful to avoid using the explicit zero in `Space d`,
or adding two `Space d` values together. Where possible one should use
the `VAdd (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) (Space d)` instance instead.

declarations.name: Space
declarations.doc:
The type `Space d` is the world-volume which corresponds to
`d` dimensional (flat) Euclidean space with a given (but arbitrary)
choice of length unit, and a given (but arbitrary) choice of zero.

The default value of `d` is `3`. Thus `Space = Space 3`
declarations.statement:
structure Space (d : ℕ := 3) where
  /-- The underlying map `Fin d → ℝ` associated with a point in `Space`. -/
  val : Fin d → ℝ

declarations.name: Space.eq_of_val
declarations.statement:
lemma eq_of_val {d} {p q : Space d} (h : p.val = q.val) :
    p = q

declarations.name: Space.val_eq_iff
declarations.statement:
lemma val_eq_iff {d} {p q : Space d} :
    p.val = q.val ↔ p = q
instance {d} : CoeFun (Space d) (fun _ => Fin d → ℝ)

declarations.name: Space.eq_of_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma eq_of_apply {d} {p q : Space d}
    (h : ∀ i : Fin d, p i = q i) : p = q
instance {d} : Nonempty (Space d)
instance : Subsingleton (Space 0)
noncomputable instance : VAdd (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) (Space d)

declarations.name: Space.vadd_val
declarations.statement:
lemma vadd_val {d} (v : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) (s : Space d) :
    (v +ᵥ s).val = fun i => v i + s.val i

declarations.name: Space.vadd_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma vadd_apply {d} (v : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d))
    (s : Space d) (i : Fin d) :
    (v +ᵥ s) i = v i + s i

declarations.name: Space.vadd_transitive
declarations.statement:
lemma vadd_transitive {d} (s1 s2 : Space d) :
    ∃ v : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d), v +ᵥ s1 = s2
noncomputable instance : AddAction (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) (Space d)
noncomputable instance {d} : VSub (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) (Space d)

declarations.name: Space.vsub_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma vsub_apply {d} (s1 s2 : Space d) (i : Fin d) :
    (s1 -ᵥ s2) i = s1 i - s2 i
noncomputable instance {d} : AddTorsor (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) (Space d)
noncomputable instance {d} : Dist (Space d)

declarations.name: Space.dist_eq
declarations.statement: lemma dist_eq {d} (p q : Space d) : dist p q = √ (∑ i, (p i - q i) ^ 2)
noncomputable instance {d} : PseudoMetricSpace (Space d)
noncomputable instance {d} : NormedAddTorsor (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) (Space d)
noncomputable instance {d} : MetricSpace (Space d)

declarations.name: Space.instNontrivial
declarations.statement: instance instNontrivial {d : ℕ} [NeZero d] : Nontrivial (Space d)

declarations.name: Space.homEuclideanSpaceSpace
declarations.doc:
`Space d` is homoemorphic to d-dimensional euclidean space. This is used to define the `IsManifold`
instance on `Space d`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def homEuclideanSpaceSpace (d : ℕ) : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) ≃ₜ Space d
noncomputable instance (d : ℕ) : ChartedSpace (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) (Space d)
instance (d : ℕ) : IsManifold (𝓡 d) ⊤ (Space d)

declarations.name: Space.chartAt_eq
declarations.statement:
lemma chartAt_eq (d : ℕ) (p : Space d) :
    chartAt (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) p =
    (homEuclideanSpaceSpace d).symm.toOpenPartialHomeomorph

modules.title: Constant slice distributions
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

In this module we define the lift of distributions on `Space d` to distributions
on `Space d.succ` which are constant between slices in the `i`th direction.

This is used, for example, to define distributions which are translationally invariant
in the `i`th direction.

Examples of distributions which can be constructed in this way include the dirac deltas for
lines and planes, rather then points.

## ii. Key results

- `sliceSchwartz` : The continuous linear map which takes a Schwartz map on
  `Space d.succ` and gives a Schwartz map on `Space d` by integrating over the `i`th direction.
- `constantSliceDist` : The distribution on `Space d.succ` formed by a distribution on `Space d`
  which is translationally invariant in the `i`th direction.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Schwartz maps

- B. Constant slice distribution

declarations.name: Space.schwartzMap_slice_bound
declarations.statement:
lemma schwartzMap_slice_bound {n m} {d : ℕ} (i : Fin d.succ) :
    ∃ rt, ∀ (η : 𝓢(Space d.succ, ℝ)), ∃ k,
    Integrable (fun x : ℝ => ‖((1 + ‖x‖) ^ rt)⁻¹‖) volume ∧
    (∀ (x : Space d), ∀ r, ‖(slice i).symm (r, x)‖ ^ m *
      ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ n ⇑η ((slice i).symm (r, x))‖ ≤ k * ‖(1 + ‖r‖) ^ (rt)‖⁻¹)
      ∧ k = (2 ^ (rt + m, n).1 * ((Finset.Iic (rt + m, n)).sup
        fun m => SchwartzMap.seminorm ℝ m.1 m.2) η)

declarations.name: Space.schwartzMap_mul_iteratedFDeriv_integrable_slice_symm
declarations.statement:

    (η : 𝓢(Space d.succ, ℝ))
    (x : Space d) (i : Fin d.succ) :
    Integrable (fun r => ‖(slice i).symm (r, x)‖ ^ m *
    ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ n ⇑η ((slice i).symm (r, x))‖) volume

lemma schwartzMap_integrable_slice_symm {d : ℕ} (i : Fin d.succ) (η : 𝓢(Space d.succ, ℝ))

    (i : Fin d.succ) :
    Integrable (fun r => fderiv ℝ (fun x => η (((slice i).symm (r, x)))) x) volume

declarations.name: Space.schwartzMap_fderiv_left_integrable_slice_symm
declarations.statement:

declarations.statement:
lemma schwartzMap_iteratedFDeriv_slice_symm_integrable {n} {d : ℕ} (η : 𝓢(Space d.succ, ℝ))

declarations.statement:
lemma continuous_schwartzMap_slice_integral {d} (i : Fin d.succ) (η : 𝓢(Space d.succ, ℝ)) :
    Continuous (fun x : Space d => ∫ r : ℝ, η ((slice i).symm (r, x)))

declarations.statement:

    (x₀ : Space d) :
    HasFDerivAt (fun x => ∫ (r : ℝ), η ((slice i).symm (r, x)))
      (∫ (r : ℝ), fderiv ℝ (fun x : Space d => η ((slice i).symm (r, x))) x₀) x₀

declarations.statement:
lemma schwartzMap_slice_integral_differentiable {d : ℕ} (η : 𝓢(Space d.succ, ℝ))
    (i : Fin d.succ) :

declarations.statement:
lemma schwartzMap_slice_integral_contDiff {d : ℕ} (n : ℕ) (η : 𝓢(Space d.succ, ℝ))
    (i : Fin d.succ) :
    ContDiff ℝ n (fun x => ∫ (r : ℝ), η ((slice i).symm (r, x)))

declarations.name: Space.schwartzMap_slice_integral_iteratedFDeriv_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma schwartzMap_slice_integral_iteratedFDeriv_apply {d : ℕ} (n : ℕ) (η : 𝓢(Space d.succ, ℝ))
    (i : Fin d.succ) :
    ∀ x, ∀ y, iteratedFDeriv ℝ n (fun x => ∫ (r : ℝ), η ((slice i).symm (r, x))) x y =
      ∫ (r : ℝ), (iteratedFDeriv ℝ n η ((slice i).symm (r, x)))
      (fun j => (slice i).symm (0, y j))

declarations.name: Space.schwartzMap_slice_integral_iteratedFDeriv
declarations.statement:
lemma schwartzMap_slice_integral_iteratedFDeriv {d : ℕ} (n : ℕ) (η : 𝓢(Space d.succ, ℝ))
    (i : Fin d.succ) (x : Space d) :
    iteratedFDeriv ℝ n (fun x => ∫ (r : ℝ), η ((slice i).symm (r, x))) x
    = (∫ (r : ℝ), iteratedFDeriv ℝ n η ((slice i).symm (r, x))).compContinuousLinearMap
      (fun _ => (slice i).symm.toContinuousLinearMap.comp
      (ContinuousLinearMap.prod (0 : Space d →L[ℝ] ℝ) (ContinuousLinearMap.id ℝ (Space d))))

declarations.name: Space.schwartzMap_slice_integral_iteratedFDeriv_norm_le
declarations.statement:
lemma schwartzMap_slice_integral_iteratedFDeriv_norm_le {d : ℕ} (n : ℕ) (η : 𝓢(Space d.succ, ℝ))
    (i : Fin d.succ) (x : Space d) :
    ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ n (fun x => ∫ (r : ℝ), η ((slice i).symm (r, x))) x‖ ≤
        (∫ (r : ℝ), ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ n η ((slice i).symm (r, x))‖) *
        ‖(slice i).symm.toContinuousLinearMap.comp
          (ContinuousLinearMap.prod (0 : Space d →L[ℝ] ℝ)
          (ContinuousLinearMap.id ℝ (Space d)))‖ ^ n

declarations.name: Space.schwartzMap_mul_pow_slice_integral_iteratedFDeriv_norm_le
declarations.statement:
lemma schwartzMap_mul_pow_slice_integral_iteratedFDeriv_norm_le {d : ℕ} (n m : ℕ) (i : Fin d.succ) :
    ∃ rt, ∀ (η : 𝓢(Space d.succ, ℝ)),∀ (x : Space d),
    Integrable (fun x : ℝ => ‖((1 + ‖x‖) ^ rt)⁻¹‖) volume ∧
    ‖x‖ ^ m * ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ n (fun x => ∫ (r : ℝ), η ((slice i).symm (r, x))) x‖ ≤
        ((∫ (r : ℝ), ‖((1 + ‖r‖) ^ rt)⁻¹‖) *
        ‖(slice i).symm.toContinuousLinearMap.comp
          (ContinuousLinearMap.prod (0 : Space d →L[ℝ] ℝ)
          (ContinuousLinearMap.id ℝ (Space d)))‖ ^ n)
        * (2 ^ (rt + m, n).1 * ((Finset.Iic (rt + m, n)).sup
          fun m => SchwartzMap.seminorm ℝ m.1 m.2) η)

declarations.name: Space.sliceSchwartz
declarations.doc:
The continuous linear map taking a Schwartz map and integrating over the `i`th component,
to give a Schwartz map of one dimension lower.
declarations.statement:
def sliceSchwartz {d : ℕ} (i : Fin d.succ) :
    𝓢(Space d.succ, ℝ) →L[ℝ] 𝓢(Space d, ℝ)

declarations.name: Space.sliceSchwartz_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma sliceSchwartz_apply {d : ℕ} (i : Fin d.succ) (η : 𝓢(Space d.succ, ℝ)) (x : Space d) :
    sliceSchwartz i η x = ∫ (r : ℝ), η ((slice i).symm (r, x))

declarations.name: Space.constantSliceDist
declarations.doc:
Distributions on `Space d.succ` from distributions on `Space d` given a
direction `i`.
These distributions are constant on slices in the `i` direction..
declarations.statement:
def constantSliceDist {M : Type} [NormedAddCommGroup M] [NormedSpace ℝ M] {d : ℕ} (i : Fin d.succ) :
    ((Space d) →d[ℝ] M) →ₗ[ℝ] (Space d.succ) →d[ℝ] M

declarations.name: Space.constantSliceDist_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma constantSliceDist_apply {M : Type} [NormedAddCommGroup M] [NormedSpace ℝ M]
    {d : ℕ} (i : Fin d.succ) (f : (Space d) →d[ℝ] M) (η : 𝓢(Space d.succ, ℝ)) :
    constantSliceDist i f η = f (sliceSchwartz i η)

declarations.name: Space.distDeriv_constantSliceDist_same
declarations.statement:
lemma distDeriv_constantSliceDist_same {M : Type} [NormedAddCommGroup M] [NormedSpace ℝ M]
    {d : ℕ} (i : Fin d.succ) (f : (Space d) →d[ℝ] M) :
    distDeriv i (constantSliceDist i f) = 0

declarations.name: Space.distDeriv_constantSliceDist_succAbove
declarations.statement:
lemma distDeriv_constantSliceDist_succAbove {M : Type} [NormedAddCommGroup M] [NormedSpace ℝ M]
    {d : ℕ} (i : Fin d.succ) (j : Fin d) (f : (Space d) →d[ℝ] M) :
    distDeriv (i.succAbove j) (constantSliceDist i f) =
    constantSliceDist i (distDeriv j f)

modules.title: The cross product on Euclidean vectors in three dimensions
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

In this module we define the cross product on `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)`,
and prove various properties about it related to time derivatives and inner products.

## ii. Key results

- `⨯ₑ₃` : The cross product on `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)`.
- `time_deriv_cross_commute` : Time derivatives move out of cross products.
- `inner_cross_self` : Inner product of a vector with the cross product of another vector
  and itself is zero.
- `inner_self_cross` : Inner product of a vector with the cross product of itself
  and another vector is zero.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The notation for the cross product
- B. Time derivatives move out of cross products
- C. Inner product of vectors with cross products involving themselves

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: Space.fderiv_cross_commute
declarations.doc: Cross product and fderiv commute.
declarations.statement:
lemma fderiv_cross_commute {t : Time} {s : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)}
    {f : Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)} (hf : Differentiable ℝ f) :
    s ⨯ₑ₃ (fderiv ℝ (fun t' => f t') t) 1
    = fderiv ℝ (fun t' => s ⨯ₑ₃ (f t')) t 1

declarations.name: Space.time_deriv_cross_commute
declarations.doc: Cross product and time derivative commute.

declarations.name: Space.inner_cross_self
declarations.statement:
lemma inner_cross_self (v w : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)) :
    inner ℝ v (w ⨯ₑ₃ v) = 0

declarations.name: Space.inner_self_cross
declarations.statement:
lemma inner_self_cross (v w : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)) :
    inner ℝ v (v ⨯ₑ₃ w) = 0

declarations.name: Space.deriv
declarations.doc: Given a function `f : Space d → M` the derivative of `f` in direction `μ`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def deriv {M d} [AddCommGroup M] [Module ℝ M] [TopologicalSpace M]
    (μ : Fin d) (f : Space d → M) : Space d → M

declarations.name: Space.deriv_eq
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_eq [AddCommGroup M] [Module ℝ M] [TopologicalSpace M]
    (μ : Fin d) (f : Space d → M) (x : Space d) :
    deriv μ f x = fderiv ℝ f x (basis μ)

declarations.name: Space.deriv_eq_fderiv_fun
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_eq_fderiv_fun [AddCommGroup M] [Module ℝ M] [TopologicalSpace M]
    (μ : Fin d) (f : Space d → M) :
    deriv μ f = fun x => fderiv ℝ (fun x => f x) x (basis μ)

declarations.name: Space.deriv_eq_fderiv_basis
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_eq_fderiv_basis [AddCommGroup M] [Module ℝ M] [TopologicalSpace M]
    (μ : Fin d) (f : Space d → M) (x : Space d) :
    deriv μ f x = fderiv ℝ f x (basis μ)

declarations.name: Space.fderiv_eq_sum_deriv
declarations.statement:
lemma fderiv_eq_sum_deriv {M d} [AddCommGroup M] [Module ℝ M] [TopologicalSpace M]
    (f : Space d → M) (x y : Space d) :
    fderiv ℝ f x y = ∑ i : Fin d, y i • ∂[i] f x

declarations.name: Space.deriv_eq_mfderiv
declarations.doc:
The spatial-derivative in terms of the derivative of functions between
manifolds.
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_eq_mfderiv {M d} [NormedAddCommGroup M] [NormedSpace ℝ M]
    (μ : Fin d) (f : Space d → M) (x : Space d) :
    deriv μ f x = mfderiv 𝓘(ℝ, Space d) 𝓘(ℝ, M) f x (basis μ)

declarations.name: Space.mdifferentiable_manifoldStructure_iff_differentiable
declarations.statement:
lemma mdifferentiable_manifoldStructure_iff_differentiable {M d} [NormedAddCommGroup M]
    [NormedSpace ℝ M] {f : Space d → M} {x : Space d} :
    MDifferentiableAt (𝓡 d) 𝓘(ℝ, M) f x ↔ DifferentiableAt ℝ f x

declarations.name: Space.deriv_eq_mfderiv_manifoldStructure
declarations.doc:
The spatial-derivative in terms of the derivative of functions between
manifolds with the manifold structure `Space.manifoldStructure d`.
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_eq_mfderiv_manifoldStructure {M d} [NormedAddCommGroup M] [NormedSpace ℝ M]
    (μ : Fin d) (f : Space d → M) (x : Space d) :
    deriv μ f x = mfderiv (𝓡 d) 𝓘(ℝ, M) f x (EuclideanSpace.single μ 1)

declarations.name: Space.deriv_const
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_const [NormedAddCommGroup M] [NormedSpace ℝ M] (m : M) (μ : Fin d) :
    deriv μ (fun _ => m) t = 0

declarations.name: Space.deriv_add
declarations.doc: Derivatives on space distribute over addition.
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_add [NormedAddCommGroup M] [NormedSpace ℝ M]
    (f1 f2 : Space d → M) (hf1 : Differentiable ℝ f1) (hf2 : Differentiable ℝ f2) :
    ∂[u] (f1 + f2) = ∂[u] f1 + ∂[u] f2

declarations.name: Space.deriv_coord_add
declarations.doc: Derivatives on space distribute coordinate-wise over addition.
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_coord_add (f1 f2 : Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d))
    (hf1 : Differentiable ℝ f1) (hf2 : Differentiable ℝ f2) :
    (∂[u] (fun x => f1 x i + f2 x i)) =
      (∂[u] (fun x => f1 x i)) + (∂[u] (fun x => f2 x i))

declarations.name: Space.deriv_sub
declarations.doc: Derivatives on space distribute over subtraction.
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_sub [NormedAddCommGroup M] [NormedSpace ℝ M]
    (f1 f2 : Space d → M) (hf1 : Differentiable ℝ f1) (hf2 : Differentiable ℝ f2) :
    ∂[u] (f1 - f2) = ∂[u] f1 - ∂[u] f2

declarations.name: Space.deriv_smul
declarations.doc: Space derivatives on scalar product of functions.
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_smul [NormedAddCommGroup M] [NormedSpace ℝ M] [NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜]
    [NormedAlgebra ℝ 𝕜] [NormedSpace 𝕜 M] {c : Space d → 𝕜} {f : Space d → M}
    (hc : DifferentiableAt ℝ c x) (hf : DifferentiableAt ℝ f x) :
    ∂[u] (c • f) x = c x • ∂[u] f x + ∂[u] c x • f x

declarations.name: Space.deriv_const_smul
declarations.doc: Space derivatives on scalar times function.
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_const_smul [NormedAddCommGroup M] [NormedSpace ℝ M] [Semiring R]
    [Module R M] [SMulCommClass ℝ R M] [ContinuousConstSMul R M] {f : Space d → M} (c : R)
    (h : Differentiable ℝ f) : ∂[u] (c • f) = c • ∂[u] f

declarations.name: Space.deriv_coord_smul
declarations.doc: Coordinate-wise scalar multiplication on space derivatives.
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_coord_smul (f : Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) (k : ℝ)
    (hf : Differentiable ℝ f) :
    ∂[u] (fun x => k * f x i) x = k * ∂[u] (fun x => f x i) x

declarations.name: Space.deriv_commute
declarations.doc: Derivatives on space commute with one another.
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_commute [NormedAddCommGroup M] [NormedSpace ℝ M]
    (f : Space d → M) (hf : ContDiff ℝ 2 f) : ∂[u] (∂[v] f) = ∂[v] (∂[u] f)

declarations.name: Space.deriv_component_same
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_component_same (μ : Fin d) (x : Space d) :
    ∂[μ] (fun x => x μ) x = 1

declarations.name: Space.deriv_component_diff
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_component_diff (μ ν : Fin d) (x : Space d) (h : μ ≠ ν) :
    (deriv μ (fun x => x ν) x) = 0

declarations.name: Space.deriv_component
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_component (μ ν : Fin d) (x : Space d) :
    (deriv ν (fun x => x μ) x) = if ν = μ then 1 else 0

declarations.name: Space.deriv_component_sq
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_component_sq {d : ℕ} {ν μ : Fin d} (x : Space d) :
    (deriv ν (fun x => (x μ) ^ 2) x) = if ν = μ then 2 * x μ else 0

declarations.name: Space.deriv_prod_coord
declarations.doc:
The derivative in direction `μ` of `x ↦ ∏ⱼ gⱼ (xⱼ)`, a product of differentiable functions
of one coordinate each, is `gμ' (xμ)` times the product of the other factors.
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_prod_coord {d : ℕ} (g : Fin d → ℝ → ℂ) (hg : ∀ j, Differentiable ℝ (g j))
    (μ : Fin d) (x : Space d) :
    ∂[μ] (fun x : Space d => ∏ j, g j (x j)) x =
      _root_.deriv (g μ) (x μ) * ∏ j ∈ Finset.univ.erase μ, g j (x j)

declarations.name: Space.deriv_euclid
Space.deriv_lorentz_vector
Space.norm_sq_differentiable
declarations.statement: lemma norm_sq_differentiable : Differentiable ℝ (fun x : Space d => ‖x‖ ^ 2)

declarations.name: Space.deriv_norm_sq
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_norm_sq (x : Space d) (i : Fin d) :
    deriv i (fun x => ‖x‖ ^ 2) x = 2 * x i

declarations.name: Space.inner_differentiable
declarations.doc: The inner product is differentiable.
declarations.statement:
lemma inner_differentiable {d : ℕ} :
    Differentiable ℝ (fun y : Space d => ⟪y, y⟫_ℝ)

declarations.name: Space.inner_differentiableAt
declarations.statement:
lemma inner_differentiableAt {d : ℕ} (x : Space d) :
    DifferentiableAt ℝ (fun y : Space d => ⟪y, y⟫_ℝ) x

declarations.name: Space.inner_apply_differentiableAt
declarations.statement:
lemma inner_apply_differentiableAt {d : ℕ} [NormedAddCommGroup M]
    [NormedSpace ℝ M]
    {f : M → Space d} {g : M → Space d} (x : M)
    (hf : DifferentiableAt ℝ f x) (hg : DifferentiableAt ℝ g x) :
    DifferentiableAt ℝ (fun y : M => ⟪f y, g y⟫_ℝ) x

declarations.name: Space.inner_apply_differentiable
declarations.statement:
lemma inner_apply_differentiable {d : ℕ} [NormedAddCommGroup M]
    [NormedSpace ℝ M]
    {f : M → Space d} {g : M → Space d}
    (hf : Differentiable ℝ f) (hg : Differentiable ℝ g) :
    Differentiable ℝ (fun y : M => ⟪f y, g y⟫_ℝ)

declarations.name: Space.inner_contDiff
declarations.statement:
lemma inner_contDiff {n : WithTop ℕ∞} {d : ℕ} :
    ContDiff ℝ n (fun y : Space d => ⟪y, y⟫_ℝ)

declarations.name: Space.inner_apply_contDiff
declarations.statement:
lemma inner_apply_contDiff {n : WithTop ℕ∞} {d : ℕ} [NormedAddCommGroup M]
    [NormedSpace ℝ M]
    {f : M → Space d} {g : M → Space d}
    (hf : ContDiff ℝ n f) (hg : ContDiff ℝ n g) :
    ContDiff ℝ n (fun y : M => ⟪f y, g y⟫_ℝ)

declarations.name: Space.deriv_eq_inner_self
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_eq_inner_self (x : Space d) (i : Fin d) :
    deriv i (fun x => ⟪x, x⟫_ℝ) x = 2 * x i

declarations.name: Space.deriv_inner_left
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_inner_left {d} (x1 x2 : Space d) (i : Fin d) :
    deriv i (fun x => ⟪x, x2⟫_ℝ) x1 = x2 i

declarations.name: Space.deriv_inner_right
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_inner_right {d} (x1 x2 : Space d) (i : Fin d) :
    deriv i (fun x => ⟪x1, x⟫_ℝ) x2 = x1 i

declarations.name: Space.deriv_differentiable
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_differentiable {M} [NormedAddCommGroup M]
    [NormedSpace ℝ M] {d : ℕ} {f : Space d → M}
    (hf : ContDiff ℝ 2 f) (i : Fin d) :
    Differentiable ℝ (deriv i f)

declarations.name: Space.deriv_contDiff
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_contDiff {d} {f : Space d → ℝ} (hf : ContDiff ℝ (n + 1) f) :
    ContDiff ℝ n fun x i => deriv i f x

declarations.name: Space.distDeriv
declarations.doc:
Given a distribution (function) `f : Space d →d[ℝ] M` the derivative
of `f` in direction `μ`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def distDeriv {M d} [NormedAddCommGroup M] [NormedSpace ℝ M]
    (μ : Fin d) : ((Space d) →d[ℝ] M) →ₗ[ℝ] (Space d) →d[ℝ] M

declarations.name: Space.distDeriv_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma distDeriv_apply {M d} [NormedAddCommGroup M] [NormedSpace ℝ M]
    (μ : Fin d) (f : (Space d) →d[ℝ] M) (ε : 𝓢(Space d, ℝ)) :
    (∂ᵈ[μ] f) ε = fderivD ℝ f ε (basis μ)

declarations.name: Space.schwartMap_fderiv_comm
declarations.statement:
lemma schwartMap_fderiv_comm {d}
    (μ ν : Fin d) (x : Space d) (η : 𝓢(Space d, ℝ)) :
    ((SchwartzMap.evalCLM ℝ (Space d) ℝ (basis μ))
      ((fderivCLM ℝ (Space d) ℝ) ((SchwartzMap.evalCLM ℝ (Space d) ℝ (basis ν))
      ((fderivCLM ℝ (Space d) ℝ) η)))) x =
    ((SchwartzMap.evalCLM ℝ (Space d) ℝ (basis ν))
      ((fderivCLM ℝ (Space d) ℝ) ((SchwartzMap.evalCLM ℝ (Space d) ℝ (basis μ))
      ((fderivCLM ℝ (Space d) ℝ) η)))) x

declarations.name: Space.distDeriv_commute
declarations.statement:
lemma distDeriv_commute {M d} [NormedAddCommGroup M] [NormedSpace ℝ M]
    (μ ν : Fin d) (f : (Space d) →d[ℝ] M) :
    (∂ᵈ[ν] (∂ᵈ[μ] f)) = (∂ᵈ[μ] (∂ᵈ[ν] f))

modules.title: Curl on Space
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

In this module we define the curl of functions and distributions on 3-dimensional
space `Space 3`.

We also prove some basic vector-identities involving of the curl operator.

## ii. Key results

- `curl` : The curl operator on functions from `Space 3` to `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)`.
- `distCurl` : The curl operator on distributions from `Space 3` to `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)`.
- `div_of_curl_eq_zero` : The divergence of the curl of a function is zero.
- `distCurl_distGrad_eq_zero` : The curl of the gradient of a distribution is zero.
- `curl_eq_sum_leviCivitaSymbol` : The components of the curl as a contraction with the
  Levi-Civita symbol.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The curl on functions
  - A.1. The curl on the zero function
  - A.2. The curl on a constant function
  - A.3. Basic operations on curl
  - A.4. The curl of a linear map is a linear map
  - A.5. Preliminary lemmas about second derivatives
  - A.6. The div of a curl is zero
  - A.7. The curl of a grad is zero
  - A.8. The curl of a curl
  - A.9. A divergence-free field is a curl
  - A.10. A curl-free field is a gradient
  - A.11. The curl in terms of the Levi-Civita symbol
- B. The curl on distributions
  - B.1. The components of the curl
  - B.2. Basic equalities
  - B.3. The curl of a grad is zero

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. The curl on functions
### A.1. The curl on the zero function
### A.2. The curl on a constant function
### A.3. Basic operations on curl
### A.4. The curl of a linear map is a linear map
### A.5. Preliminary lemmas about second derivatives
### A.6. The div of a curl is zero
### A.7. The curl of a grad is zero
### A.8. The curl of a curl

### A.9. A divergence-free field is a curl

We now prove that if the divergence of a function is zero,
then it is equal to the curl of some function.

This proof is involved, thus we have split it up into private definitions and lemmas.
The proof is by explicit construction. If `f` has divergence zero,
then we construct
```
∫ t in 0..1, (t • x) ⨯ f (t • x)
```
and show that the curl of this is equal to `f`.

We call the integrand of this function the `homotopyOperatorIntegrand`.
We build API around this to help in our proof.

### A.10. A curl-free field is a gradient

We show that if the curl of a function is zero, then it is equal to the gradient of some function.
The key lemma here is
`Convex.exists_forall_hasFDerivAt_of_fderiv_symmetric`, which is
a more general version of this result in Mathlib. We turn this here into something
more familiar, to the physicists via `deriv_comm_of_curl_zero`.
### A.11. The curl in terms of the Levi-Civita symbol
## B. The curl on distributions
### B.1. The components of the curl
### B.2. Basic equalities
### B.3. The curl of a grad is zero

declarations.name: Space.curl
declarations.doc: The vector calculus operator `curl`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def curl (f : Space → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)) :
    Space → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)

declarations.name: Space.curl_zero
declarations.statement: lemma curl_zero : ∇ ⨯ (0 : Space → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)) = 0

declarations.name: Space.curl_const
declarations.statement: lemma curl_const : ∇ ⨯ (fun _ : Space => v₃) = 0

declarations.name: Space.curl_add
declarations.statement:
lemma curl_add (f1 f2 : Space → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3))
    (hf1 : Differentiable ℝ f1) (hf2 : Differentiable ℝ f2) :
    ∇ ⨯ (f1 + f2) = ∇ ⨯ f1 + ∇ ⨯ f2

declarations.name: Space.curl_smul
declarations.statement:
lemma curl_smul (f : Space → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)) (k : ℝ)
    (hf : Differentiable ℝ f) :
    ∇ ⨯ (k • f) = k • ∇ ⨯ f

declarations.name: Space.curl_neg
declarations.statement:
lemma curl_neg (f : Space → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)) (hf : Differentiable ℝ f) :
    ∇ ⨯ (-f) = -∇ ⨯ f

declarations.name: Space.curl_sub
declarations.statement:
lemma curl_sub (f1 f2 : Space → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3))
    (hf1 : Differentiable ℝ f1) (hf2 : Differentiable ℝ f2) :
    ∇ ⨯ (f1 - f2) = ∇ ⨯ f1 - ∇ ⨯ f2

declarations.name: Space.curl_linear_map
declarations.statement:
lemma curl_linear_map (f : W → Space 3 → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3))
    (hf : ∀ w, Differentiable ℝ (f w))
    (hf' : IsLinearMap ℝ f) :
    IsLinearMap ℝ (fun w => ∇ ⨯ (f w))

declarations.name: Space.deriv_coord_2nd_add
declarations.doc: Second derivatives distribute coordinate-wise over addition (all three components for div).
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_coord_2nd_add (f : Space → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)) (hf : ContDiff ℝ 2 f) :
    ∂[i] (fun x => ∂[u] (fun x => f x u) x + (∂[v] (fun x => f x v) x + ∂[w] (fun x => f x w) x)) =
    (∂[i] (∂[u] (fun x => f x u))) + (∂[i] (∂[v] (fun x => f x v))) +
    (∂[i] (∂[w] (fun x => f x w)))

declarations.name: Space.deriv_coord_2nd_sub
declarations.doc: Second derivatives distribute coordinate-wise over subtraction (two components for curl).
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_coord_2nd_sub (f : Space → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)) (hf : ContDiff ℝ 2 f) :
    ∂[u] (fun x => ∂[v] (fun x => f x w) x - ∂[w] (fun x => f x v) x) =
    (∂[u] (∂[v] (fun x => f x w))) - (∂[u] (∂[w] (fun x => f x v)))

declarations.name: Space.div_of_curl_eq_zero
declarations.statement:
lemma div_of_curl_eq_zero (f : Space → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)) (hf : ContDiff ℝ 2 f) :
    ∇ ⬝ (∇ ⨯ f) = 0

declarations.name: Space.curl_of_grad_eq_zero
declarations.statement:
lemma curl_of_grad_eq_zero (f : Space → ℝ) (hf : ContDiff ℝ 2 f) :
    ∇ ⨯ (∇ f) = 0

declarations.name: Space.curl_of_curl
declarations.statement:
lemma curl_of_curl (f : Space → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)) (hf : ContDiff ℝ 2 f) :
    ∇ ⨯ (∇ ⨯ f) = ∇ (∇ ⬝ f) - Δᵥ f

declarations.name: Space.eq_neg_curl_of_div_zero
declarations.statement:
lemma eq_neg_curl_of_div_zero (f : Space → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)) (hf : ContDiff ℝ 1 f)
    (hdiv : ∇ ⬝ f = 0) :
    f = - curl (fun x => ∫ (t : ℝ) in 0..1, (t • basis.repr x) ⨯ₑ₃ f (t • x) ∂(volume))

declarations.name: Space.exists_curl_of_div_zero
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_curl_of_div_zero (f : Space → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)) (hf : ContDiff ℝ 1 f)
    (hdiv : ∇ ⬝ f = 0) :
    ∃ g : Space → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3), f = curl g ∧ Differentiable ℝ g

declarations.name: Space.deriv_comm_of_curl_zero
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_comm_of_curl_zero (f : Space → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)) (hf : Differentiable ℝ f)
    (hcurl : curl f = 0) (x : Space) (i j : Fin 3) :
    ∂[i] f x j = ∂[j] f x i

declarations.name: Space.exists_grad_of_curl_zero
declarations.statement:
lemma exists_grad_of_curl_zero (f : Space → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)) (hf : Differentiable ℝ f)
    (hcurl : curl f = 0) : ∃ g : Space → ℝ, f = grad g ∧ Differentiable ℝ g

declarations.name: Space.eq_grad_integral_of_curl_zero
declarations.doc:
A constructive form of the statement that if the curl of a function is zero,
then it is equal to the grad of another function.

In the context of e.g. electromagnetism the potential given by this lemma corresponds
to that defined by the work done to move a unit charge from the origin to the
point `x` along a straight line.
declarations.statement:
lemma eq_grad_integral_of_curl_zero (f : Space → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)) (hf : ContDiff ℝ 1 f)
    (hcurl : curl f = 0) :
    f = grad (fun x => ∫ t in (0 : ℝ)..1, ⟪f (t • x), basis.repr x⟫_ℝ ∂(volume))

declarations.name: Space.curl_eq_sum_leviCivitaSymbol
declarations.doc:
The components of the curl as a contraction with the Levi-Civita symbol,
`(∇ ⨯ f) x i = ∑ j k, ε_{ijk} ∂[j] fₖ x`.
declarations.statement:
lemma curl_eq_sum_leviCivitaSymbol (f : Space → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3))
    (x : Space) (i : Fin 3) :
    (∇ ⨯ f) x i = ∑ j, ∑ k, (leviCivitaSymbol ![i, j, k] : ℝ) * ∂[j] (fun y => f y k) x

declarations.name: Space.distCurl
declarations.doc:
The curl of a distribution `Space →d[ℝ] (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3))` as a distribution
`Space →d[ℝ] (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3))`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def distCurl : (Space →d[ℝ] (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3))) →ₗ[ℝ]
    (Space) →d[ℝ] (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3))

declarations.name: Space.distCurl_coord_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma distCurl_coord_apply {i : Fin 3}
    (f : Space →d[ℝ] (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3))) (η : 𝓢(Space, ℝ)) :
    (∇ᵈ ⨯ f) η i = - f (SchwartzMap.evalCLM ℝ Space ℝ (basis (i+2)) (fderivCLM ℝ Space ℝ η)) (i+1)
    + f (SchwartzMap.evalCLM ℝ Space ℝ (basis (i+1)) (fderivCLM ℝ Space ℝ η)) (i+2)

declarations.name: Space.distCurl_apply_one
declarations.statement:
lemma distCurl_apply_one (f : Space →d[ℝ] (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3))) (η : 𝓢(Space, ℝ)) :
    (∇ᵈ ⨯ f) η 1 = - f (SchwartzMap.evalCLM ℝ Space ℝ (basis 0) (fderivCLM ℝ Space ℝ η)) 2
    + f (SchwartzMap.evalCLM ℝ Space ℝ (basis 2) (fderivCLM ℝ Space ℝ η)) 0

declarations.name: Space.distCurl_apply_two
declarations.statement:
lemma distCurl_apply_two (f : Space →d[ℝ] (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3))) (η : 𝓢(Space, ℝ)) :
    (∇ᵈ ⨯ f) η 2 = - f (SchwartzMap.evalCLM ℝ Space ℝ (basis 1) (fderivCLM ℝ Space ℝ η)) 0
    + f (SchwartzMap.evalCLM ℝ Space ℝ (basis 0) (fderivCLM ℝ Space ℝ η)) 1

declarations.name: Space.distCurl_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma distCurl_apply (f : Space →d[ℝ] (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3))) (η : 𝓢(Space, ℝ)) :
    (∇ᵈ ⨯ f) η = WithLp.toLp 2 fun i =>
      - f (SchwartzMap.evalCLM ℝ Space ℝ (basis (i+2)) (fderivCLM ℝ Space ℝ η)) (i+1)
      + f (SchwartzMap.evalCLM ℝ Space ℝ (basis (i+1)) (fderivCLM ℝ Space ℝ η)) (i+2)

declarations.name: Space.distCurl_distGrad_eq_zero
declarations.doc: The curl of a grad is equal to zero.
declarations.statement:
lemma distCurl_distGrad_eq_zero (f : (Space) →d[ℝ] ℝ) :
    ∇ᵈ ⨯ (∇ᵈ f) = 0

declarations.name: Space.distDiv_apply_eq_sum_fderivD
Space.distDiv_apply_eq_sum_distDeriv

declarations.name: Space.grad
declarations.doc: The vector calculus operator `grad`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def grad {d} (f : Space d → ℝ) :
  Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)

declarations.name: Space.grad_zero
declarations.statement: lemma grad_zero : ∇ (0 : Space d → ℝ) = 0

declarations.name: Space.grad_add

    (hf1 : Differentiable ℝ f1) (hf2 : Differentiable ℝ f2) :

declarations.name: Space.grad_fun_add_const

lemma grad_fun_add_const (f : Space d → ℝ) (c : ℝ) :
    ∇ (fun x => f x + c) = ∇ f

declarations.name: Space.grad_const
declarations.statement: lemma grad_const : ∇ (fun _ : Space d => c) = 0

declarations.name: Space.grad_smul
declarations.statement:
lemma grad_smul (f : Space d → ℝ) (k : ℝ)
    (hf : Differentiable ℝ f) :
    ∇ (k • f) = k • ∇ f

declarations.name: Space.grad_neg
declarations.statement:
lemma grad_neg (f : Space d → ℝ) :
    ∇ (- f) = - ∇ f

declarations.name: Space.grad_eq_sum
declarations.statement:
lemma grad_eq_sum {d} (f : Space d → ℝ) (x : Space d) :
    ∇ f x = ∑ i, ∂[i] f x • EuclideanSpace.single i 1

declarations.name: Space.grad_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma grad_apply {d} (f : Space d → ℝ) (x : Space d) (i : Fin d) :
    (∇ f x) i = ∂[i] f x

declarations.name: Space.grad_inner_single
declarations.statement:
lemma grad_inner_single {d} (f : Space d → ℝ) (x : Space d) (i : Fin d) :
    ⟪∇ f x, EuclideanSpace.single i 1⟫_ℝ = ∂[i] f x

declarations.name: Space.grad_inner_eq
declarations.statement:
lemma grad_inner_eq {d} (f : Space d → ℝ) (x : Space d) (y : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) :
    ⟪∇ f x, y⟫_ℝ = ∑ i, y i * ∂[i] f x

declarations.name: Space.inner_grad_eq
declarations.statement:
lemma inner_grad_eq {d} (f : Space d → ℝ) (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) (y : Space d) :
    ⟪x, ∇ f y⟫_ℝ = ∑ i, x i * ∂[i] f y

declarations.name: Space.grad_inner_repr_eq
declarations.statement:
lemma grad_inner_repr_eq {d} (f : Space d → ℝ) (x y : Space d) :
    ⟪∇ f x, (Space.basis).repr y⟫_ℝ = fderiv ℝ f x y

declarations.name: Space.repr_grad_inner_eq
declarations.statement:
lemma repr_grad_inner_eq {d} (f : Space d → ℝ) (x y : Space d) :
    ⟪(Space.basis).repr x, ∇ f y⟫_ℝ = fderiv ℝ f y x

declarations.name: Space.grad_eq_gradient
declarations.statement:
lemma grad_eq_gradient {d} (f : Space d → ℝ) :
    ∇ f = basis.repr ∘ gradient f

declarations.name: Space.gradient_eq_grad
declarations.statement:
lemma gradient_eq_grad {d} (f : Space d → ℝ) :
    gradient f = basis.repr.symm ∘ ∇ f

declarations.name: Space.gradient_apply_eq_grad
declarations.statement:
lemma gradient_apply_eq_grad {d} (f : Space d → ℝ) (x : Space d) :
    gradient f x = basis.repr.symm (∇ f x)

declarations.name: Space.gradient_eq_sum
declarations.statement:
lemma gradient_eq_sum {d} (f : Space d → ℝ) (x : Space d) :
    gradient f x = ∑ i, ∂[i] f x • basis i

declarations.name: Space.euclid_gradient_eq_sum
declarations.statement:
lemma euclid_gradient_eq_sum {d} (f : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d) → ℝ) (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) :
    gradient f x = ∑ i, fderiv ℝ f x (EuclideanSpace.single i 1) • EuclideanSpace.single i 1

declarations.name: DifferentiableAt.hasGradientAt_grad
declarations.statement:
lemma _root_.DifferentiableAt.hasGradientAt_grad {d} {f : Space d → ℝ} (x : Space d)
    (hf : DifferentiableAt ℝ f x) :
    HasGradientAt f (basis.repr.symm (∇ f x)) x

declarations.name: Space.grad_inner_space_unit_vector
declarations.doc: The gradient in the direction of the space position.
declarations.statement:
lemma grad_inner_space_unit_vector {d} (x : Space d) (f : Space d → ℝ) (hd : Differentiable ℝ f) :
    ⟪∇ f x, ‖x‖⁻¹ • basis.repr x⟫_ℝ = _root_.deriv (fun r => f (r • ‖x‖⁻¹ • x)) ‖x‖

declarations.name: Space.grad_inner_space
declarations.statement:
lemma grad_inner_space {d} (x : Space d) (f : Space d → ℝ) (hd : Differentiable ℝ f) :
    ⟪∇ f x, basis.repr x⟫_ℝ = ‖x‖ * _root_.deriv (fun r => f (r • ‖x‖⁻¹ • x)) ‖x‖

declarations.name: Space.grad_smul_inner_space
declarations.statement:
lemma grad_smul_inner_space {d} (x : Space d) (f : Space d → ℝ) (hd : Differentiable ℝ f) (t : ℝ)
    (ht : 0 < t) :
    ⟪∇ f (t • x), basis.repr x⟫_ℝ = _root_.deriv (fun r => f (r • x)) t

declarations.name: Space.eq_integral_grad
declarations.statement:
lemma eq_integral_grad {f : Space → ℝ} (hf : ContDiff ℝ 1 f) :
    f = (fun x => ∫ t in (0 : ℝ)..1, ⟪∇ f (t • x), basis.repr x⟫_ℝ ∂(volume)
      + f 0)

declarations.name: Space.grad_norm_sq
declarations.statement:
lemma grad_norm_sq (x : Space d) :
    ∇ (fun x => ‖x‖ ^ 2) x = (2 : ℝ) • basis.repr x

declarations.name: Space.grad_inner
declarations.doc: The gradient of the inner product is given by `2 • x`.
declarations.statement:
lemma grad_inner {d : ℕ} :
    ∇ (fun y : Space d => ⟪y, y⟫_ℝ) = fun z => (2 : ℝ) • basis.repr z

declarations.name: Space.grad_inner_left
declarations.statement:
lemma grad_inner_left {d : ℕ} (x : Space d) :
    ∇ (fun y : Space d => ⟪y, x⟫_ℝ) = fun _ => basis.repr x

declarations.name: Space.grad_inner_right
declarations.statement:
lemma grad_inner_right {d : ℕ} (x : Space d) :
    ∇ (fun y : Space d => ⟪x, y⟫_ℝ) = fun _ => basis.repr x

declarations.name: Space.integrable_isDistBounded_inner_grad_schwartzMap
Space.integrable_isDistBounded_inner_grad_schwartzMap_spherical
declarations.statement:
lemma integrable_isDistBounded_inner_grad_schwartzMap_spherical {d : ℕ}
    {f : Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)}
    (hf : IsDistBounded f) (η : 𝓢(Space d, ℝ)) :
    Integrable ((fun x => ⟪f x.1, Space.grad η x.1⟫_ℝ)
      ∘ (homeomorphUnitSphereProd (Space d)).symm)
      ((volume (α := Space d)).toSphere.prod
      (Measure.volumeIoiPow (Module.finrank ℝ (Space d) - 1)))

declarations.name: Space.contDiff_grad
declarations.statement:
lemma contDiff_grad {n} {f : Space → ℝ} (hf : ContDiff ℝ (n + 1) f) :
    ContDiff ℝ n (fun x => ∇ f x)

declarations.name: Space.distGrad
declarations.doc:
The gradient of a distribution `(Space d) →d[ℝ] ℝ` as a distribution
`(Space d) →d[ℝ] (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d))`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def distGrad {d} :
    ((Space d) →d[ℝ] ℝ) →ₗ[ℝ] (Space d) →d[ℝ] (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d))

declarations.name: Space.distGrad_inner_eq
declarations.statement:
lemma distGrad_inner_eq {d} (f : (Space d) →d[ℝ] ℝ) (η : 𝓢(Space d, ℝ))
    (y : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) : ⟪∇ᵈ f η, y⟫_ℝ = fderivD ℝ f η (basis.repr.symm y)

declarations.name: Space.distGrad_eq_of_inner
declarations.statement:
lemma distGrad_eq_of_inner {d} (f : (Space d) →d[ℝ] ℝ)
    (g : (Space d) →d[ℝ] EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d))
    (h : ∀ η y, fderivD ℝ f η y = ⟪g η, basis.repr y⟫_ℝ) :
    ∇ᵈ f = g

declarations.name: Space.distGrad_eq_sum_basis
declarations.statement:
lemma distGrad_eq_sum_basis {d} (f : (Space d) →d[ℝ] ℝ) (η : 𝓢(Space d, ℝ)) :
    ∇ᵈ f η =
      ∑ i, - f (SchwartzMap.evalCLM ℝ (Space d) ℝ (basis i) (fderivCLM ℝ (Space d) ℝ η)) •
      EuclideanSpace.single i 1

declarations.name: Space.distGrad_toFun_eq_distDeriv
declarations.statement:
lemma distGrad_toFun_eq_distDeriv {d} (f : (Space d) →d[ℝ] ℝ) :
    (∇ᵈ f).toFun = fun ε => WithLp.toLp 2 fun i => ∂ᵈ[i] f ε

declarations.name: Space.distGrad_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma distGrad_apply {d} (f : (Space d) →d[ℝ] ℝ) (ε : 𝓢(Space d, ℝ)) :
    (∇ᵈ f) ε = fun i => ∂ᵈ[i] f ε

declarations.name: Space.distGrad_const
declarations.statement:
lemma distGrad_const {d} (c : ℝ) :
    ∇ᵈ (Distribution.const ℝ (Space d) c) = 0

declarations.name: Space.gradSchwartz
declarations.doc: The gradient on Scwhwartz maps.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def gradSchwartz {d} : 𝓢(Space d, ℝ) →L[ℝ] 𝓢(Space d, EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d))

declarations.name: Space.gradSchwartz_apply_eq_grad
declarations.statement:
lemma gradSchwartz_apply_eq_grad {d} (η : 𝓢(Space d, ℝ)) (x : Space d) :
    gradSchwartz η x = ∇ η x

modules.title: Iterated derivatives on `Space d`
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

This module defines iterated coordinate derivatives on `Space d` indexed by multi-indices.

The implementation is intentionally modest. A multi-index is first expanded into a canonical list
of coordinate directions, and the iterated derivative is then defined by repeated application of
`Space.deriv` along that list.

## ii. Key results

- `Space.iteratedDeriv` : iterated coordinate derivatives on `Space d`.
- `∂^[I] f` : notation for the iterated derivative indexed by the multi-index `I`.
- `Space.iteratedDeriv_add`, `Space.iteratedDeriv_const_smul` :
  algebraic compatibility for smooth scalar-valued functions.
- `Space.iteratedDeriv_contDiff` : smooth scalar-valued functions remain smooth after
  iterated coordinate differentiation.
- `Space.tsupport_iteratedDeriv_subset` :
  the support of an iterated spatial derivative is contained in that of the original function.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Iterated derivatives on `Space d`
- B. Algebraic and regularity lemmas
- C. Support lemmas

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: Space.iteratedDeriv
declarations.doc: The iterated coordinate derivative on `Space d` indexed by a multi-index.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def iteratedDeriv [AddCommGroup M] [Module ℝ M] [TopologicalSpace M]
    (I : MultiIndex d) (f : Space d → M) : Space d → M

declarations.name: Space.iteratedDeriv_zero
declarations.statement:
lemma iteratedDeriv_zero [AddCommGroup M] [Module ℝ M] [TopologicalSpace M]
    (f : Space d → M) : ∂^[0] f = f

declarations.name: Space.iteratedDeriv_increment_zero
declarations.statement:
lemma iteratedDeriv_increment_zero [NeZero d] [AddCommGroup M] [Module ℝ M] [TopologicalSpace M]
    (I : MultiIndex d) (f : Space d → M) :
    ∂^[MultiIndex.increment I 0] f = ∂[0] (∂^[I] f)

declarations.name: Space.iteratedDeriv_single
declarations.statement:
lemma iteratedDeriv_single [AddCommGroup M] [Module ℝ M] [TopologicalSpace M]
    (i : Fin d) (f : Space d → M) :
    ∂^[MultiIndex.increment 0 i] f = ∂[i] f

declarations.name: Space.iteratedDeriv_add
Space.iteratedDeriv_const_smul
Space.iteratedDeriv_contDiff
declarations.doc: Iterated spatial derivatives preserve smoothness for scalar-valued functions.

declarations.name: Space.tsupport_deriv_subset
declarations.doc:
The topological support of a spatial derivative is contained in that of the original
function.
declarations.statement:
lemma tsupport_deriv_subset (i : Fin d) {f : Space d → ℝ} :
    tsupport (deriv i f) ⊆ tsupport f

declarations.name: Space.deriv_iteratedDeriv_commute
declarations.doc:
An extra spatial derivative commutes with iterated spatial derivatives for smooth
scalar-valued functions.

declarations.name: Space.tsupport_iteratedDeriv_subset
declarations.doc:
The topological support of an iterated spatial derivative is contained in that of the
original function.
declarations.statement:
lemma tsupport_iteratedDeriv_subset (I : MultiIndex d) {f : Space d → ℝ} :
    tsupport (∂^[I] f) ⊆ tsupport f

declarations.name: Space.iteratedDeriv_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport
declarations.doc:
An iterated spatial derivative vanishes outside the topological support of the original
function.

modules.title: The Laplacian operator on `Space d`
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

In this module we define the Laplacian operator on functions and vector-valued
functions defined on `Space d`.

## ii. Key results

- `laplacian` : The Laplacian operator on scalar functions on `Space d`.
- `laplacianVec` : The Laplacian operator on vector-valued functions on `Space d`.
- `distLaplacian` : The Laplacian operator on distributions on `Space d`.
- `laplacian_comp_linearIsometryEquiv` : The Laplacian commutes with composition by a linear
  isometry of `Space d`.
- `laplacianVec_comp_linearIsometryEquiv` : The vector Laplacian commutes with composition by a
  linear isometry of `Space d`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Laplacian on functions to ℝ
  - A.1. Relation between laplacian and divergence of gradient
- B. Laplacian on vector valued functions
- C. Laplacian of distributions
  - C.1. Laplacian of constant distributions
- D. Composition with a linear isometry

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.doc: The scalar `laplacian` operator.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def laplacian {d} (f : Space d → ℝ) : Space d → ℝ

declarations.name: Space.laplacian_eq_sum_snd_deriv
declarations.statement:
lemma laplacian_eq_sum_snd_deriv {d} (f : Space d → ℝ) :
    Δ f = fun x => ∑ i, ∂[i] (∂[i] f) x

declarations.name: Space.laplacianVec
declarations.doc: The vector `laplacianVec` operator.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def laplacianVec {d} (f : Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) :
    Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)

declarations.name: Space.distLaplacian
declarations.doc: The distributional `distLaplacian` operator.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def distLaplacian {d} :
    ((Space d) →d[ℝ] ℝ) →ₗ[ℝ] (Space d) →d[ℝ] ℝ

declarations.name: Space.distLaplacian_const
declarations.statement:
lemma distLaplacian_const {d : ℕ} (c : ℝ) :
    Δᵈ (Distribution.const ℝ (Space d) c) = 0

declarations.name: Space.laplacian_comp_linearIsometryEquiv
declarations.doc:
The Laplacian of `f ∘ R` at `x` is the Laplacian of `f` at `R x`, for a linear isometry `R`
of space.
declarations.statement:
lemma laplacian_comp_linearIsometryEquiv {d : ℕ} (f : Space d → ℝ) (R : Space d ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] Space d)
    (x : Space d) (hf : DifferentiableAt ℝ (fderiv ℝ f) (R x)) :
    Δ (fun y => f (R y)) x = Δ f (R x)

declarations.name: Space.laplacianVec_comp_linearIsometryEquiv
declarations.doc:
The vector Laplacian of `f ∘ R` at `x` is the vector Laplacian of `f` at `R x`, for a linear
isometry `R` of space.
declarations.statement:
lemma laplacianVec_comp_linearIsometryEquiv {d : ℕ} (f : Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d))
    (R : Space d ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] Space d) (x : Space d)
    (hf : ∀ i, DifferentiableAt ℝ (fderiv ℝ (fun y => f y i)) (R x)) :
    Δᵥ (fun y => f (R y)) x = Δᵥ f (R x)

modules.title: Matrix divergence on Space
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

In this module we define the matrix divergence operator on matrix-valued
functions from `Space d`.

For a field `T : Space d → Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ`, the matrix divergence is
the vector field whose `i`th component is

`∑ j, ∂[j] (fun x => T x i j) x`.

## ii. Key results

- `matrixDiv` : The divergence of a matrix-valued function on `Space d`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The matrix divergence on functions
  - A.1. Basic equalities
  - A.2. The matrix divergence on the zero function
  - A.3. The matrix divergence on a constant function
  - A.4. The matrix divergence distributes over addition
  - A.5. The matrix divergence distributes over scalar multiplication

## iv. References

* None.

### A.1. Basic equalities

### A.3. The matrix divergence on a constant function

declarations.name: Space.matrixDiv
declarations.doc:
The divergence of a matrix-valued spatial field.

For a field `T : Space d → Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ`, `matrixDiv T` is the
vector field whose `i`th component is

`∑ j, ∂[j] (fun x => T x i j) x`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def matrixDiv (d : ℕ) (T : Space d → Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ) :
    Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)

declarations.name: Space.matrixDiv_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma matrixDiv_apply (d : ℕ) (T : Space d → Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ)
    (x : Space d) (i : Fin d) :
    matrixDiv d T x i = ∑ j, ∂[j] (fun x => T x i j) x

declarations.name: Space.matrixDiv_zero
declarations.statement:
lemma matrixDiv_zero (d : ℕ) :
    matrixDiv d (0 : Space d → Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ) = 0

declarations.name: Space.matrixDiv_const
declarations.statement:
lemma matrixDiv_const (d : ℕ) (T : Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ) :
    matrixDiv d (fun _ : Space d => T) = 0

declarations.name: Space.matrixDiv_add
declarations.statement:
lemma matrixDiv_add (d : ℕ) (T1 T2 : Space d → Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ)
    (hT1 : Differentiable ℝ T1) (hT2 : Differentiable ℝ T2) :
    matrixDiv d (T1 + T2) = matrixDiv d T1 + matrixDiv d T2

declarations.name: Space.matrixDiv_smul
declarations.statement:
lemma matrixDiv_smul (d : ℕ) (T : Space d → Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ) (k : ℝ)
    (hT : Differentiable ℝ T) :
    matrixDiv d (k • T) = k • matrixDiv d T

modules.title: Multi-indices
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

This module defines the basic type of multi-indices used to index iterated partial derivatives.

A multi-index on `d` source coordinates is represented as a structure with an underlying function
`Fin d → ℕ`, together with the first basic operations needed later in the local Classical Field
Theory development.

## ii. Key results

- `Physlib.MultiIndex` : multi-indices on `d` coordinates.
- `MultiIndex.order` : the order `|I|` of a multi-index.
- `MultiIndex.increment` : increment a single coordinate of a multi-index.
- `MultiIndex.toList` : the canonical ordered list of directions encoded by a multi-index.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The basic type of multi-indices
  - A.1. Basic operations
  - A.2. Basic lemmas
  - A.3. Canonical ordered lists of directions

## iv. References

* None.

### A.1. Basic operations
### A.2. Basic lemmas
### A.3. Canonical ordered lists of directions

declarations.name: Physlib.MultiIndex
declarations.doc: A multi-index on `d` source coordinates.
declarations.statement:
structure MultiIndex (d : ℕ) where
  /-- The coordinates of the multi-index. -/
  toFun : Fin d → ℕ
deriving DecidableEq
instance : CoeFun (MultiIndex d) (fun _ => Fin d → ℕ)
instance : Zero (MultiIndex d)
instance : Add (MultiIndex d)

declarations.name: Physlib.MultiIndex.order
declarations.doc: The order `|I|` of a multi-index `I`, defined as the sum of its components.
declarations.statement: def order (I : MultiIndex d) : Nat

declarations.name: Physlib.MultiIndex.increment
declarations.doc: Increment the `i`-th coordinate of a multi-index by one.
declarations.statement: def increment (I : MultiIndex d) (i : Fin d) : MultiIndex d

declarations.name: Physlib.MultiIndex.ext
declarations.statement: lemma ext {I J : MultiIndex d} (h : ∀ i, I i = J i) : I = J

declarations.name: Physlib.MultiIndex.zero_apply
declarations.statement: lemma zero_apply (i : Fin d) : (0 : MultiIndex d) i = 0

declarations.name: Physlib.MultiIndex.add_apply
declarations.statement: lemma add_apply (I J : MultiIndex d) (i : Fin d) : (I + J) i = I i + J i

declarations.name: Physlib.MultiIndex.increment_apply_same
declarations.statement:
lemma increment_apply_same (I : MultiIndex d) (i : Fin d) :
    increment I i i = I i + 1

declarations.name: Physlib.MultiIndex.increment_apply_ne
declarations.statement:
lemma increment_apply_ne (I : MultiIndex d) {i j : Fin d} (h : j ≠ i) :
    increment I i j = I j

declarations.name: Physlib.MultiIndex.order_zero
declarations.statement: lemma order_zero : order (0 : MultiIndex d) = 0

declarations.name: Physlib.MultiIndex.order_add
declarations.statement: lemma order_add (I J : MultiIndex d) : order (I + J) = order I + order J

declarations.name: Physlib.MultiIndex.order_single
declarations.statement: lemma order_single (i : Fin d) : order (⟨Pi.single i 1⟩ : MultiIndex d) = 1

declarations.name: Physlib.MultiIndex.order_increment
declarations.statement:
lemma order_increment (I : MultiIndex d) (i : Fin d) :
    order (increment I i) = order I + 1

declarations.name: Physlib.MultiIndex.tail
declarations.doc: The tail of a multi-index on `d + 1` coordinates, dropping the `0`-th coordinate.
declarations.statement: def tail (I : MultiIndex d.succ) : MultiIndex d

declarations.name: Physlib.MultiIndex.toList
declarations.doc: The canonical ordered list of coordinate directions encoded by a multi-index.
declarations.statement: def toList : {d : ℕ} → MultiIndex d → List (Fin d)

declarations.name: Physlib.MultiIndex.tail_zero
declarations.statement: lemma tail_zero : tail (0 : MultiIndex d.succ) = 0

declarations.name: Physlib.MultiIndex.tail_increment_zero
declarations.statement: lemma tail_increment_zero (I : MultiIndex d.succ) : tail (increment I 0) = tail I

declarations.name: Physlib.MultiIndex.tail_increment_succ
declarations.statement:
lemma tail_increment_succ (I : MultiIndex d.succ) (i : Fin d) :
    tail (increment I i.succ) = increment (tail I) i

declarations.name: Physlib.MultiIndex.toList_zero
declarations.statement: lemma toList_zero : toList (0 : MultiIndex d) = []

declarations.name: Physlib.MultiIndex.length_toList
declarations.statement: lemma length_toList (I : MultiIndex d) : I.toList.length = I.order

declarations.name: Physlib.MultiIndex.toList_increment_zero
declarations.statement:
lemma toList_increment_zero (I : MultiIndex d.succ) :
    toList (increment I 0) = 0 :: toList I

declarations.name: Physlib.MultiIndex.toList_single
declarations.statement: lemma toList_single (i : Fin d) : toList (increment 0 i : MultiIndex d) = [i]

modules.title: The constant distribution on space
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

In this module we define the constant distribution from `Space d` to a module `M`.
That is the distribution which sends every Schwartz function to its
integral multiplied by a fixed element `m : M`.

We show that the derivatives of this constant distribution are zero.
## ii. Key results

- `distConst` : The constant distribution from `Space d` to a module `M`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The definition of the constant distribution
- B. Derivatives of the constant distribution

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.doc:
The constant distribution from `Space d` to a module `M` associated with

declarations.statement:
