modules.title: Distributions from functions on space
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

In this module we define distributions on space constructed from functions
`f : Space d → F` satisfying the condition `IsDistBounded f`.

This gives a convenient way to construct distributions from functions, without needing
to reference the underlying Schwartz maps.

## ii. Key results

- `distOfFunction f hf` : The distribution on space constructed from the function
  `f : Space d → F` satisfying the `IsDistBounded f` condition.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Definition of a distribution from a function
- B. Linarity properties of getting distributions from functions
- C. Properties related to inner products
- D. Derivatives
- E. Components

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. Definition of a distribution from a function
## B. Linarity properties of getting distributions from functions
## C. Properties related to inner products
## D. Derivatives
## E. Components

declarations.name: Space.distOfFunction
declarations.doc:
A distribution `Space d →d[ℝ] F` from a function
`f : Space d → F` which satisfies the `IsDistBounded f` condition.
declarations.statement:
def distOfFunction {d : ℕ} (f : Space d → F) (hf : IsDistBounded f) :
    (Space d) →d[ℝ] F

declarations.name: Space.distOfFunction_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma distOfFunction_apply {d : ℕ} (f : Space d → F)
    (hf : IsDistBounded f) (η : 𝓢(Space d, ℝ)) :
    distOfFunction f hf η = ∫ x, η x • f x

declarations.name: Space.distOfFunction_zero_eq_zero
declarations.statement:
lemma distOfFunction_zero_eq_zero {d : ℕ} :
    distOfFunction (fun _ : Space d => (0 : F)) (by fun_prop) = 0

declarations.name: Space.distOfFunction_smul
declarations.statement:
lemma distOfFunction_smul {d : ℕ} (f : Space d → F)
    (hf : IsDistBounded f) (c : ℝ) :
    distOfFunction (c • f) (by fun_prop) = c • distOfFunction f hf

declarations.name: Space.distOfFunction_smul_fun
declarations.statement:
lemma distOfFunction_smul_fun {d : ℕ} (f : Space d → F)
    (hf : IsDistBounded f) (c : ℝ) :
    distOfFunction (fun x => c • f x) (by fun_prop) = c • distOfFunction f hf

declarations.name: Space.distOfFunction_mul_fun
declarations.statement:
lemma distOfFunction_mul_fun {d : ℕ} (f : Space d → ℝ)
    (hf : IsDistBounded f) (c : ℝ) :
    distOfFunction (fun x => c * f x) (by fun_prop) = c • distOfFunction f hf

declarations.name: Space.distOfFunction_neg
declarations.statement:
lemma distOfFunction_neg {d : ℕ} (f : Space d → F)
    (hf : IsDistBounded (fun x => - f x)) :
    distOfFunction (fun x => - f x) hf = - distOfFunction f (by simpa using hf.neg)

declarations.name: Space.distOfFunction_inner
declarations.statement:
lemma distOfFunction_inner {d n : ℕ} (f : Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n))
    (hf : IsDistBounded f)
    (η : 𝓢(Space d, ℝ)) (y : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) :
    ⟪distOfFunction f hf η, y⟫_ℝ = ∫ x, η x * ⟪f x, y⟫_ℝ

declarations.name: Space.distDeriv_distOfFunction
declarations.doc:
The distributional spatial derivative of the distribution associated to a differentiable
function is the distribution associated to the corresponding pointwise spatial derivative.
declarations.statement:
lemma distDeriv_distOfFunction {d : ℕ} (μ : Fin d) (f : Space d → F)
    (hf : IsDistBounded f) (hf_deriv : IsDistBounded (∂[μ] f))
    (hf_diff : Differentiable ℝ f) :
    ∂ᵈ[μ] (distOfFunction f hf) = distOfFunction (∂[μ] f) hf_deriv

declarations.name: Space.distOfFunction_eculid_eval
declarations.statement:
lemma distOfFunction_eculid_eval {d n : ℕ} (f : Space d → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n))
    (hf : IsDistBounded f) (η : 𝓢(Space d, ℝ)) (i : Fin n) :
    distOfFunction f hf η i = distOfFunction (fun x => f x i) (hf.pi_comp i) η

declarations.name: Space.distOfFunction_vector_eval
declarations.statement:
lemma distOfFunction_vector_eval {d n : ℕ} (f : Space d → Lorentz.Vector n)
    (hf : IsDistBounded f) (η : 𝓢(Space d, ℝ)) (i : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin n) :
    distOfFunction f hf η i = distOfFunction (fun x => f x i) (hf.vector_component i) η

modules.title: The action of the Euclidean group on `Space`
modules.doc:
The Euclidean group `EuclideanGroup d = ℝᵈ ⋊ O(d)` (`Space/EuclideanGroup/Basic.lean`) is the group
of rigid motions of `d`-dimensional space. This file makes that geometric meaning literal: it
endows the affine space of points `Space d` (`Space/Basic.lean`) with a `MulAction` of
`EuclideanGroup d` **by isometries**, and specialises it to the rotations.

## Main results

* `EuclideanGroup.smul_vsub_smul` — displacements transform by the linear part alone.
* `EuclideanGroup.dist_smul` — the action preserves distance.
* `EuclideanGroup.rotation_smul_origin` / `rotation_smul_vsub_origin` — rotations fix the origin
  and act about it by their orthogonal part.
* `EuclideanGroup.chartEuclidean_smul` — agreement with the affine-isometry model
  (`AffineGroup.lean`); the rest of the file does not depend on it.

## Implementation notes

`Space d` is an affine space (`NormedAddTorsor`) with no canonical origin, so the action uses its
vector-space zero `(0 : Space d)` as the basepoint:

`g • p = (g.linear • (p -ᵥ (0 : Space d)) + g.translation) +ᵥ (0 : Space d)`.

The `Zero` instance and the chart `Space.chartEuclidean` are defined in `Space/Origin.lean`.

sections.text:
## Part 1: the action of the Euclidean group on `Space`

The motion `g = ⟨t, Q⟩` acts by `g • p = (Q • (p -ᵥ origin) + t) +ᵥ origin`. The `MulAction` laws
reduce to the semidirect-product group law of `EuclideanGroup`.

## Part 2: specialisation to rotations

The `RotationGroup d` action is the restriction of the Euclidean action along
`RotationGroup d ≤ EuclideanGroup d` (`RotationGroup` elements have zero translation). The lemmas
below record that rotations fix the origin, act by their orthogonal part about the origin, and
preserve distance.

## Part 3: relation to the affine isometry action (optional bridge)

`chartEuclidean_smul` records that, under the chart `Space.chartEuclidean` (`Space/Origin.lean`),
`p ↦ p -ᵥ origin`, the Part 1 action is the transport of `toAffineIsometryMulEquiv`
(`AffineGroup.lean`) from `EuclideanSpace` to `Space`. Nothing in Parts 1–2 depends on it.

declarations.doc:
The action of the Euclidean group on the affine space of points `Space d`: `g = ⟨t, Q⟩` rotates
`p` about the coordinate origin by the orthogonal part `Q` and then translates by `t`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable instance : MulAction (EuclideanGroup d) (Space d)

declarations.name: EuclideanGroup.smul_apply
declarations.doc: Coordinate formula for the action: `(g • p) i = (Q • (p -ᵥ origin)) i + t i`.
declarations.statement:
lemma smul_apply (g : EuclideanGroup d) (p : Space d) (i : Fin d) :
    (g • p) i = (g.linear • (p -ᵥ (0 : Space d))) i + g.translation i

declarations.name: EuclideanGroup.smul_vsub_smul
declarations.doc:
The displacement between two points transforms by the **orthogonal part alone**: the
translation cancels. This is the key lemma behind `dist_smul`.
declarations.statement:
lemma smul_vsub_smul (g : EuclideanGroup d) (p q : Space d) :
    (g • p) -ᵥ (g • q) = g.linear • (p -ᵥ q)

declarations.name: EuclideanGroup.dist_smul
declarations.doc: The Euclidean group acts on `Space d` **by isometries**: every rigid motion preserves distance.
declarations.statement:
lemma dist_smul (g : EuclideanGroup d) (p q : Space d) :
    dist (g • p) (g • q) = dist p q

declarations.name: EuclideanGroup.rotation_smul_eq
declarations.doc:
The rotation-group action is the restriction of the Euclidean action: `r • p = ↑r • p`
(definitional).
declarations.statement:
lemma rotation_smul_eq (r : RotationGroup d) (p : Space d) :
    r • p = (r : EuclideanGroup d) • p

declarations.name: EuclideanGroup.rotation_smul_origin
declarations.doc:
A rotation fixes the origin: its translation part vanishes
(`RotationGroup ≤ OriginStabilizer`), so `↑r • 0 = 0`. Stated in the `↑r` form (the simp normal
form of `r • _`, via `rotation_smul_eq`) so it is a well-formed `simp` lemma.
declarations.statement:
lemma rotation_smul_origin (r : RotationGroup d) :
    (r : EuclideanGroup d) • (0 : Space d) = (0 : Space d)

declarations.name: EuclideanGroup.rotation_smul_vsub_origin
declarations.doc:
A rotation acts on the displacement from the origin by its orthogonal part, for every `p`:
`(r • p) -ᵥ origin = Q • (p -ᵥ origin)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma rotation_smul_vsub_origin (r : RotationGroup d) (p : Space d) :
    (r • p) -ᵥ (0 : Space d) = (r : EuclideanGroup d).linear • (p -ᵥ (0 : Space d))

declarations.name: EuclideanGroup.rotation_dist_smul
declarations.doc: The rotation group acts on `Space d` **by isometries** (inherited from `dist_smul`).
declarations.statement:
lemma rotation_dist_smul (r : RotationGroup d) (p q : Space d) :
    dist (r • p) (r • q) = dist p q

declarations.name: EuclideanGroup.chartEuclidean_smul
declarations.doc:
Under the standard chart, the Euclidean action on `Space d` is the
transport of `toAffineIsometryMulEquiv` acting on `EuclideanSpace`:
`chart (g • p) = (toAffineIsometryMulEquiv g) (chart p)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma chartEuclidean_smul (g : EuclideanGroup d) (p : Space d) :
    Space.chartEuclidean d (g • p) = toAffineIsometryMulEquiv g (Space.chartEuclidean d p)

modules.title: The inclusion of the Euclidean group into the affine automorphism group
modules.doc:
This file has two parts.

**Part 1: the inclusion.** The abstract Euclidean group `EuclideanGroup n = ℝⁿ ⋊ O(n)` is
included into Mathlib's affine automorphism group as the composite of two monoid homomorphisms

`EuclideanGroup n →* AffineIsometryEquiv ℝ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) _ →* AffineEquiv ℝ _ _`.

* `EuclideanGroup.orthogonalToLinearIsometryEquiv` : an orthogonal matrix as a linear isometry
  equivalence of `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)`; the linear ingredient of the first leg.
* `EuclideanGroup.toAffineIsometryHom` : the first leg, `⟨t, Q⟩ ↦ (x ↦ Q x + t)`.
* `AffineIsometryEquiv.toAffineEquivHom` : the second leg, `AffineIsometryEquiv.toAffineEquiv`
  as a monoid homomorphism.
* `EuclideanGroup.toAffineEquiv` : the composite of the two legs; the result intended for use
  elsewhere.

**Part 2: strengthening the first leg to an isomorphism.** Every affine isometry of
`EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)` is `x ↦ Q x + t` for a unique orthogonal `Q` and translation `t`, so
the first leg is in fact a group isomorphism. We record it as
`EuclideanGroup.toAffineIsometryMulEquiv`, a `MulEquiv` whose fields are supplied as follows:

* `toFun`, `map_mul'` : reused from `EuclideanGroup.toAffineIsometryHom` in part 1;
* `invFun` : built from `EuclideanGroup.linearIsometryEquivToOrthogonal`, the inverse of the
  linear bridge `orthogonalToLinearIsometryEquiv`;
* `left_inv` : from the round trip `orthogonalToLinearIsometryEquiv_left_inv` together with the
  projection lemma `linearIsometryEquiv_constVAdd_mul`;
* `right_inv` : from the round trip `orthogonalToLinearIsometryEquiv_right_inv`.

Part 2 is self-contained; nothing in part 1 depends on it.

sections.text:
## Part 1: the inclusion

The chain is: `orthogonalToLinearIsometryEquiv` (linear ingredient) → `toAffineIsometryHom`
(first leg) → `AffineIsometryEquiv.toAffineEquivHom` (second leg) → `toAffineEquiv`
(the composite).

## Part 2: strengthening the first leg to an isomorphism

The first leg `toAffineIsometryHom` is in fact a group isomorphism: every affine isometry of
`EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)` is `x ↦ Q x + t` for a unique orthogonal `Q` and translation `t`. The
declarations below supply the remaining fields of the `MulEquiv` `toAffineIsometryMulEquiv`, in
field order: the `invFun` ingredient, the two lemmas proving `left_inv`, and the lemma proving
`right_inv`. Nothing in part 1 depends on this section.

declarations.name: EuclideanGroup.orthogonalToLinearIsometryEquiv
declarations.doc:
An orthogonal matrix viewed as a linear isometry equivalence of `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)`;
the linear ingredient of the first leg `toAffineIsometryHom`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def orthogonalToLinearIsometryEquiv
    (Q : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ) :
    EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)

declarations.name: EuclideanGroup.orthogonalToLinearIsometryEquiv_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma orthogonalToLinearIsometryEquiv_apply
    (Q : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ) (x : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) :
    orthogonalToLinearIsometryEquiv Q x = Q • x

declarations.name: EuclideanGroup.toAffineIsometryHom
declarations.doc:
The first leg of the inclusion: `⟨t, Q⟩ ↦ (x ↦ Q x + t)`, bundled as a monoid homomorphism
from the Euclidean group into the affine isometry group of `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def toAffineIsometryHom :
    EuclideanGroup n →*
      AffineIsometryEquiv ℝ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n))

declarations.name: EuclideanGroup.toAffineIsometryHom_apply
declarations.doc: Unfolds `toAffineIsometryHom` into its translation and linear factors.
declarations.statement:
lemma toAffineIsometryHom_apply (A : EuclideanGroup n) :
    toAffineIsometryHom A =
      AffineIsometryEquiv.constVAdd ℝ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) A.translation *
        (orthogonalToLinearIsometryEquiv A.linear).toAffineIsometryEquiv

declarations.name: AffineIsometryEquiv.toAffineEquivHom
declarations.doc:
The second leg of the inclusion: `AffineIsometryEquiv.toAffineEquiv` bundled as a monoid
homomorphism into the affine automorphism group.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def _root_.AffineIsometryEquiv.toAffineEquivHom :
    AffineIsometryEquiv ℝ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) →*
      AffineEquiv ℝ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n))

declarations.name: EuclideanGroup.toAffineEquiv
declarations.doc:
The inclusion of the Euclidean group into Mathlib's affine automorphism group: the composite
of the two legs `toAffineIsometryHom` and `AffineIsometryEquiv.toAffineEquivHom`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def toAffineEquiv :
    EuclideanGroup n →* AffineEquiv ℝ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n))

declarations.name: EuclideanGroup.linearIsometryEquivToOrthogonal
declarations.doc:
The `invFun` ingredient of `toAffineIsometryMulEquiv`: a linear isometry equivalence read back
as an orthogonal matrix, inverse to the linear bridge `orthogonalToLinearIsometryEquiv` (see the
round-trip `@[simp]` lemmas below).
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def linearIsometryEquivToOrthogonal
    (L : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) :
    Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ

declarations.name: EuclideanGroup.orthogonalToLinearIsometryEquiv_left_inv
declarations.doc:
`linearIsometryEquivToOrthogonal` is a left inverse of `orthogonalToLinearIsometryEquiv`.
Together with `linearIsometryEquiv_constVAdd_mul`, this proves `left_inv` of
`toAffineIsometryMulEquiv`.
declarations.statement:
lemma orthogonalToLinearIsometryEquiv_left_inv
    (Q : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ) :
    linearIsometryEquivToOrthogonal (orthogonalToLinearIsometryEquiv Q) = Q

declarations.name: EuclideanGroup.linearIsometryEquiv_constVAdd_mul
declarations.doc:
The affine map `x ↦ t +ᵥ L x`, projected to its linear isometry component, is `L`.
Together with `orthogonalToLinearIsometryEquiv_left_inv`, this proves `left_inv` of
`toAffineIsometryMulEquiv`.
declarations.statement:
lemma linearIsometryEquiv_constVAdd_mul
    (t : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n))
    (L : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) :
    ((AffineIsometryEquiv.constVAdd ℝ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) t *
        L.toAffineIsometryEquiv).linearIsometryEquiv) = L

declarations.name: EuclideanGroup.orthogonalToLinearIsometryEquiv_right_inv
declarations.doc:
`linearIsometryEquivToOrthogonal` is a right inverse of `orthogonalToLinearIsometryEquiv`;
this proves `right_inv` of `toAffineIsometryMulEquiv`.
declarations.statement:
lemma orthogonalToLinearIsometryEquiv_right_inv
    (L : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) :
    orthogonalToLinearIsometryEquiv (linearIsometryEquivToOrthogonal L) = L

declarations.name: EuclideanGroup.toAffineIsometryMulEquiv
declarations.doc:
`EuclideanGroup n ≃* AffineIsometryEquiv ℝ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) _`: the Euclidean group
is the full group of affine isometries of Euclidean space. This upgrades `toAffineIsometryHom` to
a group isomorphism with the same underlying map.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def toAffineIsometryMulEquiv :
    EuclideanGroup n ≃*
      AffineIsometryEquiv ℝ (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n))

declarations.name: EuclideanGroup.toAffineIsometryMulEquiv_apply
declarations.doc: `toAffineIsometryMulEquiv` agrees with `toAffineIsometryHom`.
declarations.statement:
lemma toAffineIsometryMulEquiv_apply (A : EuclideanGroup n) :
    toAffineIsometryMulEquiv A = toAffineIsometryHom A

modules.title: Euclidean group
modules.doc:
This file defines the Euclidean group as translations composed with orthogonal maps, together
with the special Euclidean group, translation subgroup, and rotation subgroups.

The affine group, together with the inclusion of the Euclidean group into it, is defined in
`Physlib.SpaceAndTime.Space.EuclideanGroup.AffineGroup`.

sections.text:
### `One`/`Mul` projection lemmas

These expose the semidirect-product formulas behind the `Group` instance so that `simp` can
reduce the translation/linear components of `1` and `A * B`.

declarations.name: EuclideanGroup
declarations.doc:
An n-dimensional `Euclidean group` is a group of
rotations, reflections, and translations.
declarations.statement:
structure EuclideanGroup (n : ℕ) where
  /-- The translation part of a Euclidean transformation. -/
  translation : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)
  /-- The orthogonal linear part of a Euclidean transformation. -/
  linear : Matrix.orthogonalGroup (Fin n) ℝ

declarations.doc:
Group structure on `E(n) = ℝ^n ⋊ O(n)`. The orthogonal component acts on translations by
the inherited matrix-vector action on `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)`, transported through `WithLp`
from the coordinate action `Q.val *ᵥ v.ofLp`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable instance : Group (EuclideanGroup n)

declarations.name: EuclideanGroup.one_translation
declarations.statement: lemma one_translation : (1 : EuclideanGroup n).translation = 0

declarations.name: EuclideanGroup.one_linear
declarations.statement: lemma one_linear : (1 : EuclideanGroup n).linear = 1

declarations.name: EuclideanGroup.mul_translation
declarations.statement:
lemma mul_translation (A B : EuclideanGroup n) :
    (A * B).translation = A.translation + A.linear • B.translation

declarations.name: EuclideanGroup.mul_linear
declarations.statement:
lemma mul_linear (A B : EuclideanGroup n) :
    (A * B).linear = A.linear * B.linear

declarations.name: EuclideanGroup.SpecialEuclideanGroup
declarations.doc: Special Euclidean Group is the subgroup with det(Q) = 1 where Q ∈ O(n)
declarations.statement: def SpecialEuclideanGroup (n : ℕ) : Subgroup (EuclideanGroup n)

declarations.name: EuclideanGroup.SpecialEuclideanGroup.incl
declarations.doc: The inclusion of the special Euclidean group into the Euclidean group.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def SpecialEuclideanGroup.incl (n : ℕ) :
    SpecialEuclideanGroup n →* EuclideanGroup n

declarations.name: EuclideanGroup.TranslationGroup
declarations.doc: Translation is the subgroup with Q = 1.
declarations.statement: def TranslationGroup (n : ℕ) : Subgroup (EuclideanGroup n)

declarations.name: EuclideanGroup.TranslationGroup.incl
declarations.doc: The inclusion of the translation subgroup into the Euclidean group.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def TranslationGroup.incl (n : ℕ) :
    TranslationGroup n →* EuclideanGroup n

declarations.name: EuclideanGroup.translationVector.incl
declarations.doc: MonoidHom including a translation vector into the Euclidean Group.
declarations.statement:
def translationVector.incl (n : ℕ) :
    Multiplicative (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) →* EuclideanGroup n

declarations.name: EuclideanGroup.translationVector.incl_range
declarations.doc: An API feature: the translation vector inclusion image is the `TranslationGroup` carrier.
declarations.statement:
lemma translationVector.incl_range :
    Set.range (@translationVector.incl n) = (TranslationGroup n : Set (EuclideanGroup n))

declarations.name: EuclideanGroup.translation_zero
declarations.doc: The translation by the zero vector is the identity of the Euclidean group.
declarations.statement:
lemma translation_zero : translationVector.incl n
    (Multiplicative.ofAdd (0 : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n))) = 1

declarations.name: EuclideanGroup.OriginStabilizer
declarations.doc:
The subgroup of `EuclideanGroup n` whose elements fix the origin
(translation = 0). This is the copy of `O(n)` sitting inside `E(n)`.
declarations.statement: def OriginStabilizer (n : ℕ) : Subgroup (EuclideanGroup n)

declarations.name: EuclideanGroup.RotationGroup
declarations.doc:
Rotation Group is the subgroup of E(n) consisting of rotations about the origin:
elements with `det = 1` (orientation-preserving) and `translation = 0` (origin-fixing).
declarations.statement: noncomputable def RotationGroup (n : ℕ) : Subgroup (EuclideanGroup n)

declarations.name: EuclideanGroup.RotationGroup.incl
declarations.doc: The inclusion of the rotation subgroup into the Euclidean group.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def RotationGroup.incl (n : ℕ) :
    RotationGroup n →* EuclideanGroup n

declarations.name: EuclideanGroup.RotationsAbout
declarations.doc:
The subgroup of rotation about a spatial point `p : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)` consists of
elements of the form T(p) * r * T(-p) with T(·) : translationVector.incl n (Multiplicative.ofAdd ·)
and r : RotationGroup where r is viewed as a rotation about the origin. Note T(-p) = T(p)⁻¹.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def RotationsAbout : Subgroup (EuclideanGroup n)

declarations.name: EuclideanGroup.RotationsAbout.incl
declarations.doc: The inclusion of rotations about `p` into the Euclidean group.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def RotationsAbout.incl : RotationsAbout p →* EuclideanGroup n

declarations.name: EuclideanGroup.RotationsAbout.toOrigin
declarations.doc: Conjugate a rotation about `p` back to a rotation about the origin.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def RotationsAbout.toOrigin :
    RotationsAbout p →* RotationGroup n

declarations.name: EuclideanGroup.RotationsAbout.fromOrigin
declarations.doc: Conjugate a rotation about the origin to a rotation about `p`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def RotationsAbout.fromOrigin :
    RotationGroup n →* RotationsAbout p

declarations.name: EuclideanGroup.RotationsAbout.fromOrigin_comp_toOrigin
declarations.doc:
`RotationsAbout.toOrigin p` followed by `RotationsAbout.fromOrigin p` is the identity; the
forward leg of the isomorphism `RotationsAboutEquiv`.
declarations.statement:
lemma RotationsAbout.fromOrigin_comp_toOrigin :
    (RotationsAbout.fromOrigin p).comp (RotationsAbout.toOrigin p) =
      MonoidHom.id (RotationsAbout p)

declarations.name: EuclideanGroup.RotationsAbout.toOrigin_comp_fromOrigin
declarations.doc:

modules.title: Integrals in Space
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

In this module we give general properties of integrals over `Space d`.
We focus here on the volume measure, which is the usual measure on `Space d`, i.e.
`dx dy dz`.

## ii. Key results

- `volume_eq_addHaar` : The volume measure on `Space d` is the same as the Haar measure
  associated with the basis of `Space d`.
- `integral_volume_eq_spherical` : The integral of a function over `Space d` with
  respect to the volume measure can be expressed as an integral over the unit sphere and
  the positive reals.
- `lintegral_volume_eq_spherical` : The lower Lebesgue integral of a function over `Space d`
  with respect to the volume measure can be expressed as a lower Lebesgue integral over the unit
  sphere and the positive reals.

sections.text: ## A. Properties of the volume measure
## B. Integrals over one-dimensional space
## C. Integrals over volume to spherical
## D. Lower Lebesgue integral over volume to spherical

    ∫ x, f x ∂volume = ∫ x, f (oneEquiv.symm x) ∂volume

declarations.name: Space.integral_volume_eq_spherical
declarations.statement:
lemma integral_volume_eq_spherical (d : ℕ) [NeZero d] (f : Space d → F)
    [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F] :
    ∫ x, f x ∂volume = ∫ x, f (x.2.1 • x.1.1) ∂(volume (α := Space d).toSphere.prod
        (Measure.volumeIoiPow (Module.finrank ℝ (Space d) - 1)))

declarations.name: Space.integrable_spherical_of_integrable
declarations.statement:
lemma integrable_spherical_of_integrable {d : ℕ} {F : Type*}
    [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F] {f : Space d → F}
    (hf : Integrable f volume) :
    Integrable
      (fun x : ↑(Metric.sphere (0 : Space d) 1) × Set.Ioi (0 : ℝ) =>
        f (x.2.1 • x.1.1))
      (volume (α := Space d).toSphere.prod
        (Measure.volumeIoiPow (Module.finrank ℝ (Space d) - 1)))

declarations.name: Space.integral_volume_eq_spherical_iterated
declarations.statement:
lemma integral_volume_eq_spherical_iterated {d : ℕ} [NeZero d] {F : Type*}
    [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F] (f : Space d → F)
    (hf : Integrable f volume) :
    ∫ x : Space d, f x =
      ∫ n : ↑(Metric.sphere (0 : Space d) 1),
        ∫ r : Set.Ioi (0 : ℝ), f (r.1 • n.1)
          ∂(Measure.volumeIoiPow (Module.finrank ℝ (Space d) - 1))
        ∂(volume (α := Space d).toSphere)

instance : SFinite (@Measure.comap ↑(Set.Ioi 0) ℝ Subtype.instMeasurableSpace
        Real.measureSpace.toMeasurableSpace Subtype.val volume)

declarations.name: Space.integral_volume_eq_spherical_integral
declarations.statement:
lemma integral_volume_eq_spherical_integral {d : ℕ} [NeZero d] {F : Type*}
    [NormedAddCommGroup F] [NormedSpace ℝ F] (f : Space d → F)
    (hf : Integrable f volume) :
    ∫ x : Space d, f x =
      ∫ n : ↑(Metric.sphere (0 : Space d) 1),
        ∫ r : Set.Ioi (0 : ℝ), (r.1 ^ (d - 1)) • f (r.1 • n.1)
          ∂(.comap Subtype.val volume)
        ∂(volume (α := Space d).toSphere)

declarations.name: Space.lintegral_volume_eq_spherical
declarations.statement:
lemma lintegral_volume_eq_spherical (d : ℕ) [NeZero d]
    (f : Space d → ENNReal) (hf : Measurable f) :
    ∫⁻ x, f x ∂volume = ∫⁻ x, f (x.2.1 • x.1.1) ∂(volume (α := Space d).toSphere.prod
        (Measure.volumeIoiPow (Module.finrank ℝ (Space d) - 1)))

declarations.name: Space.lintegral_volume_eq_spherical_mul
declarations.statement:
lemma lintegral_volume_eq_spherical_mul (d : ℕ) [NeZero d]
    (f : Space d → ENNReal) (hf : Measurable f) :
    ∫⁻ x, f x ∂volume = ∫⁻ x, f (x.2.1 • x.1.1) * .ofReal (x.2.1 ^ (d - 1))
      ∂(volume (α := Space d).toSphere.prod (Measure.volumeIoiPow 0))

modules.title: Integrability of norm powers on subsets of Space
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

This module contains results on the integrability of `x ↦ ‖x‖ᵖ` for real exponents `p` on subsets of
`Space d`.

The integrability of `x ↦ ‖x‖ᵖ` on `ball 0 b` and `(ball 0 b)ᶜ` follows from the 1d results
`integrableOn_Ioo_rpow_iff` and `integrableOn_Ioi_rpow_iff` after changing to spherical coordinates.

## ii. Key results

- `integrableOn_norm_rpow_iff_of_isBounded_nhds`: Necessary and sufficient condition for
    integrability on a set `s` which is a bounded neighborhood of the origin.
- `integrableOn_norm_rpow_of_isBounded_compl_nhds`: Integrability for all bounded sets `s`
    with `0 ∉ closure s`.
- `integrableOn_norm_rpow_of_compl_nhds`: A sufficient condition for integrability on `s`
    with `0 ∉ closure s`.
- `radial_norm_power_spherical_integral_eq_space_integral`: The spherical-coordinate integral
    identity for integer powers of the norm against a Schwartz map.

## iii. Table of contents

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: Space.radial_jacobian_zpow_mul_self
declarations.statement:
lemma radial_jacobian_zpow_mul_self
    {d p : ℕ} [NeZero d] {q : ℤ} (hp_int : (p : ℤ) = q + (d : ℤ))
    {r : ℝ} (hr : 0 < r) :
    r ^ (d - 1) * (r ^ q * r) = r ^ p

declarations.name: Space.radial_norm_power_spherical_integral_eq_space_integral
declarations.statement:
lemma radial_norm_power_spherical_integral_eq_space_integral
    {d p : ℕ} [NeZero d] {q : ℤ} (hp_int : (p : ℤ) = q + (d : ℤ))
    (hp_pos : 0 < p) (η : 𝓢(Space d, ℝ)) :
    ∫ x : Space d, η x * ‖x‖ ^ q =
      ∫ (n : ↑(Metric.sphere (0 : Space d) 1)),
        ∫ (r : Set.Ioi (0 : ℝ)),
          r.1 ^ (p - 1) * η (r.1 • n.1)
          ∂(.comap Subtype.val volume)
        ∂(volume (α := Space d).toSphere)

declarations.name: Space.integrableOn_norm_rpow_shell

modules.title: The radial angular measure on Space
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

The normal measure on `Space d` is `r^(d-1) dr dΩ` in spherical coordinates,
where `dΩ` is the angular measure on the unit sphere. The radial angular measure
is the measure `dr dΩ`, cancelling the radius contribution from the measure in spherical
coordinates.

This file is equivalent to `invPowMeasure`, which will slowly be deprecated.

## ii. Key results

- `radialAngularMeasure`: The radial angular measure on `Space d`.

## iii. Table of contents

- B. Integrals with respect to radialAngularMeasure
- C. The radialAngularMeasure on balls
- D. Integrability conditions
- E. HasTemperateGrowth of measures

modules.title: Functions on `Space d` which can be made into distributions
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

In this module, for functions `f : Space d → F`, we define the property `IsDistBounded f`.
Functions satisfying this property can be used to create distributions `Space d →d[ℝ] F`
by integrating them against Schwartz maps.

The condition `IsDistBounded f` essentially says that `f` is bounded by a finite sum of terms
of the form `c * ‖x + g‖ ^ p` for constants `c`, `g` and `- (d - 1) ≤ p ` where `d` is the dimension
of the space.

## ii. Key results

- `IsDistBounded` : The boundedness condition on functions `Space d → F` for them to
  form distributions.
- `IsDistBounded.integrable_space` : If `f` satisfies `IsDistBounded f`, then
  `fun x => η x • f x` is integrable for any Schwartz map `η : 𝓢(Space d, ℝ)`.
- `IsDistBounded.integrable_time_space` : If `f` satisfies `IsDistBounded f`, then
  `fun x => η x • f x.2` is integrable for any Schwartz map
  `η : 𝓢(Time × Space d, ℝ)`.
- `IsDistBounded.mono` : If `f₁` satisfies `IsDistBounded f₁` and
  `‖f₂ x‖ ≤ ‖f₁ x‖` for all `x`, then `f₂` satisfies `IsDistBounded f₂`.

## iii. Table of contents

modules.title: Units on Length
modules.doc:
A unit of length corresponds to a choice of translationally-invariant
metric on the space manifold (to be defined). Such a choice is (non-canonically) equivalent to a
choice of positive real number. We define the type `LengthUnit` to be equivalent to the
positive reals.

On `LengthUnit` there is an instance of division giving a real number, corresponding to the
ratio of the two scales of length unit.

To define specific length units, we first state the existence of a
a given length unit, and then construct all other length units from it. We choose to state the
existence of the length unit of meters, and construct all other length units from that.

## References

* The BIPM SI Brochure, for the meter, the speed of light, and SI prefixes.
  [ref: bipm_si_brochure_2019]
* NIST Handbook 44, Appendix C, for the international foot-based units and the international
  nautical mile. [ref: nist_hb44_2023]
* IAU 2012 Resolution B2, for the astronomical unit. [ref: iau_2012_resolution_b2]
* The IAU Style Manual recommendations, for the Julian year convention used in the light-year.
  [ref: iau_style_manual_units]
* IAU 2015 Resolution B2, for the exact parsec convention. [ref: iau_2015_resolution_b2]

sections.text:
## Specific choices of Length units

To define a specific length units.
We first define the notion of a meter to correspond to the length unit with underlying value
equal to `1`. This is really down to a choice in the isomorphism between the set of metrics
on the space manifold and the positive reals.
From this choice of meters, we can define other length units by scaling meters.

The references for the numerical definitions used below are:
* the BIPM SI Brochure for the meter, the speed of light, and SI prefixes:
  https://www.bipm.org/documents/d/guest/si-brochure-9-en-pdf [ref: bipm_si_brochure_2019]
* NIST Handbook 44, Appendix C, for the international foot-based units and
  the international nautical mile:
  https://doi.org/10.6028/NIST.HB.44-2023 [ref: nist_hb44_2023]
* IAU 2012 Resolution B2 for the astronomical unit:
  https://iauarchive.eso.org/static/resolutions/IAU2012_English.pdf [ref: iau_2012_resolution_b2]
* the IAU Style Manual recommendations for the Julian year convention used in
  the light-year:
  https://iauarchive.eso.org/publications/proceedings_rules/units/ [ref: iau_style_manual_units]
* IAU 2015 Resolution B2 for the exact parsec convention:
  https://iauarchive.eso.org/static/resolutions/IAU2015_English.pdf [ref: iau_2015_resolution_b2]
## Relations between length units

modules.title: The structure of a module on Space
modules.doc:
The scope of this module is to define on `Space d` the structure of a `Module`
(aka vector space), a `Norm` and an `InnerProductSpace`, and give properties of these structures.

These instances require certain non-canonical choices to be made, for example the choice
of a zero and for a basis, a choice of orientation.

## Instances in Lean

In Lean, an `instance` supplies a typeclass automatically. When a definition or
theorem needs a structure such as `AddCommGroup (Space d)`, `Module ℝ (Space d)`,
`NormedAddCommGroup (Space d)`, `InnerProductSpace ℝ (Space d)`, or
`MeasurableSpace (Space d)`, typeclass inference searches for the corresponding
instance and inserts it without the user passing it explicitly.

These instances make `Space d` usable with standard mathematical notation and
with the Mathlib API. For example, they allow expressions such as `p + q`,
`c • p`, `‖p‖`, `inner ℝ p q`, and measurable-set arguments involving the Borel
structure. They also make general theorems about modules, normed groups, inner
product spaces, and measurable spaces apply directly to `Space d`.

For `Space d`, these instances are intentional choices rather than inherited
facts: the type was defined as a structure instead of an abbreviation for
Euclidean space. In particular, the additive and module structures choose an
origin, while the norm, inner product, and Borel structure choose the standard
Euclidean coordinate geometry.

sections.text: ## A.1. Instance of an additive commutative monoid
## A.2. Instance of a module over `ℝ`
## A.3. Instance of an inner product space
## A.4. Instance of a measurable space
## The norm on `Space`

## Basis

A basis in Lean is typically represented by `Module.Basis ι R M`: an indexed
family of vectors in an `R`-module `M` such that every element of `M` has a
unique finite linear expansion in those vectors. The index type `ι` names the
basis vectors, and the map `basis.repr` gives the coordinate representation of a
vector with respect to that basis.

For inner product spaces, Lean also has `OrthonormalBasis ι R M`. This is a
basis whose vectors are orthonormal, packaged together with a linear isometric
equivalence between `M` and its coordinate space. It can be coerced to the
underlying `Module.Basis` using `basis.toBasis` when only the linear-algebraic
basis structure is needed.

The standard basis below is indexed by `Fin d`, so the basis vector `basis i`
is the unit vector in the `i`th coordinate direction of `Space d`.

modules.title: The norm on space
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

The main content of this file is defining `Space.normPowerSeries`, a sequence of smooth
functions which are differentiable everywhere, and which tend to the norm in the limit as `n → ∞`.

We use properties of this sequence to prove various results about distributions involving norms.

## ii. Key results

- `normPowerSeries` : A sequence of functions which are differentiable everywhere, and in the limit
  as `n → ∞` tends to `‖x‖`.
- `normPowerSeries_differentiable` : Each `normPowerSeries n` is differentiable everywhere.
- `normPowerSeries_tendsto` : `normPowerSeries n` tends to the norm in the limit as `n → ∞`.
- `distGrad_distOfFunction_norm_zpow` : The gradient of the distribution defined by a power of the
  norm.
- `distGrad_distOfFunction_log_norm` : The gradient of the distribution defined by the logarithm
  of the norm.
- `distDiv_norm_zpow_smul_repr_self_eq_smul` : The divergence of the distribution defined by
  `x ↦ ‖x‖ ^ q • x`.
- `distLaplacian_distOfFunction_norm_zpow` : The Laplacian of the distribution defined by a power
  of the norm.
- `distDiv_inv_pow_eq_dim` : The divergence of `x ↦ ‖x‖ ^ (-d) • x` equals `d * volume (ball 0 1)`
  times the Dirac delta at the origin.
- `distLaplacian_fundamentalSolution_norm_zpow` : The Laplacian of the power-form fundamental
  solution `‖x‖ ^ (2 - d)`, in every dimension (trivial at `d = 0, 2`).
- `distLaplacian_fundamentalSolution_log_norm` : The Laplacian of the two-dimensional logarithmic
  fundamental solution `Real.log ‖x‖`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The norm as a limit of smooth functions
  - A.1. Differentiability of the smooth approximation of the norm
  - A.2. The limit of the smooth approximation of the norm
  - A.3. The derivative of the smooth approximation of the norm
  - A.4. Limits of the derivative of the smooth approximation
  - A.5. The smooth approximation is AEStronglyMeasurable
  - A.6. Bounds on the smooth approximation of the norm
  - A.7. The `IsDistBounded` property of the smooth approximation of the norm
  - A.8. Differentiability of functions
  - A.9. Derivatives of functions
  - A.10. Gradients of distributions based on powers
    - A.10.1. The limits of gradients of distributions based on powers
  - A.11. Gradients of distributions based on logs
    - A.11.1. The limits of gradients of distributions based on logs
- B. Distributions involving norms
  - B.1. The gradient of distributions based on powers
  - B.2. The gradient of distributions based on logs
  - B.3. Divergence of radial norm-power distributions
  - B.4. The Laplacian of distributions based on powers
  - B.5. Divergence equal dirac delta
  - B.6. The Laplacian of the fundamental solution

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: Space.normPowerSeries
declarations.doc:
A sequence of functions which are differentiable everywhere, and in the limit
as `n → ∞` tends to `‖x‖`.
declarations.statement: def normPowerSeries {d} : ℕ → Space d → ℝ

declarations.name: Space.normPowerSeries_eq
declarations.statement:
lemma normPowerSeries_eq (n : ℕ) :
    normPowerSeries (d := d) n = fun x => √(‖x‖ ^ 2 + 1/(n + 1))

declarations.name: Space.normPowerSeries_eq_rpow
declarations.statement:

declarations.statement:

declarations.name: Space.deriv_normPowerSeries_tendsto
declarations.doc: The coordinate derivatives of `normPowerSeries` converge pointwise, including at zero.
declarations.statement:

    Filter.Tendsto (fun n => ∂[i] (normPowerSeries n) x) Filter.atTop (𝓝 (x i * (‖x‖)⁻¹))

declarations.name: Space.fderiv_normPowerSeries_tendsto
declarations.doc:
For every fixed direction, the derivatives of `normPowerSeries` converge pointwise,
including at zero.
declarations.statement:
lemma fderiv_normPowerSeries_tendsto {d} (x y : Space d) :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun n => fderiv ℝ (fun (x : Space d) => normPowerSeries n x) x y)
      Filter.atTop (𝓝 (⟪y, x⟫_ℝ * (‖x‖)⁻¹))

declarations.name: Space.differentiable_log_normPowerSeries
declarations.statement:
lemma differentiable_log_normPowerSeries {d : ℕ} {n : ℕ} :
    Differentiable ℝ (fun x : Space d => Real.log (normPowerSeries n x))

declarations.name: Space.deriv_normPowerSeries_zpow
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_normPowerSeries_zpow {d : ℕ} {n : ℕ} (m : ℤ) (x : Space d) (i : Fin d) :
    ∂[i] (fun x : Space d => (normPowerSeries n x) ^ m) x =
      m * x i * (normPowerSeries n x) ^ (m - 2)

declarations.name: Space.fderiv_normPowerSeries_zpow
declarations.statement:
lemma fderiv_normPowerSeries_zpow {d : ℕ} {n : ℕ} (m : ℤ) (x y : Space d) :
    fderiv ℝ (fun x : Space d => (normPowerSeries n x) ^ m) x y =
      m * ⟪y, x⟫_ℝ * (normPowerSeries n x) ^ (m - 2)

declarations.name: Space.deriv_log_normPowerSeries
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_log_normPowerSeries {d : ℕ} {n : ℕ} (x : Space d) (i : Fin d) :
    ∂[i] (fun x : Space d => Real.log (normPowerSeries n x)) x =
      x i * (normPowerSeries n x) ^ (-2 : ℤ)

declarations.name: Space.fderiv_log_normPowerSeries
declarations.statement:
lemma fderiv_log_normPowerSeries {d : ℕ} {n : ℕ} (x y : Space d) :
    fderiv ℝ (fun x : Space d => Real.log (normPowerSeries n x)) x y =
      ⟪y, x⟫_ℝ * (normPowerSeries n x) ^ (-2 : ℤ)

declarations.name: Space.gradient_dist_normPowerSeries_zpow
declarations.statement:
lemma gradient_dist_normPowerSeries_zpow {d : ℕ} {n : ℕ} (m : ℤ) :
    ∇ᵈ (distOfFunction (fun x : Space d => (normPowerSeries n x) ^ m) (by fun_prop)) =
    distOfFunction (fun x : Space d => (m * (normPowerSeries n x) ^ (m - 2)) • basis.repr x)
    (by fun_prop)

declarations.name: Space.gradient_dist_normPowerSeries_zpow_tendsTo_distGrad_norm
declarations.statement:
lemma gradient_dist_normPowerSeries_zpow_tendsTo_distGrad_norm {d : ℕ} [NeZero d] (m : ℤ)
    (hm : - (d - 1 : ℕ) ≤ m) (η : 𝓢(Space d, ℝ))
    (y : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun n =>
    ⟪(∇ᵈ (distOfFunction
    (fun x : Space d => (normPowerSeries n x) ^ m) (by fun_prop))) η, y⟫_ℝ)
    Filter.atTop
    (𝓝 (⟪∇ᵈ (distOfFunction (fun x : Space d => ‖x‖ ^ m)
    (IsDistBounded.pow m hm)) η, y⟫_ℝ))

declarations.name: Space.gradient_dist_normPowerSeries_zpow_tendsTo
declarations.statement:
lemma gradient_dist_normPowerSeries_zpow_tendsTo {d : ℕ} [NeZero d] (m : ℤ)
    (hm : - (d - 1 : ℕ) + 1 ≤ m)
    (η : 𝓢(Space d, ℝ)) (y : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun n =>
    ⟪(∇ᵈ (distOfFunction (fun x : Space d => (normPowerSeries n x) ^ m)
    (by fun_prop))) η, y⟫_ℝ)
    Filter.atTop
    (𝓝 (⟪distOfFunction (fun x : Space d => (m * ‖x‖ ^ (m - 2)) • basis.repr x) (by
    simp [← smul_smul]
    refine IsDistBounded.const_fun_smul ?_ ↑m
    apply IsDistBounded.zpow_smul_repr_self
    omega) η, y⟫_ℝ))

declarations.name: Space.gradient_dist_normPowerSeries_log
declarations.statement:
lemma gradient_dist_normPowerSeries_log {d : ℕ} {n : ℕ} :
    ∇ᵈ (distOfFunction (fun x : Space d => Real.log (normPowerSeries n x)) (by fun_prop)) =
    distOfFunction (fun x : Space d => ((normPowerSeries n x) ^ (- 2 : ℤ)) • basis.repr x)
    (by fun_prop)

declarations.name: Space.gradient_dist_normPowerSeries_log_tendsTo_distGrad_norm
declarations.statement:
lemma gradient_dist_normPowerSeries_log_tendsTo_distGrad_norm {d : ℕ} (hd : 2 ≤ d)
    (η : 𝓢(Space d, ℝ)) (y : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun n =>
    ⟪(∇ᵈ (distOfFunction
    (fun x : Space d => Real.log (normPowerSeries n x)) (by fun_prop))) η, y⟫_ℝ)
    Filter.atTop
    (𝓝 (⟪∇ᵈ (distOfFunction (fun x : Space d => Real.log ‖x‖)
    (IsDistBounded.log_norm)) η, y⟫_ℝ))

declarations.name: Space.gradient_dist_normPowerSeries_log_tendsTo
declarations.statement:
lemma gradient_dist_normPowerSeries_log_tendsTo {d : ℕ} (hd : 2 ≤ d)
    (η : 𝓢(Space d, ℝ)) (y : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun n =>
    ⟪(∇ᵈ (distOfFunction (fun x : Space d => Real.log (normPowerSeries n x))
    (by fun_prop))) η, y⟫_ℝ)
    Filter.atTop
    (𝓝 (⟪distOfFunction (fun x : Space d => (‖x‖ ^ (- 2 : ℤ)) • basis.repr x) (by
    refine (IsDistBounded.zpow_smul_repr_self _ ?_)
    omega) η, y⟫_ℝ))

declarations.name: Space.distGrad_distOfFunction_norm_zpow
declarations.statement:
lemma distGrad_distOfFunction_norm_zpow {d : ℕ} [NeZero d]
    (m : ℤ) (hm : - (d - 1 : ℕ) + 1 ≤ m) :
    ∇ᵈ (distOfFunction (fun x : Space d => ‖x‖ ^ m)
      (IsDistBounded.pow m (by omega)))
    = distOfFunction (fun x : Space d => (m * ‖x‖ ^ (m - 2)) • basis.repr x) (by
      simp [← smul_smul]
      refine IsDistBounded.const_fun_smul ?_ ↑m
      apply IsDistBounded.zpow_smul_repr_self
      omega)

declarations.name: Space.distGrad_distOfFunction_log_norm
declarations.statement:
lemma distGrad_distOfFunction_log_norm {d : ℕ} (hd : 2 ≤ d := by omega) :
    ∇ᵈ (distOfFunction (fun x : Space d => Real.log ‖x‖)
      (IsDistBounded.log_norm))
    = distOfFunction (fun x : Space d => (‖x‖ ^ (- 2 : ℤ)) • basis.repr x) (by
      refine (IsDistBounded.zpow_smul_repr_self _ ?_)
      omega)

declarations.name: Space.distDiv_norm_zpow_smul_repr_self_eq_smul
declarations.statement:
lemma distDiv_norm_zpow_smul_repr_self_eq_smul
    {d : ℕ} [NeZero d] (q : ℤ) (hq : 0 < q + (d : ℤ)) :
    ∇ᵈ ⬝ (distOfFunction (fun x : Space d => ‖x‖ ^ q • basis.repr x)
      (IsDistBounded.zpow_smul_repr_self q (by omega))) =
      (((q + d : ℤ) : ℝ) •
        distOfFunction (fun x : Space d => ‖x‖ ^ q)
          (IsDistBounded.pow q (by omega)))

declarations.name: Space.distLaplacian_distOfFunction_norm_zpow
declarations.statement:
lemma distLaplacian_distOfFunction_norm_zpow {d : ℕ} [NeZero d] (m : ℤ)
    (hdiv : 0 < m - 2 + (d : ℤ)) :
    Δᵈ (distOfFunction (fun x : Space d => ‖x‖ ^ m)
      (IsDistBounded.pow m (by omega))) =
      (((m : ℝ) * (((m - 2 + d : ℤ) : ℝ))) •
        distOfFunction (fun x : Space d => ‖x‖ ^ (m - 2))
          (IsDistBounded.pow (m - 2) (by omega)))

declarations.name: Space.distDiv_inv_pow_eq_dim
declarations.doc:
The distributional divergence of the radial field `x ↦ ‖x‖ ^ (-d) • x` (i.e. `x / ‖x‖ ^ d`)
equals `d * volume (Metric.ball 0 1)` — the surface area of the unit sphere `S^{d-1}` — times the
Dirac delta at the origin. This is the Gauss-law identity underlying the fundamental solution of
the Laplacian: away from `0` the field is divergence-free, and all of its flux concentrates at the
origin.
declarations.statement:
lemma distDiv_inv_pow_eq_dim {d : ℕ} [NeZero d] :
    ∇ᵈ ⬝ (distOfFunction (fun x : Space d => ‖x‖ ^ (- d : ℤ) • basis.repr x)
      (IsDistBounded.zpow_smul_repr_self (- d : ℤ) (by omega))) =
      (d * (volume (α := Space d)).real (Metric.ball 0 1)) • diracDelta ℝ 0

declarations.name: Space.distLaplacian_fundamentalSolution_norm_zpow
declarations.doc:
The distributional Laplacian of `‖x‖ ^ (2 - d)` is `(2 - d) * d * volume (Metric.ball 0 1)`
times the Dirac delta at the origin. For `d ≥ 3` this `‖x‖ ^ (2 - d)` is the (singular)
fundamental solution of the Laplacian, and for `d = 1` it is `‖x‖`. When `d = 2` the exponent
vanishes, so the identity collapses to the trivial `Δᵈ 1 = 0`; the genuine two-dimensional
fundamental solution is the logarithm, proved in `distLaplacian_fundamentalSolution_log_norm`.
The statement also holds vacuously for `d = 0`, where the space is trivial.
declarations.statement:
lemma distLaplacian_fundamentalSolution_norm_zpow {d : ℕ} :
    Δᵈ (distOfFunction (fun x : Space d => ‖x‖ ^ (- ((d : ℤ) - 2)))
      (IsDistBounded.pow _ (by omega))) =
      ((- ((d : ℝ) - 2)) * d *
        (volume (α := Space d)).real (Metric.ball 0 1)) • diracDelta ℝ 0

declarations.name: Space.distLaplacian_fundamentalSolution_log_norm
declarations.doc:
In dimension two the fundamental solution of the Laplacian is the logarithm: the
distributional Laplacian of `Real.log ‖x‖` is `2 * volume (Metric.ball 0 1)` times the Dirac
delta at the origin.
declarations.statement:
lemma distLaplacian_fundamentalSolution_log_norm :
    Δᵈ (distOfFunction (fun x : Space 2 => Real.log ‖x‖) IsDistBounded.log_norm) =
      (2 * (volume (α := Space 2)).real (Metric.ball 0 1)) • diracDelta ℝ 0

modules.title: Iterated Laplacians of norm distributions
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

This file proves the distributional identity corresponding to the classical odd-dimensional
formula that, in dimension `2 * m + 1`, applying the Laplacian `m + 1` times to the norm
gives a nonzero constant multiple of the Dirac delta at the origin.

## ii. Key results

- `iterated_distLaplacian_norm_zpow_odd_eq_smul_diracDelta` : The `(m + 1)`-fold
  Laplacian of the norm in dimension `2 * m + 1` is a nonzero multiple of the Dirac delta.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The odd-dimensional iterated Laplacian of the norm

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. The odd-dimensional iterated Laplacian of the norm

declarations.name: Space.oddNormIteratedLaplacianCoeff
declarations.doc: The scalar factor in the odd-dimensional iterated Laplacian of the norm.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def oddNormIteratedLaplacianCoeff (m : ℕ) : ℝ

declarations.name: Space.oddNormIteratedLaplacianCoeff_ne_zero
declarations.doc: The scalar factor in the odd-dimensional iterated Laplacian of the norm is nonzero.
declarations.statement:
lemma oddNormIteratedLaplacianCoeff_ne_zero (m : ℕ) :
    oddNormIteratedLaplacianCoeff m ≠ 0

declarations.name: Space.iterated_distLaplacian_norm_zpow_odd_eq_smul_diracDelta
declarations.doc:
In dimension `2 * m + 1`, the `(m + 1)`-fold distributional Laplacian of the
distribution induced by the norm is a nonzero multiple of the Dirac delta at the origin.
declarations.statement:
lemma iterated_distLaplacian_norm_zpow_odd_eq_smul_diracDelta (m : ℕ) :
    ((distLaplacian (d := 2 * m + 1))^[m + 1])
      (distOfFunction (fun x : Space (2 * m + 1) => ‖x‖ ^ (1 : ℤ))
        (IsDistBounded.pow 1 (by omega))) =
      oddNormIteratedLaplacianCoeff m • diracDelta ℝ 0

modules.title: Regularized powers of the norm on space
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

This file contains basic API for regularized powers of the norm on `Space d`, namely
`x ↦ (‖x‖ ^ 2 + ε ^ 2) ^ (s / 2)`.

## ii. Key results

- `normRegularizedPow` : The regularized norm power `x ↦ (‖x‖ ^ 2 + ε ^ 2) ^ (s / 2)`.
- `normRegularizedPow_pos` : Positivity for nonzero regularization parameter.
- `normRegularizedPow_hasTemperateGrowth` : Temperate growth of regularized norm powers.
- `normRegularizedPow_measurable` : Measurability of regularized norm powers.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Regularized powers of the norm

## iv. References

* None.

declarations.name: Space.normRegularizedPow

declarations.name: Space.normRegularizedPow_eq
declarations.statement:
lemma normRegularizedPow_eq (d : ℕ) (ε s : ℝ) :

declarations.name: Space.norm_sq_add_unit_sq_pos

declarations.statement: lemma norm_sq_add_unit_sq_pos {d : ℕ} (ε : ℝˣ) (x : Space d) : 0 < ‖x‖ ^ 2 + ε ^ 2

declarations.name: Space.normRegularizedPow_pos
declarations.doc: The regularized norm power is positive for nonzero regularization parameter.
declarations.statement:
lemma normRegularizedPow_pos (d : ℕ) (ε : ℝˣ) (s : ℝ) (x : Space d) :

modules.title: The origin of `Space` and the Euclidean chart
modules.doc:
The choice of origin for `Space d` is its vector-space zero `(0 : Space d)`. This file provides
that `Zero` instance and the standard chart, isolated so they can be shared by the full module
structure (`Space/Module.lean`) and the Euclidean action (`Space/EuclideanGroup/Action.lean`)
without those depending on each other.

* `(0 : Space d)` — the coordinate origin, the point all of whose coordinates vanish.
* `Space.chartEuclidean` — the standard affine isometry `Space d ≃ᵃⁱ[ℝ] EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)`,
  `p ↦ p -ᵥ 0`, identifying a point with its coordinate vector relative to the origin.

declarations.statement: instance {d} : Zero (Space d)

declarations.name: Space.zero_val
declarations.statement: lemma zero_val {d : ℕ} : (0 : Space d).val = fun _ => 0

declarations.name: Space.zero_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma zero_apply {d : ℕ} (i : Fin d) :
    (0 : Space d) i = 0

declarations.name: Space.vectorToSpace
declarations.doc: A Euclidean vector, based at the chosen origin, viewed as a point of `Space d`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def vectorToSpace {d : ℕ} (v : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) : Space d

declarations.name: Space.vectorToSpace_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma vectorToSpace_apply {d : ℕ} (v : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) (i : Fin d) :
    vectorToSpace v i = v i

declarations.name: Space.vectorToSpace_vsub_zero
declarations.statement:
lemma vectorToSpace_vsub_zero {d : ℕ} (v : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) :
    vectorToSpace v -ᵥ (0 : Space d) = v

declarations.name: Space.chartEuclidean
declarations.doc:
The standard chart `Space d ≃ᵃⁱ[ℝ] EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)`, `p ↦ p -ᵥ 0`, identifying a point
with its coordinate vector relative to the origin (the vector-space zero `(0 : Space d)`).
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def chartEuclidean (d : ℕ) :
    Space d ≃ᵃⁱ[ℝ] EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)

declarations.name: Space.chartEuclidean_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma chartEuclidean_apply (d : ℕ) (p : Space d) :
    chartEuclidean d p = p -ᵥ (0 : Space d)

modules.title: Slices of space
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

In this module we will define the equivalence between `Space d.succ` and `ℝ × Space d` which
extracts the `i`th coordinate on `Space d.succ`.

## ii. Key results

  the `i`th coordinate.

## iii. Table of contents

  - A.2. Slice as a measurable embedding
  - A.3. The norm of the slice map
  - A.4. Derivative of the slice map
  - A.5. Basis in terms of slices

declarations.name: Space.slice
declarations.doc:
The linear equivalence between `Space d.succ` and `ℝ × Space d`
extracting the `i`th coordinate.
declarations.statement: def slice {d} (i : Fin d.succ) : Space d.succ ≃L[ℝ] ℝ × Space d

declarations.name: Space.slice_symm_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma slice_symm_apply {d : ℕ} (i : Fin d.succ) (r : ℝ) (x : Space d) :
    (slice i).symm (r, x) = fun j =>
      Fin.insertNthEquiv (fun _ => ℝ) i (r, x) j

declarations.name: Space.slice_symm_apply_self
declarations.statement:
lemma slice_symm_apply_self {d : ℕ} (i : Fin d.succ) (r : ℝ) (x : Space d) :
    (slice i).symm (r, x) i = r

declarations.name: Space.slice_symm_apply_succAbove
declarations.statement:
lemma slice_symm_apply_succAbove {d : ℕ} (i : Fin d.succ) (r : ℝ) (x : Space d) (j : Fin d) :
    (slice i).symm (r, x) (Fin.succAbove i j) = x j

declarations.name: Space.slice_symm_measurableEmbedding
declarations.statement:
lemma slice_symm_measurableEmbedding {d : ℕ} (i : Fin d.succ) :
    MeasurableEmbedding (slice i).symm

declarations.name: Space.norm_slice_symm_eq
declarations.statement:
lemma norm_slice_symm_eq {d : ℕ} (i : Fin d.succ) (r : ℝ) (x : Space d) :
    ‖(slice i).symm (r, x)‖ = √(‖r‖ ^ 2 + ‖x‖ ^ 2)

declarations.name: Space.abs_right_le_norm_slice_symm
declarations.statement:
lemma abs_right_le_norm_slice_symm {d : ℕ} (i : Fin d.succ) (r : ℝ) (x : Space d) :
    |r| ≤ ‖(slice i).symm (r, x)‖

declarations.name: Space.norm_left_le_norm_slice_symm
declarations.statement:
lemma norm_left_le_norm_slice_symm {d : ℕ} (i : Fin d.succ) (r : ℝ) (x : Space d) :
    ‖x‖ ≤ ‖(slice i).symm (r, x)‖

declarations.name: Space.fderiv_slice_symm
declarations.statement:
lemma fderiv_slice_symm {d : ℕ} (i : Fin d.succ) (p1 : ℝ × Space d) :
    fderiv ℝ (slice i).symm p1 = (slice i).symm

declarations.name: Space.fderiv_slice_symm_left_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma fderiv_slice_symm_left_apply {d : ℕ} (i : Fin d.succ) (x : Space d) (r1 r2 : ℝ) :
    (fderiv ℝ (fun r => (slice i).symm (r, x))) r1 r2 = (slice i).symm (r2, 0)

declarations.name: Space.fderiv_slice_symm_right_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma fderiv_slice_symm_right_apply {d : ℕ} (i : Fin d.succ) (r : ℝ)
    (x1 x2 : Space d) :
    (fderiv ℝ (fun x => (slice i).symm (r, x))) x1 x2 = (slice i).symm (0, x2)

declarations.name: Space.fderiv_fun_slice_symm_right_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma fderiv_fun_slice_symm_right_apply {d : ℕ} (i : Fin d.succ) (r : ℝ)
    (x1 x2 : Space d) (f : Space d.succ → F) (hf : DifferentiableAt ℝ f ((slice i).symm (r, x1))) :
    (fderiv ℝ (fun x => f ((slice i).symm (r, x)))) x1 x2 =
    fderiv ℝ f ((slice i).symm (r, x1)) ((slice i).symm (0, x2))

declarations.name: Space.fderiv_fun_slice_symm_left_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma fderiv_fun_slice_symm_left_apply {d : ℕ} (i : Fin d.succ) (r1 r2 : ℝ)
    (x : Space d) (f : Space d.succ → F) (hf : DifferentiableAt ℝ f ((slice i).symm (r1, x))) :
    (fderiv ℝ (fun r => f ((slice i).symm (r, x)))) r1 r2 =
    fderiv ℝ f ((slice i).symm (r1, x)) ((slice i).symm (r2, 0))

declarations.name: Space.basis_self_eq_slice
declarations.statement:
lemma basis_self_eq_slice {d : ℕ} (i : Fin d.succ) :
    basis i = (slice i).symm (1, 0)

declarations.name: Space.basis_succAbove_eq_slice
declarations.statement:
lemma basis_succAbove_eq_slice {d : ℕ} (i : Fin d.succ) (j : Fin d) :
    basis (Fin.succAbove i j) = (slice i).symm (0, basis j)

modules.title: Smooth real-valued functions on space
modules.doc:
`Space.cmap` bundles a smooth real-valued function on `Space d`, given as a plain function
together with a `ContDiff` proof, into the space of bundled smooth maps
`C^⊤⟮𝓘(ℝ, Space d), Space d; 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ), ℝ⟯`. Such bundled maps are, for instance, the test
functions on which the mass distribution of a rigid body acts.

declarations.name: Space.cmap
declarations.doc:
Bundle a smooth real-valued function on `Space d` as an element of the space of bundled
smooth maps. Keeping this as a named constructor ensures the resulting type head stays
`ContMDiffMap`, so the module/ring operations and `comp` resolve correctly.
declarations.statement:
def cmap {d : ℕ} (f : Space d → ℝ) (hf : ContDiff ℝ ⊤ f) :
    C^⊤⟮𝓘(ℝ, Space d), Space d; 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ), ℝ⟯

declarations.name: Space.cmap_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma cmap_apply {d : ℕ} (f : Space d → ℝ) (hf : ContDiff ℝ ⊤ f) (y : Space d) :
    cmap f hf y = f y

Translations for part of the Poincaré group.

declarations.name: Space.translateSchwartz
declarations.doc: The continuous linear map translating Schwartz maps.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def translateSchwartz {d : ℕ} (a : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) :
    𝓢(Space d, X) →L[ℝ] 𝓢(Space d, X)

declarations.name: Space.translateSchwartz_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma translateSchwartz_apply {d : ℕ} (a : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d))
    (η : 𝓢(Space d, X)) (x : Space d) :
    translateSchwartz a η x = η (x - basis.repr.symm a)

declarations.name: Space.translateSchwartz_coe_eq
declarations.statement:
lemma translateSchwartz_coe_eq {d : ℕ} (a : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d))
    (η : 𝓢(Space d, X)) :
    (translateSchwartz a η : Space d → X) = fun x => η (x - basis.repr.symm a)

declarations.name: Space.distTranslate
declarations.doc: The continuous linear map translating distributions.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def distTranslate {d : ℕ} (a : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) :
    ((Space d) →d[ℝ] X) →ₗ[ℝ] ((Space d) →d[ℝ] X)

declarations.name: Space.distTranslate_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma distTranslate_apply {d : ℕ} (a : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d))
    (T : (Space d) →d[ℝ] X) (η : 𝓢(Space d, ℝ)) :
    distTranslate a T η = T (translateSchwartz (-a) η)

declarations.name: Space.distTranslate_distGrad
declarations.statement:
lemma distTranslate_distGrad {d : ℕ} (a : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d))
    (T : (Space d) →d[ℝ] ℝ) :
    distGrad (distTranslate a T) = distTranslate a (distGrad T)

declarations.name: Space.distTranslate_ofFunction
declarations.statement:
lemma distTranslate_ofFunction {d : ℕ} (a : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d))
    (f : Space d → X) (hf : IsDistBounded f) :
    distTranslate a (distOfFunction f hf) =
    distOfFunction (fun x => f (x - basis.repr.symm a))
    (IsDistBounded.comp_add_right hf (- basis.repr.symm a))

declarations.name: Space.distDiv_distTranslate
declarations.statement:
lemma distDiv_distTranslate {d : ℕ} (a : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d))
    (T : (Space d) →d[ℝ] EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) :
    distDiv (distTranslate a T) = distTranslate a (distDiv T)

modules.title: Spacetime
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

In this file we define the type `SpaceTime d` which corresponds to `d+1` dimensional
spacetime. This is equipped with an instance of the action of a Lorentz group,
corresponding to Minkowski-spacetime.

It is defined through `Lorentz.Vector d`, and carries the tensorial instance,
allowing it to be used in tensorial expressions.

## ii. Key results

- `SpaceTime d` : The type corresponding to `d+1` dimensional spacetime.
- `space_equivariant` : Spatial projection intertwines the Lorentz and Euclidean actions
  of the same rotation about the coordinate origin.
- `toTimeAndSpace` : A continuous linear equivalence between `SpaceTime d`
  and `Time × Space d`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The definition of `SpaceTime d`
- C. Continuous linear map to coordinates
- D. Measures on `SpaceTime d`
  - D.1. Instance of a measurable space
  - D.2. Instance of a borel space
  - D.4. Instance of a measure space
  - D.5. Volume measure is positive on non-empty open sets
  - D.6. Volume measure is a finite measure on compact sets
  - D.7. Volume measure is an additive Haar measure
- B. Maps to and from `Space` and `Time`
  - B.1. Linear map to `Space d`
    - B.1.1. Explicit expansion of map to space
    - B.1.2. Equivariance of the to space under rotations
  - B.2. Linear map to `Time`
    - B.2.1. Explicit expansion of map to time in terms of coordinates
  - B.3. `toTimeAndSpace`: Continuous linear equivalence to `Time × Space d`
    - B.3.1. Derivative of `toTimeAndSpace`
    - B.3.2. Derivative of the inverse of `toTimeAndSpace`
    - B.3.3. `toTimeAndSpace` acting on spatial basis vectors
    - B.3.4. `toTimeAndSpace` acting on the temporal basis vectors
  - B.4. Time space basis
    - B.4.1. Elements of the basis
    - B.4.2. Equivalence adjusting time basis vector
    - B.4.3. Determinant of the equivalence
    - B.4.4. Time space basis expressed in terms of the Lorentz basis
    - B.4.5. The additive Haar measure associated to the time space basis
  - B.5. Integrals over `SpaceTime d`
    - B.5.1. Measure preserving property of `toTimeAndSpace.symm`
    - B.5.2. Integrals over `SpaceTime d` expressed as integrals over `Time` and `Space d`

## iv. References

* None.
