declarations.name: SpaceTime
declarations.doc:
`SpaceTime d` corresponds to `d+1` dimensional space-time.
This is equipped with an instance of the action of a Lorentz group,
corresponding to Minkowski-spacetime.
declarations.statement: abbrev SpaceTime (d : ℕ := 3)

declarations.name: SpaceTime.coord
declarations.doc:
For a given `μ : Fin (1 + d)` `coord μ p` is the coordinate of
`p` in the direction `μ`.

This is denoted `𝔁 μ p`, where `𝔁` is typed with `\MCx`.
declarations.statement: def coord {d : ℕ} (μ : Fin (1 + d)) : SpaceTime d →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ

declarations.name: SpaceTime.coord_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma coord_apply {d : ℕ} (μ : Fin (1 + d)) (y : SpaceTime d) :
    𝔁 μ y = y (finSumFinEquiv.symm μ)

declarations.name: SpaceTime.coordCLM
declarations.doc: The continuous linear map from a point in space time to one of its coordinates.
declarations.statement: def coordCLM (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d) : SpaceTime d →L[ℝ] ℝ
instance {d : ℕ} : MeasurableSpace (SpaceTime d)
instance {d : ℕ} : BorelSpace (SpaceTime d)
instance {d : ℕ} : MeasureSpace (SpaceTime d)
instance {d : ℕ} : (volume (α := SpaceTime d)).IsOpenPosMeasure
instance {d : ℕ} : IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts (volume (α := SpaceTime d))
instance {d : ℕ} : Measure.IsAddHaarMeasure (volume (α := SpaceTime d))

declarations.name: SpaceTime.space
declarations.doc: The space part of spacetime.
declarations.statement: def space {d : ℕ} : SpaceTime d →L[ℝ] Space d

declarations.name: SpaceTime.space_toCoord_symm
declarations.statement:
lemma space_toCoord_symm {d : ℕ} (f : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d → ℝ) :
    space f = fun i => f (Sum.inr i)

declarations.name: SpaceTime.space_equivariant
declarations.doc:
Spatial projection intertwines a rotation's Lorentz action on spacetime with its
Euclidean action on space, using the same special orthogonal matrix on both sides.
These are rotations about the coordinate origin; no boosts or translations are included.
declarations.statement:
lemma space_equivariant {d : ℕ}
    (R : Matrix.specialOrthogonalGroup (Fin d) ℝ) (x : SpaceTime d) :
    space ((LorentzGroup.ofSpecialOrthogonal R : LorentzGroup d) • x) =
      EuclideanGroup.ofRotation R • space x

declarations.name: SpaceTime.time
declarations.doc: The time part of spacetime.
declarations.statement: def time {d : ℕ} (c : SpeedOfLight := 1) : SpaceTime d →ₗ[ℝ] Time

declarations.name: SpaceTime.time_val_toCoord_symm
declarations.statement:
lemma time_val_toCoord_symm {d : ℕ} (c : SpeedOfLight) (f : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d → ℝ) :
    (time c f).val = f (Sum.inl 0) / c

declarations.name: SpaceTime.toTimeAndSpace
declarations.doc:
A continuous linear equivalence between `SpaceTime d` and
`Time × Space d`.
declarations.statement: def toTimeAndSpace {d : ℕ} (c : SpeedOfLight := 1) : SpaceTime d ≃L[ℝ] Time × Space d

declarations.name: SpaceTime.toTimeAndSpace_symm_apply_time_space
declarations.statement:
lemma toTimeAndSpace_symm_apply_time_space {d : ℕ} {c : SpeedOfLight} (x : SpaceTime d) :
    (toTimeAndSpace c).symm (x.time c, x.space) = x

declarations.name: SpaceTime.space_toTimeAndSpace_symm
declarations.statement:
lemma space_toTimeAndSpace_symm {d : ℕ} {c : SpeedOfLight} (t : Time) (s : Space d) :
    ((toTimeAndSpace c).symm (t, s)).space = s

declarations.name: SpaceTime.time_toTimeAndSpace_symm
declarations.statement:
lemma time_toTimeAndSpace_symm {d : ℕ} {c : SpeedOfLight} (t : Time) (s : Space d) :
    ((toTimeAndSpace c).symm (t, s)).time c = t

declarations.name: SpaceTime.toTimeAndSpace_symm_apply_inl
declarations.statement:
lemma toTimeAndSpace_symm_apply_inl {d : ℕ} {c : SpeedOfLight} (t : Time) (s : Space d) :
    (toTimeAndSpace c).symm (t, s) (Sum.inl 0) = c * t

declarations.name: SpaceTime.toTimeAndSpace_symm_apply_inr
declarations.statement:
lemma toTimeAndSpace_symm_apply_inr {d : ℕ} {c : SpeedOfLight} (t : Time) (x : Space d)
    (i : Fin d) :
    (toTimeAndSpace c).symm (t, x) (Sum.inr i) = x i

declarations.name: SpaceTime.toTimeAndSpace_fderiv
declarations.statement:
lemma toTimeAndSpace_fderiv {d : ℕ} {c : SpeedOfLight} (x : SpaceTime d) :
    fderiv ℝ (toTimeAndSpace c) x = (toTimeAndSpace c).toContinuousLinearMap

declarations.name: SpaceTime.toTimeAndSpace_symm_fderiv
declarations.statement:
lemma toTimeAndSpace_symm_fderiv {d : ℕ} {c : SpeedOfLight} (x : Time × Space d) :
    fderiv ℝ (toTimeAndSpace c).symm x = (toTimeAndSpace c).symm.toContinuousLinearMap

declarations.name: SpaceTime.toTimeAndSpace_basis_inr
declarations.statement:
lemma toTimeAndSpace_basis_inr {d : ℕ} {c : SpeedOfLight} (i : Fin d) :
    toTimeAndSpace c (Lorentz.Vector.basis (Sum.inr i))
    = (0, Space.basis i)

declarations.name: SpaceTime.toTimeAndSpace_basis_inl
declarations.statement:
lemma toTimeAndSpace_basis_inl {d : ℕ} {c : SpeedOfLight} :
    toTimeAndSpace (d := d) c (Lorentz.Vector.basis (Sum.inl 0)) = (⟨1/c.val⟩, 0)

declarations.name: SpaceTime.toTimeAndSpace_basis_inl'
declarations.statement:
lemma toTimeAndSpace_basis_inl' {d : ℕ} {c : SpeedOfLight} :
    toTimeAndSpace (d := d) c (Lorentz.Vector.basis (Sum.inl 0)) = (1/c.val) • (1, 0)

declarations.name: SpaceTime.timeSpaceBasis
declarations.doc:
The basis of `SpaceTime` where the first component is `(c, 0, 0, ...)` instead
of `(1, 0, 0, ....).`
declarations.statement:
def timeSpaceBasis {d : ℕ} (c : SpeedOfLight := 1) :
    Module.Basis (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d) ℝ (SpaceTime d)

declarations.name: SpaceTime.timeSpaceBasis_apply_inl
declarations.statement:
lemma timeSpaceBasis_apply_inl {d : ℕ} (c : SpeedOfLight) :
    timeSpaceBasis (d := d) c (Sum.inl 0) = c.val • Lorentz.Vector.basis (Sum.inl 0)

declarations.name: SpaceTime.timeSpaceBasis_apply_inr
declarations.statement:
lemma timeSpaceBasis_apply_inr {d : ℕ} (c : SpeedOfLight) (i : Fin d) :
    timeSpaceBasis (d := d) c (Sum.inr i) = Lorentz.Vector.basis (Sum.inr i)

declarations.name: SpaceTime.timeSpaceBasisEquiv
declarations.doc:
The equivalence on of `SpaceTime` taking `(1, 0, 0, ...)` to
of `(c, 0, 0, ....)` and keeping all other components the same.
declarations.statement:
def timeSpaceBasisEquiv {d : ℕ} (c : SpeedOfLight) :
    SpaceTime d ≃L[ℝ] SpaceTime d

declarations.name: SpaceTime.det_timeSpaceBasisEquiv
declarations.statement:
lemma det_timeSpaceBasisEquiv {d : ℕ} (c : SpeedOfLight) :
    (timeSpaceBasisEquiv (d := d) c).det = c.val

declarations.name: SpaceTime.timeSpaceBasis_eq_map_basis
declarations.statement:
lemma timeSpaceBasis_eq_map_basis {d : ℕ} (c : SpeedOfLight) :
    timeSpaceBasis (d := d) c =
    Module.Basis.map (Lorentz.Vector.basis (d := d)) (timeSpaceBasisEquiv c).toLinearEquiv

declarations.name: SpaceTime.timeSpaceBasis_addHaar
declarations.statement:
lemma timeSpaceBasis_addHaar {d : ℕ} (c : SpeedOfLight := 1) :
    (timeSpaceBasis (d := d) c).addHaar = (ENNReal.ofReal (c⁻¹)) • volume

declarations.name: SpaceTime.toTimeAndSpace_symm_measurePreserving
declarations.statement:
lemma toTimeAndSpace_symm_measurePreserving {d : ℕ} (c : SpeedOfLight) :
    MeasurePreserving (toTimeAndSpace c).symm (volume.prod (volume (α := Space d)))
    (ENNReal.ofReal c⁻¹ • volume)

declarations.name: SpaceTime.spaceTime_integral_eq_time_space_integral
declarations.statement:
lemma spaceTime_integral_eq_time_space_integral {M} [NormedAddCommGroup M]
    [NormedSpace ℝ M] {d : ℕ} (c : SpeedOfLight)
    (f : SpaceTime d → M) :
    ∫ x : SpaceTime d, f x ∂(volume) =
    c.val • ∫ tx : Time × Space d, f ((toTimeAndSpace c).symm tx) ∂(volume.prod volume)

declarations.name: SpaceTime.spaceTime_integrable_iff_space_time_integrable
declarations.statement:
lemma spaceTime_integrable_iff_space_time_integrable {M} [NormedAddCommGroup M]
    {d : ℕ} (c : SpeedOfLight)
    (f : SpaceTime d → M) :
    Integrable f volume ↔ Integrable (f ∘ ((toTimeAndSpace c).symm)) (volume.prod volume)

declarations.name: SpaceTime.spaceTime_integral_eq_time_integral_space_integral
declarations.statement:
lemma spaceTime_integral_eq_time_integral_space_integral {M} [NormedAddCommGroup M]
    [NormedSpace ℝ M] {d : ℕ} (c : SpeedOfLight)
    (f : SpaceTime d → M)
    (h : Integrable f volume) :
    ∫ x : SpaceTime d, f x =
    c.val • ∫ t : Time, ∫ x : Space d, f ((toTimeAndSpace c).symm (t, x))

declarations.name: SpaceTime.spaceTime_integral_eq_space_integral_time_integral
declarations.statement:
lemma spaceTime_integral_eq_space_integral_time_integral {M} [NormedAddCommGroup M]
    [NormedSpace ℝ M] {d : ℕ} (c : SpeedOfLight)
    (f : SpaceTime d → M)
    (h : Integrable f volume) :
    ∫ x : SpaceTime d, f x =
    c.val • ∫ x : Space d, ∫ t : Time, f ((toTimeAndSpace c).symm (t, x))

modules.title: Boosts of space time
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

In this module we consider boosts acting on points in space time,and recover simple
formulae for such applications.

Note that the material here currently assumes that the speed of light `c = 1`.

## ii. Key results

- `boost_x_smul` : The action of a boost in the x-direction on a point in space time.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The action of a boost in the x-direction

## iv. References

* https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lorentz_transformation. [ref: wiki_lorentz_transformation]

sections.text:
## A. The action of a boost in the x-direction

We show that boosting in the `x`-direction takes `(t, x, y, z)` to
`(γ (t - β x), γ (x - β t), y, z)`.

declarations.name: SpaceTime.boost_x_smul
declarations.statement:
lemma boost_x_smul (β : ℝ) (hβ : |β| < 1) (x : SpaceTime) :
    LorentzGroup.boost (d := 3) 0 β hβ • x =
      fun | Sum.inl 0 => γ β * (x (Sum.inl 0) - β * x (Sum.inr 0))
          | Sum.inr 0 => γ β * (x (Sum.inr 0) - β * x (Sum.inl 0))
          | Sum.inr 1=> x (Sum.inr 1)
          | Sum.inr 2=> x (Sum.inr 2)

declarations.name: SpaceTime.boost_zero_apply_time_space
declarations.statement:
lemma boost_zero_apply_time_space {d : ℕ} {β : ℝ} (hβ : |β| < 1) (c : SpeedOfLight)
    (t : Time) (x : Space d.succ) :
    ((boost (0 : Fin d.succ) β hβ)⁻¹ • (SpaceTime.toTimeAndSpace c).symm (t, x)) =
    (SpaceTime.toTimeAndSpace c).symm
    (γ β * (t.val + β /c * x 0),
    ⟨fun
      | (0 : Fin d.succ) => γ β * (x 0 + c * β * t.val)
      | ⟨Nat.succ n, ih⟩ => x ⟨Nat.succ n, ih⟩⟩)

modules.title: Derivatives on SpaceTime
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

In this module we define and prove basic lemmas about derivatives of functions and
distributions on `SpaceTime d`.

## ii. Key results

- `deriv` : The derivative of a function `SpaceTime d → M` along the `μ` coordinate.
- `manifoldDeriv` : The derivative of a function from `SpaceTime d` to a manifold along
  the `μ` coordinate.
- `contDiff_deriv` : If `f` is `C^{n+1}` then `∂_ μ f` is `C^n`.
- `differentiable_deriv` : If `f` is `C^2` then `∂_ μ f` is differentiable.
- `deriv_commute` : Derivatives on `SpaceTime d` commute (Clairaut's theorem).
- `deriv_sum_inr` : The derivative along a spatial coordinate in terms of the
  derivative on `Space d`.
- `deriv_sum_inl` : The derivative along the temporal coordinate in terms of the
  derivative on `Time`.
- `iteratedDeriv` : Iterated derivatives along a multiset of coordinates.
- `distDeriv` : The derivative of a distribution on `SpaceTime d` along the `μ` coordinate.
- `distDeriv_commute` : Derivatives of distributions on `SpaceTime d` commute.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Derivatives of functions on `SpaceTime d`
  - A.1. The definition of the derivative
  - A.2. Basic equality lemmas
  - A.3. Linearity of the derivative
  - A.4. Smoothness and differentiability of the derivative
  - A.5. Derivatives commute
  - A.6. The derivative of a function composed with a Lorentz transformation
  - A.7. Spacetime derivatives in terms of time and space derivatives
  - A.8. Iterated derivatives
- B. Derivatives of distributions
  - B.1. Commutation of derivatives of distributions
  - B.2. Lorentz group action on derivatives of distributions
- C. Derivatives of tensors
  - C.1. Derivatives of tensors for distributions

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. Derivatives of functions on `SpaceTime d`
### A.1. The definition of the derivative
### A.2. Basic equality lemmas
### A.3. Linearity of the derivative
### A.4. Smoothness and differentiability of the derivative
### A.5. Derivatives commute
### A.6. The derivative of a function composed with a Lorentz transformation
### A.7. Spacetime derivatives in terms of time and space derivatives

### A.8. Iterated derivatives

Derivatives along different directions commute for smooth functions, so an iterated derivative of
a smooth function depends only on how many times each direction occurs. We therefore index iterated
derivatives by a multiset `s` of directions and write `iteratedDeriv s f`. For an arbitrary function
the derivatives are taken in the order of the list `s.toList`, and the lemmas that reorder
directions assume that `f` is smooth.
## B. Derivatives of distributions
### B.1. Commutation of derivatives of distributions

### B.2. Lorentz group action on derivatives of distributions

We now show how the Lorentz group action on distributions interacts with derivatives.

## C. Derivatives of tensors

Given a function `f : SpaceTime d → M` where `M` is a tensor space, we can define the
derivative of `f` as a tensor. In particular this is `∂_μ f` viewed as a tensor in
`Lorentz.CoVector d ⊗[ℝ] M`.
### C.1. Derivatives of tensors for distributions

declarations.name: SpaceTime.deriv
declarations.doc: The derivative of a function `SpaceTime d → ℝ` along the `μ` coordinate.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def deriv {M : Type} [AddCommGroup M] [Module ℝ M] [TopologicalSpace M]
    {d : ℕ} (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d) (f : SpaceTime d → M) : SpaceTime d → M

declarations.name: SpaceTime.deriv_eq
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_eq {M : Type} [AddCommGroup M] [Module ℝ M] [TopologicalSpace M]
    {d : ℕ} (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d) (f : SpaceTime d → M) (y : SpaceTime d) :
    ∂_ μ f y =
    fderiv ℝ f y (Lorentz.Vector.basis μ)

declarations.name: SpaceTime.manifoldDeriv
declarations.doc:
The derivative of a function from `SpaceTime d` to a manifold along the `μ`
coordinate, as a tangent vector at the value of the function.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def manifoldDeriv {E H N : Type} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
    [TopologicalSpace H] (I : ModelWithCorners ℝ E H) [TopologicalSpace N]
    [ChartedSpace H N] {d : ℕ} (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d) (f : SpaceTime d → N) :
    (y : SpaceTime d) → TangentSpace I (f y)

declarations.name: SpaceTime.manifoldDeriv_eq
declarations.statement:
lemma manifoldDeriv_eq {E H N : Type} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
    [TopologicalSpace H] (I : ModelWithCorners ℝ E H) [TopologicalSpace N]
    [ChartedSpace H N] {d : ℕ} (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d) (f : SpaceTime d → N)
    (y : SpaceTime d) :
    manifoldDeriv I μ f y =
      mfderiv 𝓘(ℝ, SpaceTime d) I f y
        ((Lorentz.Vector.basis μ : SpaceTime d) : TangentSpace 𝓘(ℝ, SpaceTime d) y)

declarations.name: SpaceTime.deriv_eq_mfderiv
declarations.doc: The spacetime derivative is the manifold derivative for functions into normed spaces.
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_eq_mfderiv {M : Type} [NormedAddCommGroup M] [NormedSpace ℝ M]
    {d : ℕ} (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d) (f : SpaceTime d → M) (y : SpaceTime d) :
    deriv μ f y =
      mfderiv 𝓘(ℝ, SpaceTime d) 𝓘(ℝ, M) f y
        ((Lorentz.Vector.basis μ : SpaceTime d) : TangentSpace 𝓘(ℝ, SpaceTime d) y)

declarations.name: SpaceTime.deriv_eq_manifoldDeriv
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_eq_manifoldDeriv {M : Type} [NormedAddCommGroup M] [NormedSpace ℝ M]
    {d : ℕ} (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d) (f : SpaceTime d → M) (y : SpaceTime d) :
    deriv μ f y = manifoldDeriv 𝓘(ℝ, M) μ f y

declarations.name: SpaceTime.manifoldDeriv_const
declarations.statement:
lemma manifoldDeriv_const {E H N : Type} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
    [TopologicalSpace H] (I : ModelWithCorners ℝ E H) [TopologicalSpace N]
    [ChartedSpace H N] {d : ℕ} (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d) (n : N) (y : SpaceTime d) :
    manifoldDeriv I μ (fun _ : SpaceTime d => n) y = 0

declarations.name: SpaceTime.differentiable_vector
declarations.statement:
lemma differentiable_vector {d : ℕ} (f : SpaceTime d → Lorentz.Vector d) :
    (∀ ν, Differentiable ℝ (fun x => f x ν)) ↔ Differentiable ℝ f

declarations.name: SpaceTime.contDiff_vector
declarations.statement:
lemma contDiff_vector {d : ℕ} (f : SpaceTime d → Lorentz.Vector d) :
    (∀ ν, ContDiff ℝ n (fun x => f x ν)) ↔ ContDiff ℝ n f

declarations.name: SpaceTime.fderiv_vector
declarations.statement:
lemma fderiv_vector {d : ℕ} (f : SpaceTime d → Lorentz.Vector d)
    (hf : Differentiable ℝ f) (y dt : SpaceTime d) (ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d) :
    fderiv ℝ f y dt ν = fderiv ℝ (fun x => f x ν) y dt

declarations.name: SpaceTime.deriv_apply_eq
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_apply_eq {d : ℕ} (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d) (f : SpaceTime d → Lorentz.Vector d)
    (hf : Differentiable ℝ f)
    (y : SpaceTime d) :
    ∂_ μ f y ν = fderiv ℝ (fun x => f x ν) y (Lorentz.Vector.basis μ)

declarations.name: SpaceTime.deriv_coord
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_coord {d : ℕ} (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d) :
    ∂_ μ (fun x => x ν) = if μ = ν then 1 else 0

declarations.name: SpaceTime.deriv_zero
declarations.statement: lemma deriv_zero {d : ℕ} (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d) : SpaceTime.deriv μ (fun _ => (0 : ℝ)) = 0

declarations.name: SpaceTime.deriv_add
declarations.doc: Derivatives on spacetime distribute over addition.
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_add {M : Type} [NormedAddCommGroup M] [NormedSpace ℝ M] {d : ℕ}
    (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d) (f g : SpaceTime d → M) (hf : Differentiable ℝ f)
    (hg : Differentiable ℝ g) :
    ∂_ μ (f + g) = ∂_ μ f + ∂_ μ g

declarations.name: SpaceTime.deriv_const_smul
declarations.doc: Derivatives on spacetime commute with multiplication by a constant.
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_const_smul {M R : Type} [NormedAddCommGroup M] [NormedSpace ℝ M] [Semiring R]
    [Module R M] [SMulCommClass ℝ R M] [ContinuousConstSMul R M] {d : ℕ}
    (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d) (c : R) {f : SpaceTime d → M} (hf : Differentiable ℝ f) :
    ∂_ μ (c • f) = c • ∂_ μ f

declarations.name: SpaceTime.contDiff_deriv
declarations.doc: If `f` is `C^{n+1}` then `∂_ μ f` is `C^n`.

declarations.name: SpaceTime.differentiable_deriv
declarations.doc: If `f` is `C^2` then `∂_ μ f` is differentiable.

declarations.name: SpaceTime.deriv_commute
declarations.doc: Derivatives on spacetime commute with one another (Clairaut's theorem).

declarations.name: SpaceTime.foldl_deriv_perm
declarations.doc:
For a smooth function, iterated derivatives along a list of directions do not depend on the
order of the list.

declarations.name: SpaceTime.deriv_comp_lorentz_action
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_comp_lorentz_action {M : Type} [NormedAddCommGroup M] [NormedSpace ℝ M] {d : ℕ}
    (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d)
    (f : SpaceTime d → M) (hf : Differentiable ℝ f) (Λ : LorentzGroup d)
    (x : SpaceTime d) :
    ∂_ μ (fun x => f (Λ • x)) x = ∑ ν, Λ.1 ν μ • ∂_ ν f (Λ • x)

declarations.name: SpaceTime.deriv_equivariant
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_equivariant (f : SpaceTime d → M) (Λ : LorentzGroup d) (x : SpaceTime d)
    (hf : Differentiable ℝ f) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d) :
    ∂_ μ (fun x => Λ • f (Λ⁻¹ • x)) x =
    ∑ ν, Λ⁻¹.1 ν μ • Λ • ∂_ ν f (Λ⁻¹ • x)

declarations.name: SpaceTime.deriv_sum_inr
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_sum_inr {d : ℕ} {M : Type} [NormedAddCommGroup M] [NormedSpace ℝ M]
    (c : SpeedOfLight) (f : SpaceTime d → M)
    (hf : Differentiable ℝ f) (x : SpaceTime d) (i : Fin d) :
    ∂_ (Sum.inr i) f x
    = Space.deriv i (fun y => f ((toTimeAndSpace c).symm ((toTimeAndSpace c x).1, y)))
      (toTimeAndSpace c x).2

declarations.name: SpaceTime.deriv_sum_inl
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_sum_inl {d : ℕ} {M : Type} [NormedAddCommGroup M]
    [NormedSpace ℝ M] (c : SpeedOfLight) (f : SpaceTime d → M)
    (hf : Differentiable ℝ f) (x : SpaceTime d) :
    ∂_ (Sum.inl 0) f x
    = (1/(c : ℝ)) • Time.deriv (fun t => f ((toTimeAndSpace c).symm (t, (toTimeAndSpace c x).2)))
      (toTimeAndSpace c x).1

declarations.name: SpaceTime.iteratedDeriv
declarations.doc: The iterated derivative of `f`, differentiating once along each element of `s`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def iteratedDeriv {M : Type} [AddCommGroup M] [Module ℝ M] [TopologicalSpace M]
    {d : ℕ} (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d)) (f : SpaceTime d → M) : SpaceTime d → M

declarations.name: SpaceTime.iteratedDeriv_zero
SpaceTime.iteratedDeriv_singleton
declarations.statement:
lemma iteratedDeriv_singleton {M : Type} [AddCommGroup M] [Module ℝ M] [TopologicalSpace M]
    {d : ℕ} (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d) (f : SpaceTime d → M) :
    iteratedDeriv {μ} f = ∂_ μ f

declarations.name: SpaceTime.contDiff_iteratedDeriv
declarations.doc: Iterated derivatives of a smooth function are smooth.

declarations.name: SpaceTime.iteratedDeriv_cons
declarations.doc: An iterated derivative of a smooth function may begin with any of its directions.

declarations.name: SpaceTime.iteratedDeriv_add
declarations.doc: Iterated derivatives of smooth functions distribute over addition.
declarations.statement:
lemma iteratedDeriv_add {M : Type} [NormedAddCommGroup M] [NormedSpace ℝ M] {d : ℕ}
    (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d)) {f g : SpaceTime d → M} (hf : ContDiff ℝ ∞ f)
    (hg : ContDiff ℝ ∞ g) :
    iteratedDeriv s (f + g) = iteratedDeriv s f + iteratedDeriv s g

declarations.name: SpaceTime.iteratedDeriv_const_smul
declarations.doc: Iterated derivatives of smooth functions commute with multiplication by a constant.
declarations.statement:
lemma iteratedDeriv_const_smul {M R : Type} [NormedAddCommGroup M] [NormedSpace ℝ M] [Semiring R]
    [Module R M] [SMulCommClass ℝ R M] [ContinuousConstSMul R M] {d : ℕ}
    (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d)) (c : R) {f : SpaceTime d → M} (hf : ContDiff ℝ ∞ f) :
    iteratedDeriv s (c • f) = c • iteratedDeriv s f

declarations.name: SpaceTime.distDeriv
declarations.doc:
Given a distribution (function) `f : SpaceTime d →d[ℝ] M` the derivative
of `f` in direction `μ`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def distDeriv {M d} [NormedAddCommGroup M] [NormedSpace ℝ M]
    (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d) : ((SpaceTime d) →d[ℝ] M) →ₗ[ℝ] (SpaceTime d) →d[ℝ] M

declarations.name: SpaceTime.distDeriv_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma distDeriv_apply {M d} [NormedAddCommGroup M] [NormedSpace ℝ M]
    (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d) (f : (SpaceTime d) →d[ℝ] M) (ε : 𝓢(SpaceTime d, ℝ)) :
    distDeriv μ f ε = fderivD ℝ f ε (Lorentz.Vector.basis μ)

declarations.name: SpaceTime.distDeriv_apply'
declarations.statement:
lemma distDeriv_apply' {M d} [NormedAddCommGroup M] [NormedSpace ℝ M]
    (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d) (f : (SpaceTime d) →d[ℝ] M) (ε : 𝓢(SpaceTime d, ℝ)) :
    distDeriv μ f ε =
    - f ((SchwartzMap.evalCLM ℝ (SpaceTime d) ℝ (Lorentz.Vector.basis μ))
    ((fderivCLM ℝ (SpaceTime d) ℝ) ε))

declarations.name: SpaceTime.apply_fderiv_eq_distDeriv
declarations.statement:
lemma apply_fderiv_eq_distDeriv {M d} [NormedAddCommGroup M] [NormedSpace ℝ M]
    (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d) (f : (SpaceTime d) →d[ℝ] M) (ε : 𝓢(SpaceTime d, ℝ)) :
    f ((SchwartzMap.evalCLM ℝ (SpaceTime d) ℝ (Lorentz.Vector.basis μ))
    ((fderivCLM ℝ (SpaceTime d) ℝ) ε)) =
    - distDeriv μ f ε

declarations.name: SpaceTime.distDeriv_commute
declarations.statement:
lemma distDeriv_commute {M d} [NormedAddCommGroup M] [NormedSpace ℝ M]
    (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d) (f : (SpaceTime d) →d[ℝ] M) :
    distDeriv μ (distDeriv ν f) = distDeriv ν (distDeriv μ f)

declarations.name: SpaceTime.distDeriv_comp_lorentz_action
declarations.statement:
lemma distDeriv_comp_lorentz_action {μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin d} (Λ : LorentzGroup d)
    (f : (SpaceTime d) →d[ℝ] M) :
    distDeriv μ (Λ • f) = ∑ ν, Λ⁻¹.1 ν μ • (Λ • distDeriv ν f)

declarations.name: SpaceTime.tensorDeriv
declarations.doc: The derivative of a tensor, as a tensor.
declarations.statement:
def tensorDeriv (f : SpaceTime d → M) :
    SpaceTime d → Lorentz.CoVector d ⊗[ℝ] M

declarations.name: SpaceTime.tensorDeriv_equivariant
declarations.statement:
lemma tensorDeriv_equivariant (f : SpaceTime d → M) (Λ : LorentzGroup d) (x : SpaceTime d)
    (hf : Differentiable ℝ f) :
    tensorDeriv (fun x => Λ • f (Λ⁻¹ • x)) x =
    Λ • tensorDeriv f (Λ⁻¹ • x)

declarations.name: SpaceTime.tensorDeriv_toTensor_basis_repr
declarations.statement:
lemma tensorDeriv_toTensor_basis_repr
    {f : SpaceTime d → M}
    (hf : Differentiable ℝ f) (x : SpaceTime d)
    (b : Tensor.ComponentIdx (Fin.append ![realLorentzTensor.Color.down] c)) :
    (Tensor.basis _).repr (Tensorial.toTensor (tensorDeriv f x)) b =
    ∂_ (Lorentz.CoVector.indexEquiv (ComponentIdx.prod b).1)
      (fun x => (Tensor.basis _).repr (Tensorial.toTensor (f x))
        (ComponentIdx.prod b).2) x

declarations.name: SpaceTime.tensorDeriv_eq_sum_tensor_basis
declarations.doc: The expansion of `tensorDeriv` in terms of the tensor basis vector.
declarations.statement:
lemma tensorDeriv_eq_sum_tensor_basis
    {f : SpaceTime d → M} (hf : Differentiable ℝ f) (x : SpaceTime d) :
    tensorDeriv f x = ∑ b, ∂_ (CoVector.indexEquiv (ComponentIdx.prod b).1)
      (fun x => (Tensor.basis _).repr (toTensor (f x)) (ComponentIdx.prod b).2) x •
    toTensor.symm (Tensor.basis _ b)

declarations.name: SpaceTime.distTensorDeriv
declarations.doc: The derivative of a tensor, as a tensor for distributions.
declarations.statement:
def distTensorDeriv {M d} [NormedAddCommGroup M]
    [InnerProductSpace ℝ M] [FiniteDimensional ℝ M] :
    ((SpaceTime d) →d[ℝ] M) →ₗ[ℝ] ((SpaceTime d) →d[ℝ] Lorentz.CoVector d ⊗[ℝ] M)

declarations.name: SpaceTime.distTensorDeriv_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma distTensorDeriv_apply {M d} [NormedAddCommGroup M]
    [InnerProductSpace ℝ M] [FiniteDimensional ℝ M] (f : (SpaceTime d) →d[ℝ] M)
    (ε : 𝓢(SpaceTime d, ℝ)) :
    distTensorDeriv f ε = ∑ μ, (Lorentz.CoVector.basis μ) ⊗ₜ distDeriv μ f ε

declarations.name: SpaceTime.distTensorDeriv_equivariant
declarations.statement:
lemma distTensorDeriv_equivariant {M : Type} [NormedAddCommGroup M]
    [InnerProductSpace ℝ M] [FiniteDimensional ℝ M] [(realLorentzTensor d).Tensorial c M]
    (f : (SpaceTime d) →d[ℝ] M) (Λ : LorentzGroup d) :
    distTensorDeriv (Λ • f) = Λ • distTensorDeriv f

declarations.name: SpaceTime.distTensorDeriv_toTensor_basis_repr
declarations.statement:
lemma distTensorDeriv_toTensor_basis_repr {M : Type} [NormedAddCommGroup M]
    [InnerProductSpace ℝ M] [FiniteDimensional ℝ M] [(realLorentzTensor d).Tensorial c M]
    {f : (SpaceTime d) →d[ℝ] M}
    (ε : 𝓢(SpaceTime d, ℝ))
    (b : Tensor.ComponentIdx (Fin.append ![realLorentzTensor.Color.down] c)) :
    (Tensor.basis _).repr (Tensorial.toTensor (distTensorDeriv f ε)) b =
    (Tensor.basis _).repr (Tensorial.toTensor
    (distDeriv (Lorentz.CoVector.indexEquiv (ComponentIdx.prod b).1) f ε))
    (ComponentIdx.prod b).2

modules.title: The spacetime algebra
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

The spacetime algebra `SpaceTimeAlgebra` is the ring of formal power series with complex
coefficients in four variables, one for each spacetime direction. The value at the base point of
an iterated partial derivative of a series is the corresponding coefficient multiplied by a
factorial. Consequently, a series is determined by these derivative values, and every family of
values arises from exactly one series. Iterated derivatives of a product obey the all-orders
Leibniz rule.

## ii. Key results

- `SpaceTimeAlgebra` : formal power series in the spacetime directions.
- `SpaceTimeAlgebra.iteratedPDeriv` : iterated formal partial derivatives.
- `SpaceTimeAlgebra.constantCoeff_iteratedPDeriv` : derivative values are `s!` times coefficients.
- `SpaceTimeAlgebra.iteratedPDeriv_mul` : the all-orders Leibniz rule.
- `SpaceTimeAlgebra.ext_of_constantCoeff_iteratedPDeriv` : derivative values determine a series.
- `SpaceTimeAlgebra.ofDerivValues` : the series with given derivative values.
- `SpaceTimeAlgebra.ofDerivValues_constantCoeff_iteratedPDeriv` : Taylor's formula.
- `SpaceTimeAlgebra.derivValuesEquiv` : series and derivative values are linearly equivalent.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The spacetime algebra
- B. Iterated formal partial derivatives
  - B.1. Commutation of formal partial derivatives
  - B.2. Base-point values of iterated derivatives
  - B.3. The Leibniz rule
- C. Series with equal derivative values
- D. Series from derivative values
  - D.1. Series with prescribed derivative values
  - D.2. The linear equivalence

## iv. References

* P. Haukkanen, Formal power series in several variables, Notes on Number Theory and Discrete
  Mathematics 25 (2019) 44–57, Section 4, Definitions 4.1–4.2 and Theorem 4.1, p. 48.
  https://doi.org/10.7546/nntdm.2019.25.4.44-57 [ref: haukkanen_2019_formal_power_series]
* I. Kolář, P. W. Michor and J. Slovák, Natural Operations in Differential Geometry,
  Sections 12.5–12.6 and 12.18, for the interpretation of Taylor series as coordinate
  expressions of jets. https://www.mat.univie.ac.at/~michor/kmsbookh.pdf
  [ref: kolar_michor_slovak_1993]

sections.text:
## A. The spacetime algebra

The four spacetime directions are indexed by `Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3`, with `Sum.inl 0` the time direction
and `Sum.inr i` the three space directions. The spacetime algebra has one variable `x^μ` for each
direction `μ`.

These power series are formal, meaning that a series is an arbitrary family of complex
coefficients, one for each monomial, and no convergence condition is imposed.

The formal variables represent coordinate displacements from a fixed, implicit spacetime point, the
base point. The constant coefficient represents the field value at that point. In differential
geometry, the data of all derivatives of a smooth map at a point is called its infinite-order jet
at that point (a mathematical notion, unrelated to jets in collider physics). In fixed coordinates,
the infinite-order jet of a smooth complex-valued field at the base point is recorded by the
series of its Taylor coefficients, which is an element of the spacetime algebra.

## B. Iterated formal partial derivatives

### B.1. Commutation of formal partial derivatives

`pderiv μ` differentiates a series term by term with the power rule in `x^μ`, treating the other
variables as constants. Formal partial derivatives in different directions commute, so an iterated
derivative depends only on how many times each direction occurs. We therefore index iterated
derivatives by a multiset `s` of directions (an unordered list in which repetition is allowed) and
write `∂^s f` for `iteratedPDeriv s f`. For example, the multiset containing `μ` twice and `ν` once
gives `∂_μ ∂_μ ∂_ν f`.

### B.2. Base-point values of iterated derivatives

For a power series in one variable, the `n`-th derivative at `0` is `n!` times the coefficient of
`xⁿ`. This section proves the analogue in several variables, on which the rest of the file is
built. We write `(∂^s f)(0)` for the constant coefficient of `∂^s f`, which is its value at the base
point where every `x^μ` is zero, and call the family `s ↦ (∂^s f)(0)` the base-point derivative
values of `f`. A multiset `s` determines the monomial `x^s`, containing each `x^μ` as often as `μ`
occurs in `s`, and the number `s!`, the product of the factorials of these multiplicities. Applying
`∂^s` turns `x^s` into the constant `s!`, while every other monomial ends up either zero or without
a constant term, so `(∂^s f)(0)` is `s!` times the coefficient of `x^s` in `f`.

### B.3. The Leibniz rule

To apply `∂^s` to `f g`, each direction in `s` acts on either `f` or `g`, so `∂^s (f g)` is a sum
of `(∂^t₁ f) (∂^t₂ g)` over the splits `t₁ + t₂ = s` in `Multiset.antidiagonal s`. Each split
appears once for every assignment of the elements of `s` that produces it, so repeated directions
give multiplicities: `∂_μ² (f g) = (∂_μ² f) g + 2 (∂_μ f) (∂_μ g) + f (∂_μ² g)`. The same formula
holds for base-point derivative values, but not for the Taylor coefficients, which are divided by
`s!`.

## C. Series with equal derivative values

Since `s!` is nonzero, the coefficient of `x^s` in `f` is `(∂^s f)(0)` divided by `s!`. Two series
with the same base-point derivative values therefore have the same coefficients, and so are
equal. Similarly, a series whose first derivatives all vanish is the constant series given by its
base-point value.

## D. Series from derivative values

### D.1. Series with prescribed derivative values

A family `F` of complex numbers indexed by multisets defines the series `ofDerivValues F`, whose
coefficient of `x^s` is `F s` divided by `s!`. By B.2, its base-point derivative values are the
values of `F`. Applied to the base-point derivative values of a series `f`, this construction
returns `f`, which is Taylor's formula `f = Σ_s (∂^s f)(0) / s! · x^s` (Haukkanen, Theorem 4.1).

### D.2. The linear equivalence

The two constructions are mutually inverse and `ℂ`-linear, so together they form the linear
equivalence `derivValuesEquiv` between the spacetime algebra and `Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → ℂ`.

declarations.name: SpaceTimeAlgebra
declarations.doc: Formal power series in the four spacetime directions, with complex coefficients.
declarations.statement: abbrev SpaceTimeAlgebra : Type

declarations.name: SpaceTimeAlgebra.pderiv_comm
declarations.doc: Formal partial derivatives commute.
declarations.statement:
lemma pderiv_comm (μ ν : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (f : SpaceTimeAlgebra) :
    pderiv μ (pderiv ν f) = pderiv ν (pderiv μ f)

declarations.doc: Formal partial differentiation can be iterated over a multiset of directions.
declarations.statement: instance : RightCommutative (fun (f : SpaceTimeAlgebra) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) => pderiv μ f)

declarations.name: SpaceTimeAlgebra.iteratedPDeriv
declarations.doc:
The iterated formal partial derivative `∂^s f`, differentiating once along each element of
`s`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def iteratedPDeriv (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (f : SpaceTimeAlgebra) :
    SpaceTimeAlgebra

declarations.name: SpaceTimeAlgebra.iteratedPDeriv_zero
declarations.statement: lemma iteratedPDeriv_zero (f : SpaceTimeAlgebra) : iteratedPDeriv 0 f = f

declarations.name: SpaceTimeAlgebra.iteratedPDeriv_cons
declarations.statement:
lemma iteratedPDeriv_cons (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3))
    (f : SpaceTimeAlgebra) :
    iteratedPDeriv (μ ::ₘ s) f = iteratedPDeriv s (pderiv μ f)

declarations.name: SpaceTimeAlgebra.iteratedPDeriv_singleton
declarations.statement:
lemma iteratedPDeriv_singleton (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (f : SpaceTimeAlgebra) :
    iteratedPDeriv {μ} f = pderiv μ f

declarations.name: SpaceTimeAlgebra.iteratedPDeriv_add
declarations.statement:
lemma iteratedPDeriv_add (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (f g : SpaceTimeAlgebra) :
    iteratedPDeriv s (f + g) = iteratedPDeriv s f + iteratedPDeriv s g

declarations.name: SpaceTimeAlgebra.constantCoeff_iteratedPDeriv
declarations.doc: The base-point value of `∂^s f` is `s!` times the coefficient of `x^s` in `f`.
declarations.statement:
lemma constantCoeff_iteratedPDeriv (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (f : SpaceTimeAlgebra) :
    constantCoeff (iteratedPDeriv s f) =
      ((∏ ν, (s.count ν).factorial : ℕ) : ℂ) * coeff (Multiset.toFinsupp s) f

declarations.name: SpaceTimeAlgebra.iteratedPDeriv_mul
declarations.doc: The all-orders Leibniz rule for iterated formal partial derivatives.
declarations.statement:
lemma iteratedPDeriv_mul (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (f g : SpaceTimeAlgebra) :
    iteratedPDeriv s (f * g) =
      (s.antidiagonal.map fun p => iteratedPDeriv p.1 f * iteratedPDeriv p.2 g).sum

declarations.name: SpaceTimeAlgebra.constantCoeff_iteratedPDeriv_mul
declarations.doc: The Leibniz rule for the base-point derivative values of a product.
declarations.statement:
lemma constantCoeff_iteratedPDeriv_mul (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (f g : SpaceTimeAlgebra) :
    constantCoeff (iteratedPDeriv s (f * g)) =
      (s.antidiagonal.map fun p =>
        constantCoeff (iteratedPDeriv p.1 f) * constantCoeff (iteratedPDeriv p.2 g)).sum

declarations.name: SpaceTimeAlgebra.ext_of_constantCoeff_iteratedPDeriv
declarations.doc: Series whose iterated derivatives have the same base-point values are equal.

declarations.name: SpaceTimeAlgebra.eq_C_of_pderiv_eq_zero
declarations.doc: A series with vanishing first derivatives is constant.
declarations.statement:
lemma eq_C_of_pderiv_eq_zero {f : SpaceTimeAlgebra} (hf : ∀ μ, pderiv μ f = 0) :
    f = C (constantCoeff f)

declarations.name: SpaceTimeAlgebra.ofDerivValues
declarations.doc: The series whose base-point derivative values are `F`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def ofDerivValues (F : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → ℂ) : SpaceTimeAlgebra

declarations.name: SpaceTimeAlgebra.coeff_ofDerivValues
declarations.statement:
lemma coeff_ofDerivValues (F : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → ℂ) (m : (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) →₀ ℕ) :
    coeff m (ofDerivValues F) =
      ((∏ ν, (m ν).factorial : ℕ) : ℂ)⁻¹ * F (Finsupp.toMultiset m)

declarations.name: SpaceTimeAlgebra.constantCoeff_iteratedPDeriv_ofDerivValues
declarations.doc: The base-point derivative values of `ofDerivValues F` are `F`.
declarations.statement:
lemma constantCoeff_iteratedPDeriv_ofDerivValues (F : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → ℂ)
    (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    constantCoeff (iteratedPDeriv s (ofDerivValues F)) = F s

declarations.name: SpaceTimeAlgebra.ofDerivValues_constantCoeff_iteratedPDeriv
declarations.doc: A series is recovered from its base-point derivative values by `ofDerivValues`.
declarations.statement:
lemma ofDerivValues_constantCoeff_iteratedPDeriv (f : SpaceTimeAlgebra) :
    ofDerivValues (fun s => constantCoeff (iteratedPDeriv s f)) = f

declarations.name: SpaceTimeAlgebra.derivValuesEquiv
declarations.doc: The linear equivalence between series and their base-point derivative values.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def derivValuesEquiv : SpaceTimeAlgebra ≃ₗ[ℂ] (Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → ℂ)

declarations.name: SpaceTimeAlgebra.derivValuesEquiv_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma derivValuesEquiv_apply (f : SpaceTimeAlgebra) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    derivValuesEquiv f s = constantCoeff (iteratedPDeriv s f)

declarations.name: SpaceTimeAlgebra.derivValuesEquiv_symm_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma derivValuesEquiv_symm_apply (F : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) → ℂ) :
    derivValuesEquiv.symm F = ofDerivValues F

modules.title: Complex conjugation in the spacetime algebra
modules.doc:
The spacetime algebra is a star ring under complex conjugation of the Taylor coefficients.

## i. Overview

The star of a series in the spacetime algebra conjugates each of its complex coefficients and
fixes each coordinate variable `x^μ`. The Taylor coefficients of the complex conjugate of a smooth
field are the conjugates of its Taylor coefficients, so if `f` records a field at the base point
then `star f` records the conjugate field.

Conjugation is an involution that respects sums and products. It conjugates complex scalars, fixes
real scalars, and commutes with every iterated derivative `∂^s`.

## ii. Key results

- `SpaceTimeAlgebra.coeff_star` : the coefficients of `star f` are the conjugates of those of `f`.
- `SpaceTimeAlgebra.star_C` : conjugating a constant series conjugates the constant.
- `SpaceTimeAlgebra.star_X` : the coordinate variables are fixed by conjugation.
- `SpaceTimeAlgebra.pderiv_star` : conjugation commutes with formal partial derivatives.
- `SpaceTimeAlgebra.iteratedPDeriv_star` : conjugation commutes with iterated derivatives.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Coefficientwise conjugation
  - A.1. The star ring structure
  - A.2. Constants and coordinates
  - A.3. Real and complex scalars
- B. Formal partial derivatives

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text:
## A. Coefficientwise conjugation

The star is the coefficient map `map (starRingEnd ℂ)`. Since `SpaceTimeAlgebra` is an
abbreviation, these are instances on `MvPowerSeries (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) ℂ`.

### A.1. The star ring structure

Since the spacetime algebra is commutative, a ring homomorphism that is an involution makes it a
star ring.
### A.2. Constants and coordinates
### A.3. Real and complex scalars

## B. Formal partial derivatives

The coefficient of `x^n` in `pderiv μ f` is the coefficient of `x^(n + single μ 1)` in `f` times
the natural number `n μ + 1`, which conjugation fixes.

declarations.doc: The star of a series in the spacetime algebra conjugates each of its coefficients.
declarations.statement: instance : Star SpaceTimeAlgebra

declarations.name: SpaceTimeAlgebra.coeff_star
declarations.statement:
lemma coeff_star (n : (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) →₀ ℕ) (f : SpaceTimeAlgebra) :
    coeff n (star f) = star (coeff n f)

declarations.name: SpaceTimeAlgebra.constantCoeff_star
declarations.statement:
lemma constantCoeff_star (f : SpaceTimeAlgebra) :
    constantCoeff (star f) = star (constantCoeff f)

declarations.doc: The spacetime algebra is a star ring under coefficientwise conjugation.
declarations.statement: instance : StarRing SpaceTimeAlgebra

declarations.name: SpaceTimeAlgebra.star_C
declarations.statement: lemma star_C (a : ℂ) : star (C a : SpaceTimeAlgebra) = C (star a)

declarations.name: SpaceTimeAlgebra.star_X
declarations.statement: lemma star_X (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) : star (X μ : SpaceTimeAlgebra) = X μ

declarations.statement: instance : StarModule ℝ SpaceTimeAlgebra

declarations.name: SpaceTimeAlgebra.pderiv_star
declarations.doc: Conjugation commutes with formal partial derivatives.

lemma pderiv_star (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) (f : SpaceTimeAlgebra) :
    pderiv μ (star f) = star (pderiv μ f)

declarations.name: SpaceTimeAlgebra.iteratedPDeriv_star
declarations.doc: Conjugation commutes with iterated formal partial derivatives.

lemma iteratedPDeriv_star (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (f : SpaceTimeAlgebra) :
    iteratedPDeriv s (star f) = star (iteratedPDeriv s f)

modules.title: Taylor series of functions on spacetime
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

The Taylor series of a complex-valued function `f` on spacetime at a point `x₀` is the element of
the spacetime algebra whose base-point derivative values are the iterated derivatives of `f` at
`x₀`. For smooth `f` it is additive and `ℂ`-homogeneous in `f`, and it takes the derivative of `f`
along a direction to the formal partial derivative of the series along the same direction.

## ii. Key results

- `SpaceTimeAlgebra.taylorSeries` : the Taylor series of a function at a point.
- `SpaceTimeAlgebra.constantCoeff_iteratedPDeriv_taylorSeries` : derivative values of `f` at `x₀`.
- `SpaceTimeAlgebra.taylorSeries_deriv` : derivatives become formal partial derivatives.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The Taylor series of a function
- B. Taylor series of derivatives

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text:
## A. The Taylor series of a function

The iterated derivatives `iteratedDeriv s f` of a function are indexed by multisets of directions,
like the iterated formal partial derivatives of a series. The Taylor series of `f` at `x₀` is the
series `ofDerivValues` built from their values at `x₀`, so that its coefficient of `x^s` is
`(∂^s f)(x₀)` divided by `s!` and the base point of the spacetime algebra is identified with `x₀`.
For smooth functions, iterated derivatives distribute over sums and scalar multiples, and so does
the Taylor series.

## B. Taylor series of derivatives

Applying `∂^s` after `∂_μ` is the same as applying `∂^(μ ::ₘ s)`, both for smooth functions and
for series. Hence the Taylor series of `∂_μ f` and the formal partial derivative `pderiv μ` of the
Taylor series of `f` have the same base-point derivative values, namely `(∂^(μ ::ₘ s) f)(x₀)` at
each `s`. A series is determined by its base-point derivative values, so the two are equal.

declarations.name: SpaceTimeAlgebra.taylorSeries
declarations.doc: The Taylor series at `x₀` of a complex-valued function on spacetime.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def taylorSeries (x₀ : SpaceTime) (f : SpaceTime → ℂ) : SpaceTimeAlgebra

declarations.name: SpaceTimeAlgebra.coeff_taylorSeries
declarations.statement:
lemma coeff_taylorSeries (x₀ : SpaceTime) (f : SpaceTime → ℂ) (m : (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) →₀ ℕ) :
    coeff m (taylorSeries x₀ f) =
      ((∏ ν, (m ν).factorial : ℕ) : ℂ)⁻¹ * iteratedDeriv (Finsupp.toMultiset m) f x₀

declarations.name: SpaceTimeAlgebra.constantCoeff_iteratedPDeriv_taylorSeries
declarations.doc: The base-point derivative values of `taylorSeries x₀ f` are the derivatives of `f` at `x₀`.
declarations.statement:
lemma constantCoeff_iteratedPDeriv_taylorSeries (x₀ : SpaceTime) (f : SpaceTime → ℂ)
    (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    constantCoeff (iteratedPDeriv s (taylorSeries x₀ f)) = iteratedDeriv s f x₀

declarations.name: SpaceTimeAlgebra.taylorSeries_add
declarations.statement:
lemma taylorSeries_add (x₀ : SpaceTime) {f g : SpaceTime → ℂ} (hf : ContDiff ℝ ∞ f)
    (hg : ContDiff ℝ ∞ g) :
    taylorSeries x₀ (f + g) = taylorSeries x₀ f + taylorSeries x₀ g

modules.title: The action of spacetime series on derivative symbols
modules.doc:
The action of formal power series in spacetime coordinates on polynomials in derivatives.

## i. Overview

Multiplying a field component `φ` by a spacetime-dependent function `χ`, such as a matrix element
of a local gauge transformation, changes its derivatives by the product rule. At a point `x₀`,
`∂_μ (χ φ)(x₀) = χ(x₀) ∂_μ φ(x₀) + (∂_μ χ)(x₀) φ(x₀)`, so a first derivative of `χ φ` is a
combination of derivatives of `φ`, and the same holds for any derivative symbol `P`. The symbol
`seriesAction χ P` records this combination, applying `P` after multiplying by `χ`. We define the
action on monomials by the product rule, and it respects sums and products of series, so
`seriesAction` is a ring homomorphism from the spacetime algebra to the linear endomorphisms of
the derivative algebra.

In the statements `χ` is a series, the Taylor series of the function at `x₀`, and we use the
notation of `SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ` throughout.

## ii. Key results

- `SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ.seriesAction` : the action of series on derivative symbols.
- `SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ.pairing_seriesAction` : the action applies `P` after multiplying by `χ`.
- `SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ.seriesAction_basis_singleton` : the product rule for first-order
  symbols.
- `SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ.seriesAction_mul_basis_singleton` : the action commutes with
  multiplication by `∂_μ` up to the action of `pderiv μ χ`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The action of a series
  - A.1. The action on monomials
  - A.2. Multiplication before differentiation
- B. Low-order symbols and derivatives
  - B.1. The unit and first-order symbols
  - B.2. Multiplication by a derivative symbol

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text:
## A. The action of a series

### A.1. The action on monomials

The action of `χ` sends each monomial `∂^s` to its Leibniz expansion with `χ`, a finite sum of
symbols, which pairs with `f` as `∂^s` pairs with `χ f` by `pairing_constr_leibniz`.

### A.2. Multiplication before differentiation

Pairing a symbol with a series applies it and takes the value at `x₀`, so
`pairing (seriesAction χ P) f = pairing P (χ * f)` says that `seriesAction χ P` applies `P` after
multiplying by `χ`. In particular the constant series `C c` acts as multiplication by `c`.

## B. Low-order symbols and derivatives

### B.1. The unit and first-order symbols

A series `χ` acts on the unit symbol by `χ(x₀)`, and sends `∂_μ` to `χ(x₀) ∂_μ + (∂_μ χ)(x₀)`,
which is the product rule at the base point.

### B.2. Multiplication by a derivative symbol

Appending `∂_μ` to a symbol amounts to differentiating the series it pairs with, by
`pairing_mul_basis_singleton`, so the product rule for `∂_μ (χ f)` relates the action of `χ` to
multiplication by `∂_μ`.

declarations.name: SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ.seriesAction
declarations.doc: The action of series on derivative symbols, defined on monomials by the product rule.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def seriesAction : SpaceTimeAlgebra →+* Module.End ℂ SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ

declarations.name: SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ.seriesAction_basis
declarations.doc: The action of `χ` on a monomial `∂^s` is its Leibniz expansion.
declarations.statement:
lemma seriesAction_basis (χ : SpaceTimeAlgebra) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    seriesAction χ ∂^[s] =
      (s.antidiagonal.map fun t => constantCoeff (iteratedPDeriv t.1 χ) • ∂^[t.2]).sum

declarations.name: SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ.pairing_seriesAction
declarations.doc: The action of `χ` multiplies by `χ` before applying the symbol.
declarations.statement:
lemma pairing_seriesAction (χ : SpaceTimeAlgebra) (p : SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ)
    (f : SpaceTimeAlgebra) :
    pairing (seriesAction χ p) f = pairing p (χ * f)

declarations.name: SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ.seriesAction_C
declarations.doc: The constant series `C c` acts as scalar multiplication by `c`.
declarations.statement: lemma seriesAction_C (c : ℂ) : seriesAction (C c) = c • LinearMap.id

declarations.name: SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ.seriesAction_apply_one
declarations.doc: A series acts on the unit symbol by its base-point value.
declarations.statement:
lemma seriesAction_apply_one (χ : SpaceTimeAlgebra) :
    seriesAction χ 1 = constantCoeff χ • 1

declarations.name: SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ.seriesAction_basis_singleton
declarations.doc: A series `χ` sends `∂_μ` to `χ(x₀) ∂_μ + (∂_μ χ)(x₀)`, the product rule.
declarations.statement:
lemma seriesAction_basis_singleton (χ : SpaceTimeAlgebra) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    seriesAction χ ∂[μ] = constantCoeff χ • ∂[μ] + constantCoeff (pderiv μ χ) • 1

declarations.name: SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ.seriesAction_mul_basis_singleton
declarations.doc: The action commutes with multiplication by `∂_μ` up to the action of `pderiv μ χ`.
declarations.statement:
lemma seriesAction_mul_basis_singleton (χ : SpaceTimeAlgebra) (p : SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ)
    (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    seriesAction χ (p * ∂[μ]) = seriesAction χ p * ∂[μ] + seriesAction (pderiv μ χ) p

modules.title: The spacetime derivative algebra
modules.doc:
The algebra of derivative symbols on spacetime, which evaluate on the spacetime algebra.

## i. Overview

In field theory, local quantities are built from a field and finitely many of its derivatives at
a point. A linear combination of such derivatives is the value `(P φ)(x₀)` of a linear
differential operator `P` with constant coefficients, and such an operator is a polynomial in the
partial derivatives `∂_μ`. These polynomials, which we call derivative symbols, form the algebra
`SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ`. The value `(P φ)(x₀)` is determined by the derivatives of `φ` at `x₀`,
which its Taylor series `taylorSeries x₀ φ` records as an element of the spacetime algebra. We
therefore pair a symbol `P` with any series `f` by applying `P` to `f` and taking the value at the
base point, so that pairing with `taylorSeries x₀ φ` gives `(P φ)(x₀)`.

Throughout we use the notation of `SpaceTimeAlgebra`, whose elements we call series. For a
multiset `s` of directions,

- `x^s` is the monomial in which each `x^μ` occurs as often as `μ` occurs in `s`;
- `∂^s f` is the iterated derivative of a series `f`, and `(∂^s f)(x₀)` is its value at the base
  point `x₀`;
- `s!` is the product of the factorials of the multiplicities in `s`;
- `∂^s` is the derivative symbol of `∂^s f`, written `∂^[s]` in Lean.

## ii. Key results

- `SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ` : the algebra of derivative symbols.
- `SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ.basis` : the monomial basis indexed by multisets of directions.
- `SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ.basis_mul` : monomials multiply by adding multisets.
- `SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ.pairing` : applies a symbol to a series and evaluates at the base
  point.
- `SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ.pairing_basis` : `∂^s` pairs with `f` to the value `(∂^s f)(x₀)`.
- `SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ.pairing_injective` : the pairing separates derivative symbols.
- `SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ.pairing_mul_basis_singleton` : multiplying by `∂_μ` differentiates the
  series.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The derivative algebra
  - A.1. The monomial basis
- B. Pairing symbols with series
  - B.1. Pairing with monomials
  - B.2. Injectivity of the pairing
  - B.3. Multiplication by a derivative symbol
  - B.4. Pairing with a product

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text:
## A. The derivative algebra

The partial derivatives of a smooth field commute, so these polynomials are in commuting symbols
`∂_μ`. Each symbol involves finitely many derivatives (whereas the Taylor series of a field keeps
all of them). Formally, the derivative algebra is the symmetric algebra on
`Module.Dual ℂ Lorentz.ComplexCoVector`, the dual of the complex covector module, with `∂_μ` the
dual basis vector in direction `μ` and time coordinate `x⁰ = ct`.

### A.1. The monomial basis

The order of the monomial `∂^s` is the size of `s`, and multiplying monomials adds their
multisets. The basis is Mathlib's `Module.Basis.symmetricAlgebra`, reindexed by multisets.

## B. Pairing symbols with series

The monomial `∂^s` pairs with a series `f` to `(∂^s f)(x₀)`, and the pairing extends linearly in
the symbol (in commutative algebra this is the apolarity pairing, with power series in place of
polynomials). On the Taylor series of a field it gives `(∂^s φ)(x₀)`, by
`constantCoeff_iteratedPDeriv_taylorSeries`.

### B.1. Pairing with monomials

Since `(∂^s f)(x₀)` is `s!` times the coefficient of `x^s` in `f` (`constantCoeff_iteratedPDeriv`),
the symbol `∂_μ²` paired with the series `(x^μ)²` gives `2`, while the coefficient of `(x^μ)²` is
`1`.

### B.2. Injectivity of the pairing

The same computation on the monomials `x^s` recovers every coefficient of a symbol, so distinct
symbols take different values on some series.

### B.3. Multiplication by a derivative symbol

Appending `∂_μ` to a symbol amounts to differentiating the series along `μ`, and on
`taylorSeries x₀ φ` to differentiating the field, by `taylorSeries_deriv`.

### B.4. Pairing with a product

Pairing `∂^s` with a product `χ f` gives `(∂^s (χ f))(x₀)`, which the Leibniz rule
`constantCoeff_iteratedPDeriv_mul` expands as a sum of terms `(∂^t₁ χ)(x₀) (∂^t₂ f)(x₀)` with
`t₁ + t₂ = s`. Replacing each `(∂^t₂ f)(x₀)` by the symbol `∂^t₂`, and extending linearly to all
symbols, gives a symbol that pairs with `f` as the original pairs with `χ f`.

declarations.name: SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ
declarations.doc:
The algebra of derivative symbols on spacetime, the polynomials in four commuting symbols
`∂_μ`.
declarations.statement: abbrev SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ : Type

declarations.name: SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ.basis
declarations.doc: The monomial basis of the derivative algebra, in which `basis s` is the monomial `∂^s`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def basis : Module.Basis (Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) ℂ SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ

declarations.name: SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ.basis_apply
declarations.doc:
The monomial `∂^s` is the polynomial monomial whose exponents are the multiplicities in
`s`.
declarations.statement:
lemma basis_apply (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    ∂^[s] = (SymmetricAlgebra.equivMvPolynomial Lorentz.ComplexCoVector.basis.dualBasis).symm
      (MvPolynomial.monomial (Multiset.toFinsupp s) 1)

declarations.name: SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ.basis_zero
declarations.doc: The empty monomial is the unit.
declarations.statement: lemma basis_zero : ∂^[0] = 1

declarations.name: SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ.basis_singleton
declarations.doc: The monomial of a single direction `μ` is the derivative symbol `∂_μ`.
declarations.statement:
lemma basis_singleton (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3) :
    ∂[μ] = SymmetricAlgebra.ι ℂ _ (Lorentz.ComplexCoVector.basis.dualBasis μ)

declarations.name: SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ.basis_mul
declarations.doc: Monomials multiply by adding multisets, `∂^s ∂^t = ∂^(s + t)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma basis_mul (s t : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    ∂^[s] * ∂^[t] = ∂^[s + t]

declarations.name: SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ.pairing
declarations.doc:
The pairing of a symbol `P` with a series `f`, given by the value of `P f` at the base
point.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def pairing : SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ →ₗ[ℂ] SpaceTimeAlgebra →ₗ[ℂ] ℂ

declarations.name: SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ.pairing_basis
declarations.doc: The monomial `∂^s` pairs with `f` to the base-point value `(∂^s f)(x₀)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma pairing_basis (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (f : SpaceTimeAlgebra) :
    pairing ∂^[s] f = constantCoeff (iteratedPDeriv s f)

declarations.name: SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ.pairing_one
declarations.doc: The unit symbol pairs with `f` to its base-point value `f(x₀)`.
declarations.statement: lemma pairing_one (f : SpaceTimeAlgebra) : pairing 1 f = constantCoeff f

declarations.name: SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ.pairing_monomial
declarations.doc:
Pairing a symbol with the series `x^s` gives `s!` times the coefficient of `∂^s` in the
symbol.
declarations.statement:
lemma pairing_monomial (p : SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ) (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) :
    pairing p (monomial (Multiset.toFinsupp s) 1) =
      ((∏ ν, (s.count ν).factorial : ℕ) : ℂ) * basis.repr p s

declarations.name: SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ.pairing_injective
declarations.doc: The pairing separates derivative symbols.
declarations.statement: lemma pairing_injective : Function.Injective pairing

declarations.name: SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ.ext_of_pairing_eq
declarations.doc: Symbols that pair equally with every series are equal.
declarations.statement:
lemma ext_of_pairing_eq {p q : SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ} (h : ∀ f, pairing p f = pairing q f) :
    p = q

declarations.name: SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ.pairing_mul_basis_singleton
declarations.doc: Multiplying a symbol by `∂_μ` corresponds to applying `pderiv μ` to the series.
declarations.statement:
lemma pairing_mul_basis_singleton (p : SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ) (μ : Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)
    (f : SpaceTimeAlgebra) :
    pairing (p * ∂[μ]) f = pairing p (pderiv μ f)

declarations.name: SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ.pairing_basis_mul
declarations.doc: Pairing `∂^s` with a product `χ f` expands by the Leibniz rule.
declarations.statement:
lemma pairing_basis_mul (s : Multiset (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 3)) (χ f : SpaceTimeAlgebra) :
    pairing ∂^[s] (χ * f) =
      (s.antidiagonal.map fun t =>
        constantCoeff (iteratedPDeriv t.1 χ) * pairing ∂^[t.2] f).sum

declarations.name: SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ.pairing_constr_leibniz
declarations.doc:
Replacing each monomial `∂^s` of `p` by its Leibniz expansion with `χ` gives a symbol that
pairs with `f` as `p` pairs with `χ f`.
declarations.statement:
lemma pairing_constr_leibniz (χ : SpaceTimeAlgebra) (p : SpaceTimeDerivAlgebraℂ)
    (f : SpaceTimeAlgebra) :
    pairing (basis.constr ℂ (fun s => (s.antidiagonal.map fun t =>
      constantCoeff (iteratedPDeriv t.1 χ) • ∂^[t.2]).sum) p) f = pairing p (χ * f)

modules.title: Time slice
modules.doc:
Time slicing functions on spacetime, turning them into a function
`Time → Space d → M`.

This is useful when going from relativistic physics (defined using `SpaceTime`)
to non-relativistic physics (defined using `Space` and `Time`).

sections.text: ## B. Time slices of distributions
### B.1. Time slices and derivatives

declarations.name: SpaceTime.timeSlice
declarations.doc:
The timeslice of a function `SpaceTime d → M` forming a function
`Time → Space d → M`.
declarations.statement:
def timeSlice {d : ℕ} {M : Type} (c : SpeedOfLight := 1) :
    (SpaceTime d → M) ≃ (Time → Space d → M)

declarations.name: SpaceTime.timeSlice_contDiff
declarations.statement:
lemma timeSlice_contDiff {d : ℕ} {M : Type} [NormedAddCommGroup M]
    [NormedSpace ℝ M]
    {n} (c : SpeedOfLight) (f : SpaceTime d → M) (h : ContDiff ℝ n f) :
    ContDiff ℝ n ↿(timeSlice c f)

declarations.name: SpaceTime.timeSlice_differentiable
declarations.statement:
lemma timeSlice_differentiable {d : ℕ} {M : Type} [NormedAddCommGroup M]
    [NormedSpace ℝ M] (c : SpeedOfLight)
    (f : SpaceTime d → M) (h : Differentiable ℝ f) :
    Differentiable ℝ ↿(timeSlice c f)

declarations.name: SpaceTime.timeSlice_symm_contDiff
declarations.statement:
lemma timeSlice_symm_contDiff {d : ℕ} {M : Type} [NormedAddCommGroup M] [NormedSpace ℝ M]
    {n} (c : SpeedOfLight) (f : Time → Space d → M) (h : ContDiff ℝ n ↿f) :
    ContDiff ℝ n ((timeSlice c).symm f)

declarations.name: SpaceTime.timeSlice_symm_differentiable
declarations.statement:
lemma timeSlice_symm_differentiable {d : ℕ} {M : Type} [NormedAddCommGroup M] [NormedSpace ℝ M]
    (c : SpeedOfLight)
    (f : Time → Space d → M) (h : Differentiable ℝ ↿f) :
    Differentiable ℝ ↿((timeSlice c).symm f)

declarations.name: SpaceTime.timeSliceLinearEquiv
declarations.doc:
The timeslice of a function `SpaceTime d → M` forming a function
`Time → Space d → M`, as a linear equivalence.
declarations.statement:
def timeSliceLinearEquiv {d : ℕ} {M : Type} [AddCommGroup M] [Module ℝ M]
    (c : SpeedOfLight := 1) :
    (SpaceTime d → M) ≃ₗ[ℝ] (Time → Space d → M)

declarations.name: SpaceTime.timeSliceLinearEquiv_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma timeSliceLinearEquiv_apply {d : ℕ} {M : Type} [AddCommGroup M] [Module ℝ M]
    (c : SpeedOfLight) (f : SpaceTime d → M) : timeSliceLinearEquiv c f = timeSlice c f

declarations.name: SpaceTime.timeSliceLinearEquiv_symm_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma timeSliceLinearEquiv_symm_apply {d : ℕ} {M : Type} [AddCommGroup M] [Module ℝ M]
    (c : SpeedOfLight) (f : Time → Space d → M) :
    (timeSliceLinearEquiv c).symm f = (timeSlice c).symm f

declarations.name: SpaceTime.distTimeSlice
declarations.doc:
The time slice of a distribution on `SpaceTime d` to form a distribution
on `Time × Space d`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def distTimeSlice {M d} [NormedAddCommGroup M] [NormedSpace ℝ M]
    (c : SpeedOfLight := 1) :
    ((SpaceTime d) →d[ℝ] M) ≃L[ℝ] ((Time × Space d) →d[ℝ] M)

declarations.name: SpaceTime.distTimeSlice_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma distTimeSlice_apply {M d} [NormedAddCommGroup M] [NormedSpace ℝ M]
    (c : SpeedOfLight) (f : (SpaceTime d) →d[ℝ] M)
    (κ : 𝓢(Time × Space d, ℝ)) : distTimeSlice c f κ =
    f (compCLMOfContinuousLinearEquiv ℝ (toTimeAndSpace c) κ)

declarations.name: SpaceTime.distTimeSlice_symm_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma distTimeSlice_symm_apply {M d} [NormedAddCommGroup M] [NormedSpace ℝ M]
    (c : SpeedOfLight) (f : (Time × (Space d)) →d[ℝ] M)
    (κ : 𝓢(SpaceTime d, ℝ)) : (distTimeSlice c).symm f κ =
    f (compCLMOfContinuousLinearEquiv ℝ (toTimeAndSpace c).symm κ)

declarations.name: SpaceTime.distTimeSlice_distDeriv_inl
declarations.statement:
lemma distTimeSlice_distDeriv_inl {M d} [NormedAddCommGroup M] [NormedSpace ℝ M]
    {c : SpeedOfLight}
    (f : (SpaceTime d) →d[ℝ] M) :
    distTimeSlice c (distDeriv (Sum.inl 0) f) =
    (1/c.val) • Space.distTimeDeriv (distTimeSlice c f)

declarations.name: SpaceTime.distDeriv_inl_distTimeSlice_symm
declarations.statement:
lemma distDeriv_inl_distTimeSlice_symm {M d} [NormedAddCommGroup M] [NormedSpace ℝ M]
    {c : SpeedOfLight}
    (f : (Time × Space d) →d[ℝ] M) :
    distDeriv (Sum.inl 0) ((distTimeSlice c).symm f) =
    (1/c.val) • (distTimeSlice c).symm (Space.distTimeDeriv f)

declarations.name: SpaceTime.distTimeSlice_symm_distTimeDeriv_eq
declarations.statement:
lemma distTimeSlice_symm_distTimeDeriv_eq {M d} [NormedAddCommGroup M] [NormedSpace ℝ M]
    {c : SpeedOfLight}
    (f : (Time × Space d) →d[ℝ] M) :
    (distTimeSlice c).symm (Space.distTimeDeriv f) =
    c.val • distDeriv (Sum.inl 0) ((distTimeSlice c).symm f)

declarations.name: SpaceTime.distTimeSlice_distDeriv_inr
declarations.statement:
lemma distTimeSlice_distDeriv_inr {M d} [NormedAddCommGroup M] [NormedSpace ℝ M]
    {c : SpeedOfLight}
    (i : Fin d) (f : (SpaceTime d) →d[ℝ] M) :
    distTimeSlice c (distDeriv (Sum.inr i) f) =
    Space.distSpaceDeriv i (distTimeSlice c f)

declarations.name: SpaceTime.distDeriv_inr_distTimeSlice_symm
declarations.statement:
lemma distDeriv_inr_distTimeSlice_symm {M d} [NormedAddCommGroup M] [NormedSpace ℝ M]
    {c : SpeedOfLight}
    (i : Fin d) (f : (Time × Space d) →d[ℝ] M) :
    distDeriv (Sum.inr i) ((distTimeSlice c).symm f) =
    (distTimeSlice c).symm (Space.distSpaceDeriv i f)

modules.title: Time
modules.doc:
`Time` represents instants with a fixed but arbitrary unit and orientation. It is an
affine space over `ℝ`: two instants determine a real-valued elapsed time, and adding
such a duration to an instant produces another instant. There is no distinguished zero.

The field `Time.val` is an implementation coordinate, not a frame-relative time
coordinate. A reference frame chooses its own time origin. Import
`Physlib.SpaceAndTime.Time.InnerProductSpace` to use the inner product space structure with the
implicit origin `Time.mk 0`, including addition of instants, norms, and derivatives.

sections.text: # A. The `Time` type
# B. The affine structure
# C. The metric and manifold structure

    ContMDiff 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ) 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ) n (fun t : Time ↦ t -ᵥ t₀)

modules.title: Time Derivatives
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

In this module we define and prove basic lemmas about derivatives of functions on `Time`.

## ii. Key results

- `deriv` : The derivative of a function `Time → M` at a given time.
- `manifoldDeriv` : The derivative of a function from `Time` to a manifold.
- `derivVec` : The derivative of a function from `Time` into a torsor, such as `Space d`,
  valued in the vector space of displacements of that torsor.
- `hasDerivAt_comp_toRealCLE_symm` : The time derivative as a `HasDerivAt` on `ℝ`, for a curve
  reparametrised through the canonical equivalence `toRealCLE.symm : ℝ ≃L[ℝ] Time`.
- `deriv_comp_toRealCLE_of_hasDerivAt` : Its converse, a `HasDerivAt` on `ℝ` read as the time
  derivative of the curve pulled back to `Time` through `toRealCLE`.
- `hasDerivAt_mk_of_differentiableAt` and `deriv_eq_of_hasDerivAt` : The same two bridges for a
  real-valued curve `f : Time → ℝ`, stated at `t : Time` through the curve `τ ↦ f ⟨τ⟩` on `ℝ`.
- `deriv_comp_neg` and `deriv_deriv_comp_neg` : The first and second time derivatives under the
  reversal of time `t ↦ -t`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The definition of the derivative
  - A.1. Derivatives of functions into vector spaces
  - A.2. The derivative through the canonical equivalence with `ℝ`
  - A.3. Derivatives of functions into manifolds
  - A.4. Derivatives of functions into torsors
- B. Linearlity properties of the derivative
- C. Derivative of constant functions
- D. Smoothness properties and the reversal of time
- E. Derivatives of components
- F. Derivatives of trajectories into `Space`

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. The definition of the derivative
### A.1. Derivatives of functions into vector spaces

### A.2. The derivative through the canonical equivalence with `ℝ`

`Time` is identified with `ℝ` by the continuous linear equivalence `toRealCLE`. Precomposing a
curve `w : Time → M` with `toRealCLE.symm : ℝ ≃L[ℝ] Time` gives a curve on `ℝ`, whose Mathlib
derivative (`HasDerivAt`) at `τ` is the time derivative `∂ₜ w` evaluated at `toRealCLE.symm τ`.
This is the bridge through which Mathlib's calculus and ODE theory on `ℝ` applies to curves on
`Time`. Conversely, a `HasDerivAt` on `ℝ` at `toRealCLE t` is the time derivative at `t` of the
curve pulled back to `Time` through `toRealCLE`.
### A.3. Derivatives of functions into manifolds

### A.4. Derivatives of functions into torsors

A trajectory in physical space is a curve of points, and its velocity is a displacement per
unit time, that is a vector. For a torsor `P` over a vector space `V`, for example
`Space d` over `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)`, the derivative of a curve `f : Time → P` is
therefore valued in `V` rather than in `P`. It is defined by differentiating the displacement
curve `s ↦ f s -ᵥ f t`, which is `V`-valued, so that no origin of `P` is ever chosen. The
reference point used to form the displacement is irrelevant, see `derivVec_eq_fderiv_vsub`.
## B. Linearlity properties of the derivative
## C. Derivative of constant functions
## D. Smoothness properties and the reversal of time
## E. Derivatives of components

## F. Derivatives of trajectories into `Space`

For a trajectory `f : Time → Space d` of points in space, the torsor derivative `∂ₜᵥ f` is
valued in the displacement space `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)`. Componentwise it agrees with the
time derivatives of the coordinates, and under the identification of `Space d` with its
displacement space given by the (arbitrary) zero point it recovers the vector space derivative
`∂ₜ f`. The latter bridges `∂ₜᵥ` to the existing `∂ₜ` API.

Note that `Space d` carries two `AddTorsor` instances: the intended one over
`EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)`, and one over itself coming from the module structure on `Space d`.
Instance resolution selects the former, so `∂ₜᵥ` of a trajectory in `Space d` is valued in
`EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)` as intended.

declarations.name: Time.deriv
declarations.doc: Given a function `f : Time → M` the derivative of `f`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def deriv [AddCommGroup M] [Module ℝ M] [TopologicalSpace M]
    (f : Time → M) : Time → M

declarations.name: Time.deriv_eq
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_eq [AddCommGroup M] [Module ℝ M] [TopologicalSpace M]
    (f : Time → M) (t : Time) : Time.deriv f t = fderiv ℝ f t 1

declarations.name: Time.toRealCLE_symm_one
declarations.doc: The canonical equivalence `toRealCLE.symm : ℝ ≃L[ℝ] Time` sends `1 : ℝ` to `1 : Time`.
declarations.statement: lemma toRealCLE_symm_one : toRealCLE.symm (1 : ℝ) = (1 : Time)

declarations.name: Time.hasDerivAt_comp_toRealCLE_symm
declarations.doc:
Bridge from the time derivative to `HasDerivAt`: if `w : Time → M` is differentiable at
`toRealCLE.symm τ`, then the curve `τ ↦ w (toRealCLE.symm τ)` on `ℝ` has derivative
`∂ₜ w (toRealCLE.symm τ)` at `τ`.
declarations.statement:
lemma hasDerivAt_comp_toRealCLE_symm [NormedAddCommGroup M] [NormedSpace ℝ M]
    (w : Time → M) (τ : ℝ) (hw : DifferentiableAt ℝ w (toRealCLE.symm τ)) :
    HasDerivAt (fun τ : ℝ => w (toRealCLE.symm τ)) (∂ₜ w (toRealCLE.symm τ)) τ

declarations.name: Time.deriv_comp_toRealCLE_of_hasDerivAt
declarations.doc:
The converse of the bridge `hasDerivAt_comp_toRealCLE_symm`: if the curve `γ : ℝ → M` has
derivative `v` at `toRealCLE t`, then the curve `t ↦ γ (toRealCLE t)` on `Time` has time
derivative `v` at `t`.
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_comp_toRealCLE_of_hasDerivAt [NormedAddCommGroup M] [NormedSpace ℝ M]
    (γ : ℝ → M) (t : Time) (v : M) (h : HasDerivAt γ v (toRealCLE t)) :
    ∂ₜ (fun s => γ (toRealCLE s)) t = v

declarations.name: Time.deriv_eq_of_hasDerivAt
declarations.doc:
The time derivative of any `f : Time → ℝ` at `t` is the derivative at `t.val` of the curve
`τ ↦ f ⟨τ⟩` on `ℝ`.
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_eq_of_hasDerivAt {f : Time → ℝ} {t : Time} {v : ℝ}
    (h : HasDerivAt (fun τ : ℝ => f ⟨τ⟩) v t.val) : ∂ₜ f t = v

declarations.name: Time.hasDerivAt_mk_of_differentiableAt
declarations.doc:
A curve `f : Time → ℝ` differentiable at `t` gives the curve `σ ↦ f ⟨σ⟩` on `ℝ`,
whose Mathlib derivative at `t.val` is the time derivative `∂ₜ f t`.

declarations.name: Time.manifoldDeriv
declarations.doc:
The time derivative of a function from `Time` to a manifold, as a tangent vector at
the value of the function.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def manifoldDeriv {E H N : Type} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
    [TopologicalSpace H] (I : ModelWithCorners ℝ E H) [TopologicalSpace N]
    [ChartedSpace H N] (f : Time → N) : (t : Time) → TangentSpace I (f t)

declarations.name: Time.manifoldDeriv_eq
declarations.statement:
lemma manifoldDeriv_eq {E H N : Type} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
    [TopologicalSpace H] (I : ModelWithCorners ℝ E H) [TopologicalSpace N]
    [ChartedSpace H N] (f : Time → N) (t : Time) :
    manifoldDeriv I f t =
      mfderiv 𝓘(ℝ, Time) I f t ((1 : Time) : TangentSpace 𝓘(ℝ, Time) t)

declarations.name: Time.deriv_eq_mfderiv
declarations.doc: The time derivative is the manifold derivative for functions into normed spaces.
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_eq_mfderiv [NormedAddCommGroup M] [NormedSpace ℝ M]
    (f : Time → M) (t : Time) :
    deriv f t =
      mfderiv 𝓘(ℝ, Time) 𝓘(ℝ, M) f t
        ((1 : Time) : TangentSpace 𝓘(ℝ, Time) t)

declarations.name: Time.deriv_eq_manifoldDeriv
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_eq_manifoldDeriv [NormedAddCommGroup M] [NormedSpace ℝ M]
    (f : Time → M) (t : Time) :
    deriv f t = manifoldDeriv 𝓘(ℝ, M) f t

declarations.name: Time.manifoldDeriv_const
declarations.statement:
lemma manifoldDeriv_const {E H N : Type} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
    [TopologicalSpace H] (I : ModelWithCorners ℝ E H) [TopologicalSpace N]
    [ChartedSpace H N] (n : N) :
    manifoldDeriv I (fun _ : Time => n) t = 0

declarations.name: Time.derivVec
declarations.doc:
The time derivative of a trajectory into a torsor `P` over a vector space `V`,
valued in `V`. For a trajectory `f : Time → Space d` this is the velocity, a spatial vector in
`EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)` rather than a point of `Space d`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def derivVec {V P : Type} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℝ V] [TopologicalSpace V]
    [AddTorsor V P] (f : Time → P) : Time → V

declarations.name: Time.derivVec_eq
declarations.statement:
lemma derivVec_eq {V P : Type} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℝ V] [TopologicalSpace V]
    [AddTorsor V P] (f : Time → P) (t : Time) :
    ∂ₜᵥ f t = fderiv ℝ (fun s => f s -ᵥ f t) t 1

declarations.name: Time.derivVec_eq_fderiv_vsub
declarations.doc:
The derivative of a trajectory into a torsor does not depend on the reference point used
to form the displacement: any base point `p` gives the same derivative. The normed hypotheses on
`V` here come from `fderiv_add_const`; the definition itself needs only a topological vector
space.
declarations.statement:
lemma derivVec_eq_fderiv_vsub {V P : Type} [NormedAddCommGroup V] [NormedSpace ℝ V]
    [AddTorsor V P] (f : Time → P) (p : P) (t : Time) :
    ∂ₜᵥ f t = fderiv ℝ (fun s => f s -ᵥ p) t 1

declarations.name: Time.deriv_smul
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_smul (f : Time → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) (k : ℝ)
    (hf : Differentiable ℝ f) :
    ∂ₜ (fun t => k • f t) t = k • ∂ₜ (fun t => f t) t

declarations.name: Time.deriv_neg
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_neg [NormedAddCommGroup M] [NormedSpace ℝ M] (f : Time → M) :
    ∂ₜ (-f) t = -∂ₜ f t

declarations.name: Time.deriv_add
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_add [NormedAddCommGroup M] [NormedSpace ℝ M] (f g : Time → M)
    (hf : DifferentiableAt ℝ f t) (hg : DifferentiableAt ℝ g t) :
    ∂ₜ (fun s => f s + g s) t = ∂ₜ f t + ∂ₜ g t

declarations.name: Time.deriv_fun_sum
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_fun_sum {ι : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup M] [NormedSpace ℝ M]
    (s : Finset ι) (a : ι → Time → M) (ha : ∀ i ∈ s, DifferentiableAt ℝ (a i) t) :
    ∂ₜ (fun x => ∑ i ∈ s, a i x) t = ∑ i ∈ s, ∂ₜ (a i) t

declarations.name: Time.deriv_mul_const
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_mul_const (f : Time → ℝ) (c : ℝ) (hf : DifferentiableAt ℝ f t) :
    ∂ₜ (fun s => f s * c) t = ∂ₜ f t * c

declarations.name: Time.deriv_div
declarations.doc:
Quotient rule for `Time.deriv` on real-valued functions: if `c` and `g` are
differentiable at `t` and `g t ≠ 0`, then
`∂ₜ (c / g) t = (∂ₜ c t * g t - c t * ∂ₜ g t) / (g t)^2`.
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_div {c g : Time → ℝ}
    (hc : DifferentiableAt ℝ c t) (hg : DifferentiableAt ℝ g t) (hgz : g t ≠ 0) :
    ∂ₜ (fun s => c s / g s) t =
      (∂ₜ c t * g t - c t * ∂ₜ g t) / (g t) ^ 2

declarations.name: Time.deriv_const
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_const [NormedAddCommGroup M] [NormedSpace ℝ M] (m : M) :
    ∂ₜ (fun _ => m) t = 0

declarations.name: Time.derivVec_const
declarations.doc: A trajectory constant at a point of a torsor has zero derivative.
declarations.statement:
lemma derivVec_const {V P : Type} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℝ V] [TopologicalSpace V]
    [AddTorsor V P] (p : P) :
    ∂ₜᵥ (fun _ => p) t = (0 : V)

declarations.name: Time.val_contDiff
declarations.statement: lemma val_contDiff {n : WithTop ℕ∞} : ContDiff ℝ n Time.val

declarations.name: Time.deriv_differentiable_of_contDiff
Time.deriv_contDiff_of_contDiff
Time.deriv_contDiff_of_contDiff_succ
declarations.doc: The time derivative of a `C^(n+1)` curve is `C^n`.

declarations.name: Time.deriv_differentiable_of_contDiff_two
declarations.doc: The time derivative of a `C²` curve is differentiable.

declarations.name: Time.deriv_contDiff_of_space
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_contDiff_of_space {n} {M : Type} [NormedAddCommGroup M] [NormedSpace ℝ M]
    (f : Time → Space d → M) (hf : ContDiff ℝ (n + 1) ↿f) :
    ContDiff ℝ n fun (x : Space d) => (∂ₜ fun t => f t x) t

declarations.name: Time.deriv_comp_neg
declarations.doc:
The chain rule for the time derivative under the reversal of time: the derivative of
`t ↦ f (-t)` at `t` is minus the derivative of `f` at `-t`.
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_comp_neg {M : Type} [NormedAddCommGroup M] [NormedSpace ℝ M]
    (f : Time → M) (t : Time) (hf : DifferentiableAt ℝ f (-t)) :
    ∂ₜ (fun s => f (-s)) t = -∂ₜ f (-t)

declarations.name: Time.deriv_deriv_comp_neg
declarations.doc:
The second derivative is unchanged by the reversal of time: for a `C²` curve `f`, the second
derivative of `t ↦ f (-t)` at `t` is the second derivative of `f` at `-t`, the two changes of sign
cancelling.
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_deriv_comp_neg {M : Type} [NormedAddCommGroup M] [NormedSpace ℝ M]
    (f : Time → M) (hf : ContDiff ℝ 2 f) (t : Time) :
    ∂ₜ (∂ₜ (fun s => f (-s))) t = ∂ₜ (∂ₜ f) (-t)

declarations.name: Time.differentiable_euclid
Time.deriv_comp_coord
declarations.doc:
Chain rule for a real function of one coordinate of a curve in Euclidean space: the time

modules.title: Time as an inner product space
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

In this module we equip the affine type `Time` with a real inner product space structure,
choosing the implicit origin represented by `Time.mk 0`. The units and orientation agree with the
real-valued displacements defined in `Physlib.SpaceAndTime.Time.Basic`.

We note that this is the version of time most often used in undergraduate and
non-mathematical physics.

The choice of units or origin can be made on a case-by-case basis, as
long as they are done consistently. However, since the choice of units and origin is
left implicit, Lean will not catch inconsistencies in the choice of units or origin when
working with `Time`.

For example, for the classical mechanics system corresponding to the harmonic oscillator,
one can take the origin of time to be the time at which the initial conditions are specified,
and the units can be taken as anything as long as the units chosen for time `t` and
the angular frequency `ω` are consistent.

With this choice, `Time` becomes a 1d vector space over `ℝ` with an inner product.

## ii. Key results

- `toRealCLE` : The continuous linear equivalence from `Time` to `ℝ`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Instances on Time
  - A.1. Natural numbers as elements of `Time`
  - A.2. Real numbers as elements of `Time`
  - A.3. Time is inhabited
  - A.4. The order on `Time`
