modules.title: Curves in normed spaces over `Time`
modules.doc:
A curve `Time → F` is smooth, or has a given derivative, iff its coordinate curve does.

## i. Overview

The charts of `Time` are translations, so the coordinate curve `τ ↦ γ (τ +ᵥ t₀)` needs no origin.

## ii. Key results

- `Time.contMDiff_iff_contDiff_vadd`: a curve is `C^n` iff its coordinate curve is
- `Time.mfderiv_eq_deriv_vadd`: the manifold derivative is the derivative of the coordinate curve
- `Time.tangentMap_eq_deriv_vadd`: the tangent map of a curve in coordinates

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Smoothness and differentiability of curves
- B. Derivatives of curves

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. Smoothness and differentiability of curves
## B. Derivatives of curves

declarations.name: Time.contMDiffAt_iff_contDiffAt_vadd
declarations.doc: A curve into a normed space is `C^n` at `x` iff its coordinate curve is `C^n` at `0`.
declarations.statement:
lemma contMDiffAt_iff_contDiffAt_vadd (γ : Time → F) (x : Time) (n : ℕ∞ω) :
    ContMDiffAt 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ) 𝓘(ℝ, F) n γ x ↔ ContDiffAt ℝ n (fun τ : ℝ ↦ γ (τ +ᵥ x)) 0

declarations.name: Time.mdifferentiableAt_iff_differentiableAt_vadd
declarations.doc: A curve into a normed space is differentiable at `x` iff its coordinate curve is at `0`.
declarations.statement:

    MDifferentiableAt 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ) 𝓘(ℝ, F) γ x ↔ DifferentiableAt ℝ (fun τ : ℝ ↦ γ (τ +ᵥ x)) 0

declarations.name: Time.contMDiff_iff_contDiff_vadd
declarations.doc:
A curve `γ : Time → F` into a normed space is `C^n` iff the coordinate curve
`τ ↦ γ (τ +ᵥ t₀)` is `C^n`.
declarations.statement:
lemma contMDiff_iff_contDiff_vadd (γ : Time → F) (t₀ : Time) (n : ℕ∞ω) :
    ContMDiff 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ) 𝓘(ℝ, F) n γ ↔ ContDiff ℝ n (fun τ : ℝ ↦ γ (τ +ᵥ t₀))

declarations.name: Time.mdifferentiableAt_vadd_iff
declarations.doc:
A curve into a normed space is differentiable at `s +ᵥ t₀` iff its coordinate curve based
at `t₀` is differentiable at `s`.
declarations.statement:
lemma mdifferentiableAt_vadd_iff (γ : Time → F) (t₀ : Time) (s : ℝ) :
    MDifferentiableAt 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ) 𝓘(ℝ, F) γ (s +ᵥ t₀) ↔
      DifferentiableAt ℝ (fun τ : ℝ ↦ γ (τ +ᵥ t₀)) s

declarations.name: Time.writtenInExtChartAt_eq_vadd
declarations.doc: A curve read in the extended chart at `x` is its coordinate curve based at `x`.
declarations.statement:
lemma writtenInExtChartAt_eq_vadd (γ : Time → F) (x : Time) :
    writtenInExtChartAt 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ) 𝓘(ℝ, F) x γ = fun τ : ℝ ↦ γ (τ +ᵥ x)

declarations.name: Time.mfderiv_eq_deriv_vadd
declarations.doc:
The manifold derivative of a curve into a normed space at `s +ᵥ t₀` applied to `1`
equals the ordinary derivative of the coordinate curve at `s`.
declarations.statement:
lemma mfderiv_eq_deriv_vadd (γ : Time → F) (t₀ : Time) (s : ℝ) :
    mfderiv 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ) 𝓘(ℝ, F) γ (s +ᵥ t₀) (1 : ℝ) = deriv (fun τ : ℝ ↦ γ (τ +ᵥ t₀)) s

declarations.name: Time.tangentMap_eq_deriv_vadd
declarations.doc:
The tangent map of a curve into a normed space sends `⟨s +ᵥ t₀, 1⟩` to the point and
the ordinary derivative of the coordinate curve.
declarations.statement:
lemma tangentMap_eq_deriv_vadd (γ : Time → F) (t₀ : Time) (s : ℝ) :
    tangentMap 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ) 𝓘(ℝ, F) γ ⟨s +ᵥ t₀, (1 : ℝ)⟩ =
      ⟨γ (s +ᵥ t₀), deriv (fun τ : ℝ ↦ γ (τ +ᵥ t₀)) s⟩

modules.title: Time derivatives of matrix-valued functions
modules.doc:
General lemmas on the time derivative `∂ₜ` of square-matrix-valued functions of time: a product
rule, the commutation of the derivative with transpose, and the commutation of the derivative with
taking a matrix entry. These are the tools needed to differentiate a path of matrices.

They rely on the (opt-in) operator-norm structure on matrices — activated here as local instances —
only to invoke the product rule and to view transpose (through `Matrix.transposeLinearEquiv`) as a
continuous linear map. Since all norms on a fixed finite-dimensional space induce the same topology,
differentiability does not depend on this choice.

declarations.name: DifferentiableAt.matrix_transpose
declarations.doc:
The transpose of a differentiable matrix-valued function is differentiable
(cf. `Continuous.matrix_transpose`).
declarations.statement:
lemma DifferentiableAt.matrix_transpose {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]
    {A : E → Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ} {t : E} (hA : DifferentiableAt ℝ A t) :
    DifferentiableAt ℝ (fun s => (A s)ᵀ) t

declarations.name: Time.deriv_matrix_mul
declarations.doc: Product rule for the time derivative of a product of matrix-valued functions.
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_matrix_mul (A B : Time → Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ) (t : Time)
    (hA : DifferentiableAt ℝ A t) (hB : DifferentiableAt ℝ B t) :
    ∂ₜ (fun s => A s * B s) t = A t * ∂ₜ B t + ∂ₜ A t * B t

declarations.name: Time.deriv_matrix_transpose
declarations.doc: The time derivative commutes with transpose.
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_matrix_transpose (A : Time → Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ) (t : Time)
    (hA : DifferentiableAt ℝ A t) :
    ∂ₜ (fun s => (A s)ᵀ) t = (∂ₜ A t)ᵀ

declarations.name: Time.deriv_matrix_apply
declarations.doc: The time derivative commutes with taking a matrix entry.
declarations.statement:
lemma deriv_matrix_apply (A : Time → Matrix (Fin d) (Fin d) ℝ) (t : Time)
    (hA : DifferentiableAt ℝ A t) (i j : Fin d) :
    ∂ₜ (fun s => A s i j) t = (∂ₜ A t) i j

modules.title: The time manifold
modules.doc:
In this module we define the type `TimeMan`, corresponding to the time manifold,
without any additional structures except an orientation, such as a choice of metric or origin.
I.e. it is a manifold diffeomorphic to `ℝ` with no additional structure.

If you are looking for a more standard version of time see the type `Time`.

`TimeMan` is sometimes called topological time, due to the absence of a metric, and its use in
topological field theories.

## Implementation details

The manifold `TimeMan` is defined via the type `ℝ`, and thus inherits a given choice
of map `TimeMan.val : TimeMan → ℝ`, which can be extended to a homeomorphism or a
diffeomorphism. When using `TimeMan.val`, one should be aware that using it does
constitute a choice being made.

sections.text:
## The topology on TimeMan.

The topology on `TimeMan` is induced from the topology on `ℝ`, via the choice
of map `TimeMan.val`.
## The manifold structure on TimeMan
## The orientation on TimeMan

modules.title: Units on time
modules.doc:
A unit of time corresponds to a choice of translationally-invariant
metric on the time manifold. Such a choice is (non-canonically) equivalent to a
choice of positive real number. We define the type `TimeUnit` to be equivalent to the
positive reals.

On `TimeUnit` there is an instance of division giving a real number, corresponding to the
ratio of the two scales of time unit.

We define `HasTimeDimension` to be a property of a function from `TimeUnit` to a type `M`
which is a function that scales with the time unit with respect to the rational power `d`.

To define specific time units, we first state the existence of a
a given time unit, and then construct all other time units from it. We choose to state the
existence of the time unit of seconds, and construct all other time units from that.

sections.text:
## Specific choices of time units

To define a specific time units.
We first define the notion of a second to correspond to the length unit with underlying value
equal to `1`. This is really down to a choice in the isomorphism between the set of metrics
on the time manifold and the positive reals.
From this choice of second, we can define other length units by scaling second.
## Relations between time units

modules.title: Functions and distributions on Time and Space d
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

In this module we define `TimeAndSpace d` as the product of `Time` and `Space d`, and
prove basic lemmas about derivatives of functions and distributions on both coordinates.

The derivative and distribution results are in the namespace `Space` by convention.

## ii. Key results

- `TimeAndSpace d` : Euclidean spacetime as the product of time and space.
- `TimeAndSpace.time` : The projection from `TimeAndSpace d` to `Time`.
- `TimeAndSpace.space` : The projection from `TimeAndSpace d` to `Space d`.
- `distTimeDeriv` : The derivative of a distribution on `Time × Space d` along the
  temporal coordinate.
- `distSpaceDeriv` : The derivative of a distribution on `Time × Space d` along the
  spatial `i` coordinate.
- `distSpaceGrad` : The spatial gradient of a distribution on `Time × Space d`.
- `distSpaceDiv` : The spatial divergence of a distribution on `Time × Space d`.
- `distSpaceCurl` : The spatial curl of a distribution on `Time × Space 3`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The coordinate product and derivatives involving time and space
  - A.1. The `TimeAndSpace` coordinate product
  - A.2. Space and time derivatives in terms of curried functions
  - A.3. Commuting time and space derivatives
  - A.4. Differentiablity conditions

declarations.name: TimeAndSpace
declarations.doc: Euclidean spacetime as the product of time and `d`-dimensional space.
declarations.statement: abbrev TimeAndSpace (d : ℕ := 3)

declarations.name: TimeAndSpace.time
declarations.doc: The time-coordinate projection from `TimeAndSpace d`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def time {d : ℕ} : TimeAndSpace d →L[ℝ] Time

declarations.name: TimeAndSpace.space
declarations.doc: The spatial-coordinate projection from `TimeAndSpace d`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def space {d : ℕ} : TimeAndSpace d →L[ℝ] Space d

declarations.name: TimeAndSpace.time_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma time_apply (tx : TimeAndSpace d) :
    time tx = tx.1

declarations.name: TimeAndSpace.space_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma space_apply (tx : TimeAndSpace d) :
    space tx = tx.2

declarations.name: TimeAndSpace.dist_time_le
declarations.doc: The time projection is nonexpanding for the product metric.
declarations.statement:
lemma dist_time_le (tx ty : TimeAndSpace d) :
    dist (time tx) (time ty) ≤ dist tx ty

declarations.name: TimeAndSpace.dist_space_le
declarations.doc: The spatial projection is nonexpanding for the product metric.
declarations.statement:
lemma dist_space_le (tx ty : TimeAndSpace d) :
    dist (space tx) (space ty) ≤ dist tx ty

declarations.name: Space.fderiv_space_eq_fderiv_curry
declarations.statement:
lemma fderiv_space_eq_fderiv_curry {M} [NormedAddCommGroup M] [NormedSpace ℝ M]
    (f : Time → Space d → M) (t : Time) (x dx : Space d)
    (hf : Differentiable ℝ ↿f) :
    fderiv ℝ (fun x' => f t x') x dx = fderiv ℝ ↿f (t, x) (0, dx)

declarations.name: Space.fderiv_time_eq_fderiv_curry
declarations.statement:
lemma fderiv_time_eq_fderiv_curry {M} [NormedAddCommGroup M] [NormedSpace ℝ M]
    (f : Time → Space d → M) (t dt : Time) (x : Space d)
    (hf : Differentiable ℝ ↿f) :
    fderiv ℝ (fun t' => f t' x) t dt = fderiv ℝ ↿f (t, x) (dt, 0)

declarations.name: Space.fderiv_time_commute_fderiv_space
declarations.doc: Derivatives along space coordinates and time commute.
declarations.statement:
lemma fderiv_time_commute_fderiv_space {M} [NormedAddCommGroup M] [NormedSpace ℝ M]
    (f : Time → Space d → M) (t dt : Time) (x dx : Space d)
    (hf : ContDiff ℝ 2 ↿f) :
    fderiv ℝ (fun t' => fderiv ℝ (fun x' => f t' x') x dx) t dt
    = fderiv ℝ (fun x' => fderiv ℝ (fun t' => f t' x') t dt) x dx

declarations.name: Space.time_deriv_comm_space_deriv
declarations.statement:
lemma time_deriv_comm_space_deriv {d i} {M} [NormedAddCommGroup M] [NormedSpace ℝ M]
    {f : Time → Space d → M} (hf : ContDiff ℝ 2 ↿f) (t : Time) (x : Space d) :
    Time.deriv (fun t' => Space.deriv i (f t') x) t
    = Space.deriv i (fun x' => Time.deriv (fun t' => f t' x') t) x

declarations.name: Space.space_deriv_differentiable_time
declarations.statement:
lemma space_deriv_differentiable_time {d i} {M} [NormedAddCommGroup M] [NormedSpace ℝ M]
    {f : Time → Space d → M} (hf : ContDiff ℝ 2 ↿f) (x : Space d) :
    Differentiable ℝ (fun t => Space.deriv i (f t) x)

declarations.name: Space.time_deriv_differentiable_space
declarations.statement:
lemma time_deriv_differentiable_space {d } {M} [NormedAddCommGroup M] [NormedSpace ℝ M]
    {f : Time → Space d → M} (hf : ContDiff ℝ 2 ↿f) (t : Time) :
    Differentiable ℝ (fun x => Time.deriv (f · x) t)

declarations.name: Space.curl_differentiable_time
declarations.statement:
lemma curl_differentiable_time
    (fₜ : Time → Space → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3))
    (hf : ContDiff ℝ 2 ↿fₜ) (x : Space) :
    Differentiable ℝ (fun t => (∇ ⨯ fₜ t) x)

declarations.name: Space.time_deriv_curl_commute
declarations.doc: Curl and time derivative commute.
declarations.statement:
lemma time_deriv_curl_commute (fₜ : Time → Space → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3))
    (t : Time) (x : Space) (hf : ContDiff ℝ 2 ↿fₜ) :
    ∂ₜ (fun t => (∇ ⨯ fₜ t) x) t = (∇ ⨯ fun x => (∂ₜ (fun t => fₜ t x) t)) x

declarations.name: Space.space_fun_of_time_deriv_eq_zero
declarations.statement:
lemma space_fun_of_time_deriv_eq_zero {d} {M} [NormedAddCommGroup M] [NormedSpace ℝ M]
    {f : Time → Space d → M} (hf : Differentiable ℝ ↿f)
    (h : ∀ t x, ∂ₜ (f · x) t = 0) :
    ∃ (g : Space d → M), ∀ t x, f t x = g x

declarations.name: Space.time_fun_of_space_deriv_eq_zero
declarations.statement:
lemma time_fun_of_space_deriv_eq_zero {d} {M} [NormedAddCommGroup M] [NormedSpace ℝ M]
    {f : Time → Space d → M} (hf : Differentiable ℝ ↿f)
    (h : ∀ t x i, Space.deriv i (f t) x = 0) :
    ∃ (g : Time → M), ∀ t x, f t x = g t

declarations.name: Space.const_of_time_deriv_space_deriv_eq_zero
declarations.statement:
lemma const_of_time_deriv_space_deriv_eq_zero {d} {M} [NormedAddCommGroup M] [NormedSpace ℝ M]
    {f : Time → Space d → M} (hf : Differentiable ℝ ↿f)
    (h₁ : ∀ t x, ∂ₜ (f · x) t = 0)
    (h₂ : ∀ t x i, Space.deriv i (f t) x = 0) :
    ∃ (c : M), ∀ t x, f t x = c

declarations.name: Space.equal_up_to_const_of_deriv_eq
declarations.statement:
lemma equal_up_to_const_of_deriv_eq {d} {M} [NormedAddCommGroup M] [NormedSpace ℝ M]
    {f g : Time → Space d → M} (hf : Differentiable ℝ ↿f) (hg : Differentiable ℝ ↿g)
    (h₁ : ∀ t x, ∂ₜ (f · x) t = ∂ₜ (g · x) t)
    (h₂ : ∀ t x i, Space.deriv i (f t) x = Space.deriv i (g t) x) :
    ∃ (c : M), ∀ t x, f t x = g t x + c

declarations.name: Space.distTimeDeriv
declarations.doc: The time derivative of a distribution dependent on time and space.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def distTimeDeriv {M d} [NormedAddCommGroup M] [NormedSpace ℝ M] :
    ((Time × Space d) →d[ℝ] M) →ₗ[ℝ] (Time × Space d) →d[ℝ] M

declarations.name: Space.distTimeDeriv_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma distTimeDeriv_apply {M d} [NormedAddCommGroup M] [NormedSpace ℝ M]
    (f : (Time × Space d) →d[ℝ] M) (ε : 𝓢(Time × Space d, ℝ)) :
    (distTimeDeriv f) ε = fderivD ℝ f ε (1, 0)

declarations.name: Space.distTimeDeriv_apply'
declarations.statement:
lemma distTimeDeriv_apply' {M d} [NormedAddCommGroup M] [NormedSpace ℝ M]
    (f : (Time × Space d) →d[ℝ] M) (ε : 𝓢(Time × Space d, ℝ)) :
    (distTimeDeriv f) ε =
    -f (SchwartzMap.evalCLM ℝ (Time × Space d) ℝ (1, 0)
    ((fderivCLM ℝ (Time × Space d) ℝ) ε))

declarations.name: Space.apply_fderiv_eq_distTimeDeriv
declarations.statement:
lemma apply_fderiv_eq_distTimeDeriv {M d} [NormedAddCommGroup M] [NormedSpace ℝ M]
    (f : (Time × Space d) →d[ℝ] M) (ε : 𝓢(Time × Space d, ℝ)) :
    f (SchwartzMap.evalCLM ℝ (Time × Space d) ℝ (1, 0) ((fderivCLM ℝ (Time × Space d) ℝ) ε)) =
    - (distTimeDeriv f) ε

declarations.name: Space.distTimeDeriv_apply_CLM
declarations.statement:
lemma distTimeDeriv_apply_CLM {M M2 d} [NormedAddCommGroup M] [NormedSpace ℝ M]
    [NormedAddCommGroup M2] [NormedSpace ℝ M2] (f : (Time × Space d) →d[ℝ] M)
    (c : M →L[ℝ] M2) : distTimeDeriv (c ∘L f) = c ∘L (distTimeDeriv f)

declarations.name: Space.distSpaceDeriv
declarations.doc: The space derivative of a distribution dependent on time and space.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def distSpaceDeriv {M d} [NormedAddCommGroup M] [NormedSpace ℝ M]
    (i : Fin d) : ((Time × Space d) →d[ℝ] M) →ₗ[ℝ] (Time × Space d) →d[ℝ] M

declarations.name: Space.distSpaceDeriv_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma distSpaceDeriv_apply {M d} [NormedAddCommGroup M] [NormedSpace ℝ M]
    (i : Fin d) (f : (Time × Space d) →d[ℝ] M) (ε : 𝓢(Time × Space d, ℝ)) :
    (distSpaceDeriv i f) ε = fderivD ℝ f ε (0, basis i)

declarations.name: Space.distSpaceDeriv_apply'
declarations.statement:
lemma distSpaceDeriv_apply' {M d} [NormedAddCommGroup M] [NormedSpace ℝ M]
    (i : Fin d) (f : (Time × Space d) →d[ℝ] M) (ε : 𝓢(Time × Space d, ℝ)) :
    (distSpaceDeriv i f) ε =
    - f ((SchwartzMap.evalCLM ℝ (Time × Space d) ℝ (0, basis i))
    ((fderivCLM ℝ (Time × Space d) ℝ) ε))

declarations.name: Space.apply_fderiv_eq_distSpaceDeriv
declarations.statement:
lemma apply_fderiv_eq_distSpaceDeriv {M d} [NormedAddCommGroup M] [NormedSpace ℝ M]
    (i : Fin d) (f : (Time × Space d) →d[ℝ] M) (ε : 𝓢(Time × Space d, ℝ)) :
    f ((SchwartzMap.evalCLM ℝ (Time × Space d) ℝ (0, basis i))
    ((fderivCLM ℝ (Time × Space d) ℝ) ε)) =
    - (distSpaceDeriv i f) ε

declarations.name: Space.distSpaceDeriv_commute
declarations.statement:
lemma distSpaceDeriv_commute {M d} [NormedAddCommGroup M] [NormedSpace ℝ M]
    (i j : Fin d) (f : (Time × Space d) →d[ℝ] M) :
    distSpaceDeriv i (distSpaceDeriv j f) = distSpaceDeriv j (distSpaceDeriv i f)

declarations.name: Space.distSpaceDeriv_apply_CLM
declarations.statement:
lemma distSpaceDeriv_apply_CLM {M M2 d} [NormedAddCommGroup M] [NormedSpace ℝ M]
    [NormedAddCommGroup M2] [NormedSpace ℝ M2]
    (i : Fin d) (f : (Time × Space d) →d[ℝ] M)
    (c : M →L[ℝ] M2) : distSpaceDeriv i (c ∘L f) = c ∘L (distSpaceDeriv i f)

declarations.name: Space.distTimeDeriv_commute_distSpaceDeriv
declarations.statement:
lemma distTimeDeriv_commute_distSpaceDeriv {M d} [NormedAddCommGroup M] [NormedSpace ℝ M]
    (i : Fin d) (f : (Time × Space d) →d[ℝ] M) :
    distTimeDeriv (distSpaceDeriv i f) = distSpaceDeriv i (distTimeDeriv f)

declarations.name: Space.distSpaceGrad
declarations.doc: The spatial gradient of a distribution dependent on time and space.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def distSpaceGrad {d} :
    ((Time × Space d) →d[ℝ] ℝ) →ₗ[ℝ] (Time × Space d) →d[ℝ] (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d))

declarations.name: Space.distSpaceGrad_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma distSpaceGrad_apply {d} (f : (Time × Space d) →d[ℝ] ℝ) (ε : 𝓢(Time × Space d, ℝ)) :
    distSpaceGrad f ε = fun i => distSpaceDeriv i f ε

declarations.name: Space.distSpaceDiv
declarations.doc: The spatial divergence of a distribution dependent on time and space.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def distSpaceDiv {d} :
    ((Time × Space d) →d[ℝ] (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d))) →ₗ[ℝ] (Time × Space d) →d[ℝ] ℝ

declarations.name: Space.distSpaceDiv_apply_eq_sum_distSpaceDeriv
Space.distSpaceCurl
declarations.doc: The curl of a distribution dependent on time and space.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def distSpaceCurl : ((Time × Space 3) →d[ℝ] (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3))) →ₗ[ℝ]
    (Time × Space 3) →d[ℝ] (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3))

modules.title: Distributions which are constant in time
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

in this module given a distribution on `Space d`, we define the associated distribution
on `Time × Space d` which is constant in time.

This is defined by integrating Schwartz Maps on `Time × Space d` over the time coordinate,
to get a Schwartz Map on `Space d`.

## ii. Key results

- `Space.timeIntegralSchwartz` : the integral over time of a Schwartz map on `Time × Space d`
  to give a Schwartz map on `Space d`.
- `Space.constantTime` : the distribution on `Time × Space d` associated with a distribution
  on `Space d`, which is constant in time.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Properties of time integrals of Schwartz maps
  - A.1. Continuity as a function of space
  - A.2. Derivative a function of space
  - A.3. Differentiability as a function of space
  - A.4. Integrability of the derivative as a function of space
  - A.5. Smoothness as a function of space
- B. Properties of schwartz maps at a constant space point
  - B.1. Integrability
  - B.2. Integrability of powers times norm of iterated derivatives
    - B.2.1. Bounds on powers times norm of iterated derivatives
    - B.2.2. Integrability of powers times norm of iterated derivatives
  - B.3. Integrability of iterated derivatives
- C. Decay results for derivatives of the time integral
  - C.1. Moving the iterated derivative inside the time integral
  - C.2. Bound on the norm of iterated derivative
  - C.3. Bound on the norm of iterated derivative mul a power
- D. The time integral as a schwartz map
- E. Constant time distributions
  - E.1. Space derivatives of constant time distributions
  - E.2. Space gradient of constant time distributions
  - E.3. Space divergence of constant time distributions
  - E.4. Space curl of constant time distributions
  - E.5. Time derivative of constant time distributions

## iv. References

declarations.name: Space.continuous_time_integral
declarations.statement:
lemma continuous_time_integral {d} (η : 𝓢(Time × Space d, ℝ)) :
    Continuous (fun x : Space d => ∫ t : Time, η (t, x))

declarations.name: Space.time_integral_hasFDerivAt
declarations.statement:
lemma time_integral_hasFDerivAt {d : ℕ} (η : 𝓢(Time × Space d, ℝ)) (x₀ : Space d) :
    HasFDerivAt (fun x => ∫ (t : Time), η (t, x))
      (∫ (t : Time), fderiv ℝ (fun x : Space d => η (t, x)) x₀) x₀

declarations.name: Space.time_integral_differentiable
declarations.statement:
lemma time_integral_differentiable {d : ℕ} (η : 𝓢(Time × Space d, ℝ)) :
    Differentiable ℝ (fun x => ∫ (t : Time), η (t, x))

declarations.name: Space.integrable_fderiv_space
declarations.statement:
lemma integrable_fderiv_space {d : ℕ} (η : 𝓢(Time × Space d, ℝ)) (x : Space d) :
    Integrable (fun t => fderiv ℝ (fun x => η (t, x)) x) volume

declarations.name: Space.time_integral_contDiff
declarations.statement:
lemma time_integral_contDiff {d : ℕ} (n : ℕ) (η : 𝓢(Time × Space d, ℝ)) :
    ContDiff ℝ n (fun x => ∫ (t : Time), η (t, x))

declarations.name: Space.integrable_time_integral
declarations.statement:
lemma integrable_time_integral {d : ℕ} (η : 𝓢(Time × Space d, ℝ)) (x : Space d) :
    Integrable (fun t => η (t, x)) volume

declarations.name: Space.pow_mul_iteratedFDeriv_norm_le
declarations.statement:
lemma pow_mul_iteratedFDeriv_norm_le {n m} {d : ℕ} :
    ∃ rt, ∀ (η : 𝓢(Time × Space d, ℝ)), ∀ (x : Space d),
    Integrable (fun x : Time => ‖((1 + ‖x‖) ^ rt)⁻¹‖) volume ∧
    ∀ t, ‖(t, x)‖ ^m * ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ n ⇑η (t, x)‖ ≤
        (2 ^ (rt + m, n).1 *
        ((Finset.Iic (rt + m, n)).sup fun m => SchwartzMap.seminorm ℝ m.1 m.2) η) *
        ‖(1 + ‖t‖) ^ (rt)‖⁻¹

declarations.name: Space.iteratedFDeriv_norm_mul_pow_integrable
declarations.statement:
lemma iteratedFDeriv_norm_mul_pow_integrable {d : ℕ} (n m : ℕ) (η : 𝓢(Time × Space d, ℝ))
    (x : Space d) :
    Integrable (fun t => ‖(t, x)‖ ^ m * ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ n ⇑η (t, x)‖) volume

declarations.name: Space.iteratedFDeriv_norm_integrable
declarations.statement:
lemma iteratedFDeriv_norm_integrable {n} {d : ℕ} (η : 𝓢(Time × Space d, ℝ))
    (x : Space d) :
    Integrable (fun t => ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ n ⇑η (t, x)‖) volume

declarations.name: Space.iteratedFDeriv_integrable
declarations.statement:
lemma iteratedFDeriv_integrable {n} {d : ℕ} (η : 𝓢(Time × Space d, ℝ)) (x : Space d) :
    Integrable (fun t => iteratedFDeriv ℝ n ⇑η (t, x)) volume

declarations.name: Space.time_integral_iteratedFDeriv_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma time_integral_iteratedFDeriv_apply {d : ℕ} (n : ℕ) (η : 𝓢(Time × Space d, ℝ)) :
    ∀ x, ∀ y, iteratedFDeriv ℝ n (fun x => ∫ (t : Time), η (t, x)) x y =
      ∫ (t : Time), (iteratedFDeriv ℝ n η (t, x)) (fun i => (0, y i))

declarations.name: Space.time_integral_iteratedFDeriv_eq
declarations.statement:
lemma time_integral_iteratedFDeriv_eq {d : ℕ} (n : ℕ) (η : 𝓢(Time × Space d, ℝ))
    (x : Space d) :
    iteratedFDeriv ℝ n (fun x => ∫ (t : Time), η (t, x)) x =
      ((∫ (t : Time), iteratedFDeriv ℝ n η (t, x)).compContinuousLinearMap
      (fun _ => ContinuousLinearMap.prod (0 : Space d →L[ℝ] Time)
      (ContinuousLinearMap.id ℝ (Space d))))

declarations.name: Space.time_integral_iteratedFDeriv_norm_le
declarations.statement:
lemma time_integral_iteratedFDeriv_norm_le {d : ℕ} (n : ℕ) (η : 𝓢(Time × Space d, ℝ))
    (x : Space d) :
    ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ n (fun x => ∫ (t : Time), η (t, x)) x‖ ≤
        (∫ (t : Time), ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ n η (t, x)‖) *
        ‖(ContinuousLinearMap.prod (0 : Space d →L[ℝ] Time)
        (ContinuousLinearMap.id ℝ (Space d)))‖ ^ n

declarations.name: Space.time_integral_mul_pow_iteratedFDeriv_norm_le
declarations.statement:
lemma time_integral_mul_pow_iteratedFDeriv_norm_le {d : ℕ} (n m : ℕ) :
    ∃ rt, ∀ (η : 𝓢(Time × Space d, ℝ)),∀ (x : Space d),
    Integrable (fun x : Time => ‖((1 + ‖x‖) ^ rt)⁻¹‖) volume ∧
    ‖x‖ ^ m * ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ n (fun x => ∫ (t : Time), η (t, x)) x‖ ≤
        ((∫ (t : Time), ‖((1 + ‖t‖) ^ rt)⁻¹‖) *
        ‖((0 : Space d →L[ℝ] Time).prod (.id ℝ (Space d)))‖ ^ n)
        * (2 ^ (rt + m, n).1 * ((Finset.Iic (rt + m, n)).sup
          fun m => SchwartzMap.seminorm ℝ m.1 m.2) η)

declarations.name: Space.timeIntegralSchwartz
declarations.doc:
The continuous linear map taking Schwartz maps on `Time × Space d` to
`space d` by integrating over time.
declarations.statement:
def timeIntegralSchwartz {d : ℕ} :
    𝓢(Time × Space d, ℝ) →L[ℝ] 𝓢(Space d, ℝ)

declarations.name: Space.timeIntegralSchwartz_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma timeIntegralSchwartz_apply {d : ℕ} (η : 𝓢(Time × Space d, ℝ)) (x : Space d) :
    timeIntegralSchwartz η x = ∫ (t : Time), η (t, x)

declarations.name: Space.constantTime
declarations.doc:
Distributions on `Time × Space d` from distributions on `Space d`.
These distributions are constant in time.
declarations.statement:
def constantTime {M : Type} [NormedAddCommGroup M] [NormedSpace ℝ M] {d : ℕ} :
    ((Space d) →d[ℝ] M) →ₗ[ℝ] (Time × Space d) →d[ℝ] M

declarations.name: Space.constantTime_apply
declarations.statement:
lemma constantTime_apply {M : Type} [NormedAddCommGroup M] [NormedSpace ℝ M]
    {d : ℕ} (f : (Space d) →d[ℝ] M)
    (η : 𝓢(Time × Space d, ℝ)) :
    constantTime f η = f (timeIntegralSchwartz η)

declarations.name: Space.constantTime_distSpaceDeriv
declarations.statement:
lemma constantTime_distSpaceDeriv {M : Type} {d : ℕ} [NormedAddCommGroup M] [NormedSpace ℝ M]
    (i : Fin d) (f : (Space d) →d[ℝ] M) :
    Space.distSpaceDeriv i (constantTime f) = constantTime (Space.distDeriv i f)

modules.title: The action of the Euclidean group on `TimeAndSpace`
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

In this file we define the action of the Euclidean group on `TimeAndSpace d`. The action fixes
the time coordinate and acts on the space coordinate by the usual Euclidean-group action on
`Space d`.

## ii. Key results

- `TimeAndSpace.instMulActionEuclideanGroup` : The action of the Euclidean group on
  `TimeAndSpace d`.
- `TimeAndSpace.dist_smul` : The Euclidean group action on `TimeAndSpace d` preserves distance.
- `TimeAndSpace.smul_hasTemperateGrowth` : The Euclidean group action has temperate growth.
- `TimeAndSpace.antilipschitz_smul` : The Euclidean group action is antilipschitz.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The Euclidean group action
- B. Temperate growth of the coordinate action

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. The Euclidean group action
## B. Temperate growth of the coordinate action

declarations.name: TimeAndSpace.instMulActionEuclideanGroup
declarations.doc: The Euclidean group acts on `TimeAndSpace d` by fixing time and acting on space.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable instance instMulActionEuclideanGroup :
    MulAction (EuclideanGroup d) (TimeAndSpace d)

declarations.name: TimeAndSpace.smul_mk
declarations.doc: Coordinate formula for the Euclidean-group action on `TimeAndSpace d`.
declarations.statement:
lemma smul_mk (g : EuclideanGroup d) (t : Time) (x : Space d) :
    g • ((t, x) : TimeAndSpace d) = (t, g • x)

declarations.name: TimeAndSpace.fst_smul
declarations.doc: The Euclidean-group action fixes the first coordinate.
declarations.statement:
lemma fst_smul (g : EuclideanGroup d) (tx : TimeAndSpace d) :
    (g • tx).1 = tx.1

declarations.name: TimeAndSpace.snd_smul
declarations.doc: The Euclidean-group action applies to the second coordinate.
declarations.statement:
lemma snd_smul (g : EuclideanGroup d) (tx : TimeAndSpace d) :
    (g • tx).2 = g • tx.2

declarations.name: TimeAndSpace.time_smul
declarations.doc: The Euclidean-group action fixes the time projection.
declarations.statement:
lemma time_smul (g : EuclideanGroup d) (tx : TimeAndSpace d) :
    time (g • tx) = time tx

declarations.name: TimeAndSpace.space_smul
declarations.doc: The Euclidean-group action applies to the space projection.
declarations.statement:
lemma space_smul (g : EuclideanGroup d) (tx : TimeAndSpace d) :
    space (g • tx) = g • space tx

declarations.name: TimeAndSpace.dist_smul
declarations.doc: The Euclidean-group action on `TimeAndSpace d` preserves product distance.
declarations.statement:
lemma dist_smul (g : EuclideanGroup d) (tx ty : TimeAndSpace d) :
    dist (g • tx) (g • ty) = dist tx ty

declarations.name: TimeAndSpace.actionLinearMap
declarations.doc: The linear part of the Euclidean-group action on `TimeAndSpace d`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def actionLinearMap (g : EuclideanGroup d) :
    TimeAndSpace d →L[ℝ] TimeAndSpace d

declarations.name: TimeAndSpace.actionTranslation
declarations.doc: The translation part of the Euclidean-group action on `TimeAndSpace d`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def actionTranslation (g : EuclideanGroup d) : TimeAndSpace d

declarations.name: TimeAndSpace.smul_eq_actionLinearMap_add
declarations.statement:
lemma smul_eq_actionLinearMap_add (g : EuclideanGroup d) (tx : TimeAndSpace d) :
    g • tx = actionLinearMap g tx + actionTranslation g

declarations.name: TimeAndSpace.smul_hasTemperateGrowth
declarations.doc: The Euclidean-group action on `TimeAndSpace d` has temperate growth.
declarations.statement:
lemma smul_hasTemperateGrowth (g : EuclideanGroup d) :
    Function.HasTemperateGrowth (fun tx : TimeAndSpace d => g • tx)

declarations.name: TimeAndSpace.isometry_smul
declarations.doc: The Euclidean-group action on `TimeAndSpace d` is an isometry.
declarations.statement:
lemma isometry_smul (g : EuclideanGroup d) :
    Isometry (fun tx : TimeAndSpace d => g • tx)

declarations.name: TimeAndSpace.antilipschitz_smul
declarations.doc: The Euclidean-group action on `TimeAndSpace d` is antilipschitz.
declarations.statement:
lemma antilipschitz_smul (g : EuclideanGroup d) :
    AntilipschitzWith 1 (fun tx : TimeAndSpace d => g • tx)

modules.title: The Euclidean group action on Schwartz maps over `TimeAndSpace`
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

In this file we define the pullback action of the Euclidean group on Schwartz maps over
`TimeAndSpace d`. The action is
`g • η = fun tx => η (g⁻¹ • tx)`.

## ii. Key results

- `TimeAndSpace.schwartzEuclideanAction` : The Euclidean group action on Schwartz maps as a
  continuous representation (`ContRepresentation`).
- `TimeAndSpace.instMulActionSchwartzMap` : The induced `MulAction` instance on Schwartz maps.
- `TimeAndSpace.smul_schwartzMap_apply` : Pointwise formula for the action.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The pullback action on Schwartz maps

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. The pullback action on Schwartz maps

declarations.name: TimeAndSpace.schwartzEuclideanAction
declarations.doc:
The Euclidean-group pullback action on Schwartz maps over `TimeAndSpace d`, as a continuous
representation `ContRepresentation ℝ (EuclideanGroup d) 𝓢(TimeAndSpace d, F)`.

`ContRepresentation R G V` unfolds to the monoid homomorphism `G →* V →L[R] V` into the
*continuous*-linear maps: the builder `SchwartzMap.compCLMOfAntilipschitz` already yields a
continuous-linear map for free, and the `→L` codomain lets the action compose under `∘L`. The
plain mathlib `Representation` (`G →* V →ₗ[ℝ] V`) is recovered via
`ContRepresentation.toRepresentation`.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def schwartzEuclideanAction {d : ℕ} :
    ContRepresentation ℝ (EuclideanGroup d) 𝓢(TimeAndSpace d, F)

declarations.name: TimeAndSpace.schwartzEuclideanAction_apply
declarations.doc: Pointwise formula for the monoid-homomorphism form of the Schwartz-map pullback action.
declarations.statement:
lemma schwartzEuclideanAction_apply {d : ℕ} (g : EuclideanGroup d) (η : 𝓢(TimeAndSpace d, F))
    (tx : TimeAndSpace d) :
    (schwartzEuclideanAction g η) tx = η (g⁻¹ • tx)

declarations.name: TimeAndSpace.instMulActionSchwartzMap
declarations.doc: The Euclidean group acts on Schwartz maps over `TimeAndSpace d` by pullback.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable instance instMulActionSchwartzMap {d : ℕ} :
    MulAction (EuclideanGroup d) 𝓢(TimeAndSpace d, F)

declarations.name: TimeAndSpace.smul_schwartzMap_apply
declarations.doc: Pointwise formula for the `MulAction` instance on Schwartz maps.
declarations.statement:
lemma smul_schwartzMap_apply {d : ℕ} (g : EuclideanGroup d) (η : 𝓢(TimeAndSpace d, F))
    (tx : TimeAndSpace d) :
    (g • η) tx = η (g⁻¹ • tx)

declarations.name: TimeAndSpace.schwartzEuclideanAction_mul_apply
declarations.doc: Applying `g` and then `h` to a Schwartz map is the pullback action of `h * g`.
declarations.statement:
lemma schwartzEuclideanAction_mul_apply {d : ℕ} (g h : EuclideanGroup d)
    (η : 𝓢(TimeAndSpace d, F)) :
    schwartzEuclideanAction h (schwartzEuclideanAction g η) =
      schwartzEuclideanAction (h * g) η

declarations.name: TimeAndSpace.schwartzEuclideanAction_injective
declarations.doc: Each Euclidean-group pullback action on Schwartz maps is injective.
declarations.statement:
lemma schwartzEuclideanAction_injective {d : ℕ} (g : EuclideanGroup d) :
    Function.Injective (schwartzEuclideanAction (F := F) g)

declarations.name: TimeAndSpace.schwartzEuclideanAction_surjective
declarations.doc: Each Euclidean-group pullback action on Schwartz maps is surjective.
declarations.statement:
lemma schwartzEuclideanAction_surjective {d : ℕ} (g : EuclideanGroup d) :
    Function.Surjective (schwartzEuclideanAction (F := F) g)

modules.title: Wave Vector Space
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

In this module we define the type `WaveVectorSpace d` corresponding to the `d`-dimensional
space of (angular) wave vectors in `Space d`.

In contrast to `Space d`, `WaveVectorSpace d` has a distinguished zero;
the purpose of this file is to define this zero, the structure of a `Module`
on `WaveVectorSpace d`, and the structure of a real `InnerProductSpace` on `WaveVectorSpace d`,
none of which requires any non-canonical choices.

`WaveVectorSpace d` is implemented as a structure with a field `val : Fin d → ℝ`
rather than as an `abbrev` of `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)` or a `def` of a type with value
`EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)` for the same reasons as for `Space d`;
see `Physlib.SpaceAndTime.Space.Basic` for a discussion of the (dis)advantages of each.

## ii. Key results

- `WaveVectorSpace d` : the space of wave vectors in `Space d`
- `instModuleReal` : `WaveVectorSpace d` is a module over `ℝ`
- `instInnerProductSpaceReal` : `WaveVectorSpace d` is a real inner product space
- `equivEuclideanSpace` : the linear isometric equivalence between `WaveVectorSpace d` and `ℝᵈ`

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The `WaveVectorSpace` type
- B. Instances on `WaveVectorSpace`
  - B.1. Coercion to functions
  - B.2. Subsingleton for `d = 0`
  - B.3. Zero
  - B.4. Additive commutative group
  - B.5. Module over `ℝ`
  - B.6. Inner product space
- C. Linear isometric equivalence with `ℝᵈ`
  - C.1. Standard basis
  - C.2. Coordinate functions

## iv. References

The type `WaveVectorSpace d` is the real vector space which corresponds to `d`-dimensional
(angular) wave vectors in `Space d` with a given (but arbitrary) choice of inverse length unit.

The default value of `d` is `3`. Thus `WaveVectorSpace = WaveVectorSpace 3`

modules.title: Duality of `Space` and `WaveVectorSpace`
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

Upon selecting an origin for the affine space `Space d`,
the spaces `Space d` and `WaveVectorSpace d` are dual as real vector spaces.
There is natural continuous bilinear map `WaveVectorSpace d × Space d → ℝ` which sends
the pair `(k, x)` to `∑ᵢ kⁱxᵢ`. For fixed `k` this gives rise to a functional `Space d →L[ℝ] ℝ`
mapping `x ↦ k ⬝ᵥ x`, and similarly for fixed `x`.

## ii. Key results

- `Space.dual x` : the functional on `WaveVectorSpace` corresponding to `x : Space d`,
  bundled as a continuous linear map.
- `WaveVectorSpace.dual k` : the functional on `Space` corresponding to `k : WaveVectorSpace d`,
  bundled as a continuous linear map.
- `WaveVectorSpace.pairingCLM` : the dual pairing between `WaveVectorSpace` and `Space`,
  bundled as a continuous bilinear map.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Strong duals
- B. Bilinear pairing

## iv. References

## B. Bilinear pairing
